proved_step: LEMMA-A-REPAIR. Setting: N=2^n, F subset {0,1}^N. A streaming search system has state q_0, transitions q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,x_{t+1}), so q_t(p) depends only on the prefix p of length t, and a decoder D on the final state q_N(w) which, for every w in {0,1}^N, outputs a circuit computing w if w in F and rejects otherwise. Call a length-t prefix p LIVE if some u has pu in F, DEAD otherwise. Claim: for each t, q_t(p) != q_t(p') whenever p is live and p' != p (length t), so the live prefixes have pairwise distinct states and no state is shared with any other prefix. Consequently 2^S >= L_t + [L_t < 2^t]. Proof: let p be live with completion u (pu in F) and suppose q_t(p')=q_t(p) with p' != p. Then q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u), so D returns the same answer on both strings. Since pu in F, D must output a circuit computing pu; so D accepts p'u with that circuit, which must compute p'u if p'u in F, and it cannot compute both pu and p'u because they differ in the first t bits. Hence p'u not in F and D must reject p'u, but it accepts pu, which is an identical decision on identical states: contradiction. A dead prefix thus gets a state no live prefix has, and if a dead prefix exists at t one extra code is needed, giving the bound. Scope: the search model above only; it says nothing about decoder size D, gate cost G, or encodings (G0001-G0004 remain open).

lemma: Structural lemma for G=1 (exact, by inspection). If a streaming step is one B2 gate g = op(x_i, x_j) over the inputs x_0..x_{S-1} (state bits) and b (input bit) plus constants, then each output bit is either a copy of one input or constant, except at most one output bit, which may equal g. So the new state differs from a permutation-with-constants of the old state and b in at most one bit. Consequence to test: the set of transitions available at G=1 is a small explicit family (choice of the gate, at most one replaced output bit, copy/constant choices), so the G=1 question reduces to a finite search over codes plus this transition family, without a general SAT encoding of arbitrary circuits.

proved_step: Lemma (repair of the G=1 structural claim). Let F: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S be computed by a circuit with exactly one non-free gate g over basis {AND,OR,XOR,const}, NOT free. Then there is I subset [S], |I| <= 1, such that for j not in I, F_j is a literal (x_i, NOT x_i, b, NOT b) or a constant; if I={i}, F_i = op(l1,l2) for a 2-input op and literals l1,l2 of (x,b) or constants. Proof: each output coordinate is wired to an input/constant or is the unique gate output, so at most one coordinate is non-literal. Consequence: the G=1 transition set is the G=0 literal-wiring set with one coordinate replaced by an arbitrary two-literal gate; this matches the existing SAT option set and gives no algorithmic saving. Does not bound G_max, decoder D, or general algorithms.

proved_step: LEMMA (dead-separated count bound). Let n=3, N=8. Fix a level t and let P_t be the set of distinct live residual functions at level t. Suppose a one-pass system with S state bits assigns codes E_t: {0,1}^t -> {0,1}^S such that (i) live prefixes with equal residual get equal code and live prefixes with different residuals get different codes; (ii) every dead prefix has a code different from all live codes; (iii) at least one dead prefix exists at level t. Then 2^S >= |P_t| + 1, hence S >= ceil(log2(|P_t|+1)). PROOF: by (i), the live residual classes receive |P_t| pairwise distinct codes in {0,1}^S. By (ii) and (iii), a dead prefix has a code outside that set, so the image of E_t has at least |P_t|+1 elements, and 2^S >= |P_t|+1. QED. APPLICATION (conditional on (iii) at the maximising level, NOT yet verified): SC_{3,1} gives S>=ceil(log2 39)=6; affine control gives S>=5; SC_{3,2} gives S>=8.

proved_step: CORRECTION of the S>=6 claim for SC_{3,1}. The quantity that must be separated is the number R_t of DISTINCT RESIDUALS of live prefixes at level t (residual = set of suffixes completing the prefix to a function in F), not the number of full truth tables. LEMMA: let E_t be dead-separated codes (live prefixes with different residuals get different codes, dead prefixes get codes outside the live set), and D_t = number of dead prefixes at level t. Then 2^S >= R_t + [D_t > 0] for every t. PROOF: if two live prefixes p, q have E_t(p)=E_t(q) but different residuals, some suffix b makes the final output differ for one of them, so the code cannot be correct for both; hence R_t distinct live codes are needed. If D_t > 0, a dead prefix needs one further code outside the live set. QED. APPLICATION: cm-6468ef6ec5214251 (SC_{3,1}, n=3, N=8, F = one-gate circuits, |F|=38) gives level 4: R=13, D=0, so S>=4; level 5: R=14, D=10, so 15 codes and S>=4; maximum over levels S>=4. lemma: Model M0 (literal wiring, G=0): initial state constant; at each step every state bit is a sign-literal of one coordinate among the input bits b_1..b_t, or a constant. proved_step: Induction on t. t=0: state constant, J_0 empty. Step: suppose every state bit at time t is a sign-literal of a coordinate in J_t or a constant. A bit at time t+1 is a literal of an old state bit (hence a sign-literal of a coordinate of J_t or a constant) or a literal of b_{t+1} or a constant. So each bit at time t+1 is a sign-literal of a coordinate in J_t union {t+1} or a constant. Let J_{t+1} be the set of coordinates appearing in these literals; |J_{t+1}| <= S since there are S bits, and J_{t+1} subset of J_t union {t+1}. Every bit is a fixed function of p restricted to J_{t+1}, so equal projections give equal states. Conversely each coordinate of J_{t+1} is exposed by some bit with fixed sign, so equal states give equal coordinates on J_{t+1}. Hence state(p)=state(q) iff p|J=q|J. Separation at time t requires state(p) different from state(q) for live p and dead q, hence p|J_t differs from q|J_t, so |J_t| >= sep_t and S >= sep_t. This is exact for M0 only.

Gap: the proof treats each output wire as a literal/constant or 'the unique gate output', which ignores fan-out. One non-free gate g can drive several output coordinates; every such coordinate equals +/-g, so it is non-literal. Counterexample: S=2, F_1=F_2=x1 AND x2 (one gate, two non-literal coordinates), so |I|<=1 fails. REPAIR (to check): there is a two-literal gate g=op(l1,l2), with l1,l2 literals of (x,b) or constants, such that every coordinate j is a literal, a constant, or +/-g; I = {j : F_j = +/-g} is arbitrary, not bounded by 1. evidence: Hand check of the induction. Base t=0: J_0 empty, state constant, fine. Step: if every bit at time t is a sign-literal of a coordinate in J_t or a constant, then under M0 (each new bit is a literal of an old bit, of b_{t+1}, or a constant) every new bit is a sign-literal of a coordinate in J_t union {t+1} or a constant. J_{t+1} is the set of coordinates appearing, so |J_{t+1}| <= S (each bit contributes at most one coordinate). State is a fixed function of p restricted to J_{t+1}, so state(p)=state(q) iff p|J=q|J: the converse holds because each coordinate of J_{t+1} appears as a literal of some bit, so equal bits give equal coordinates. Separation requires p|J_t != q|J_t for every live p and dead q, so J_t is a separating coordinate set and S >= |J_t| >= sep_t. SCOPE LIMIT: this is valid only for M0 (literal-only transducers). It does not cover general B2 transitions with fan-out (the owner contract's model), which can create bits depending on several coordinates at once. Restricted-model lemma only; no claim for the full model.

evidence: Hand check of the counting argument. Given (i) same residual gives same code, different residual gives different code, and (ii) dead codes outside the live set, the live classes use |P_t| distinct codes, and a dead prefix needs one more code, so 2^S >= |P_t|+1. Correct as stated. Strengthening note: hypotheses (i) and (ii) are not extra assumptions for a correct streaming decoder. If live p and q had equal codes with different residuals, a suffix b in R_p minus R_q would give pb in F with the same final state as qb, so the decoder would have to accept and reject the same state (contradiction). If a dead prefix d had the code of a live p, then d and p reach the same final state; the decoder outputs a witness for pu with u completing p, but d u is not in F and must be rejected, again a contradiction. So (i) and (ii) follow from decoder correctness. The application (S>=6 for SC_{3,1}) is withdrawn by S0028 and is not verified here. Condition (iii) is still needed for the +1.

lemma: G=0 projection lemma. Let an S-bit streaming transducer have q_{t+1} = F_t(q_t, x_{t+1}) where every coordinate of F_t is a constant or a literal of (q_t, x_{t+1}) (zero gates; time-dependent wiring allowed). Then for every prefix p of length t, each coordinate of q_t(p) is a constant or +-p_k for some k <= t. Hence q_t(p) is a function of the bits p_k, k in I_t, where I_t is the set of positions read by the at most S coordinates, so |I_t| <= S. Proof by induction on t: q_0 is constant. A literal of (q_t, x_{t+1}) is either a literal of a coordinate of q_t (a constant or +-p_k) or +-x_{t+1} = +-p_{t+1}. Consequence: if two prefixes agree on I_t they get the same state, so they must have the same liveness, which is a checkable necessary condition for a G=0 separator. Scope: G=0 only; it says nothing about G>=1, decoder size, or G_max.

(2) General argument, for the model G1 = tuples over B = literals of (q,b) plus constants, where a tuple may use one shared gate g and its complement: nonbase gates of two distinct literals on distinct variables are exactly 10 two-variable functions (5 complement pairs), so the number of pairs is 5*C(m,2) with m=S+1; |B|=2m+2=2S+4. Let A_p = (B u p)^S for each pair p. Then A_p cap A_q = B^S for p != q, since the coordinates of p and q are disjoint outside B; and A_p \ B^S are pairwise disjoint, because a tuple in A_p \ B^S with a coordinate in p\B cannot lie in A_q. So |union| = |B|^S + sum_p (|A_p| - |B|^S) with |A_p| = (2S+6)^S, which is the S0074 formula. Scope: holds for all S >= 1 in the stated model; it is bookkeeping and closes none of G0001/G0002. proved_step: LEMMA-A-SEARCH (repair of S0009, search semantics). Setting: N=2^n strings w in {0,1}^N, F subset {0,1}^N, streaming states q_t(p) on prefixes p of length t, final state q_N(w), decoder D with D(q_N(w)) = a circuit computing w if w in F, and reject if w not in F. Claim: for every t, if p is live (some pu in F) and p' != p has length t, then q_t(p') != q_t(p). Moreover, if a dead prefix p' exists at t then q_t(p') differs from all live codes. Proof: suppose q_t(p)=q_t(p') with pu in F. Then for every suffix v, q_N(pv)=q_N(p'v). Take v=u: the decoder accepts pu, so it returns a circuit C with C computing pu and C computing p'u only if p'u in F; but the same state gives the same decoder output, so D(q_N(p'u)) = C accepts, forcing p'u in F. Then the single state class contains two distinct F-strings pu and p'u, and D must output one circuit computing both pu and p'u, which differ in the first t bits: impossible. The same argument with a dead p' gives p'u not in F while D accepts, contradiction. Hence live codes are injective and disjoint from dead codes, so S_t >= ceil(log2(L_t + [dead prefix exists])). Scope: the search model above, time-dependent encodings, unbounded update and decoder cost. This is NOT the decision-only separation claim: the refutation of S0009 (R1146) used a counterexample with F={000,001,010,011} that gives two F-strings one code, which the search model forbids. It proves no G_max value and closes no G0001-G0004. Checked by finite enumeration: physalis_code_run for N=4, t=2 (criterion of the class condition; see cm for result).

proved_step: LEMMA-G1-REPAIR (repair of S0014, fan-out corrected). Setting: S >= 1, F: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S computed by a circuit over basis {AND, OR, XOR, constants} with NOT free, containing exactly one non-free gate g. Claim: there is a two-literal gate g* = op(l1, l2), where op is one of AND, OR, XOR and l1, l2 are literals of the inputs (x_1..x_S, b) or constants, such that every output coordinate F_j is a literal, a constant, or +/- g*, for all j. Proof: every wire feeding an output is an input, a constant, the negation of one of these, or the output of g (the only non-free gate). The inputs of g are themselves wires with no non-free gate upstream, so each is a literal or a constant; hence g = op(l1, l2) with literals or constants l1, l2. Each output coordinate is therefore a literal, a constant, or +/- g. Fan-out is allowed: any number of coordinates may equal +/- g, so the index set I = {j : F_j in {g, NOT g}} is arbitrary, with no bound |I| <= 1. Consequence: the G=1 transition set is the G=0 literal-wiring set with the coordinates in an arbitrary subset I replaced by a shared two-literal gate (with polarity). Scope: one non-free gate, free NOT, one-step transition function only. Says nothing about G_max, decoder cost D, or multi-step circuits. Mechanical check still open: enumerate S=2 single-gate circuits and compare with the stated form.

Reviewed by session R1282 (not the claiming session R1274). Hand proof: suppose p live (pu in F) and p' != p with q_t(p) = q_t(p'). Transitions depend only on state and input bit, so q_N(pu) = q_N(p'u). The decoder returns one value C on that final state, and C computes pu since pu in F. p'u differs from pu in the first t bits, so C cannot compute both. If p'u in F, the decoder must output a circuit computing p'u: contradiction. If p'u not in F, the decoder must reject, but it outputs C: contradiction. So the claim holds, also for dead p'. Consistent with the S0009 refutation: the counterexample F={000,001,010,011} needs two F-strings sharing one code, which this argument forbids. Pigeonhole gives 2^S >= L_t + [dead prefix exists]. Scope: search model only; no G_max value.

The inputs of g are therefore literals or constants, so g = op(l1, l2). Every output wire is a literal, a constant, or +/-g, and fan-out is unrestricted, so the index set I is arbitrary. proved_step: REPAIR of S0009 (conflict-graph form). Setting as in S0009: streaming system with q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,b), decoder D on q_N, correct on every w in {0,1}^N (outputs a circuit computing w if w in F, rejects otherwise). Let H_t be the graph on LIVE prefixes of length t with p~p' iff some u has pu in F and p'u in F. Claim: (a) if p != p' are live and q_t(p)=q_t(p') then no u has pu, p'u both in F; (b) if p is dead and p' live with q_t(p)=q_t(p') then no u has p'u in F. Hence live codes properly colour H_t and avoid all dead codes, so 2^S >= omega(H_t) + [a dead prefix exists]; and for each fixed u, {p : pu in F} is a clique of H_t, so 2^S >= max_u |{p : pu in F}| + [dead prefix exists]. Proof of (a): q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u), so D gives the same circuit C on both; if both are in F, C must compute pu and p'u, which differ in a coordinate among the first t positions: contradiction. Proof of (b): take u with p'u in F; D outputs C computing p'u on q_N(p'u)=q_N(pu); since pu not in F, D must reject pu, contradiction. Scope: per-time code counting with the decoder; says nothing about G_max or gate cost.

Hand re-derivation of S0086 by a different session (R1290). (a) If q_t(p)=q_t(p') and p!=p' then for every suffix u, q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u) (the transitions depend only on state and bit). D therefore returns one circuit C on both. If pu and p'u are both in F, C must compute both tables, but they differ on a prefix coordinate (t positions): impossible. (b) p dead, p' live, equal states, p'u in F for some u: D outputs a circuit C on q_N(p'u)=q_N(pu); pu is not in F, so D must reject it, but D's output depends only on the state: contradiction. Consequences: live codes properly colour H_t; dead codes avoid live codes; hence 2^S >= omega(H_t)+[dead] and 2^S >= max_u|{p: pu in F}|+[dead]. lemma: LEMMA R (residual-class bound, exact). Let F subset {0,1}^n, 1 <= t < n, and for p in {0,1}^t let g_p(u) = [pu in F] for u in {0,1}^(n-t). Let D_t(F) be the number of distinct residual functions g_p. Any deterministic streaming decider that reads the prefix p into a state s(p) and then reads the suffix with one fixed transition function, accepting iff the final state is in an accept set, needs at least D_t(F) states. Proof: if s(p)=s(q) and g_p(u) != g_q(u) for some u, then pu and qu end in the same state, so they receive the same output, but [pu in F] != [qu in F]. Hence s(p)=s(q) implies g_p=g_q. Reconciliation of S0009: for F={000,001,010,011}, t=2, the residual classes are {00,01} (g=1 on both suffixes) and {10,11} (g=0), so D=2 and two codes suffice. The dispute's 'impossible' step fails: 000 and 010 have identical residual functions, so one circuit (constant 1 on the suffix) is correct for both. The per-suffix condition in S0009 (accepted prefixes need distinct codes) is stronger than necessary and is replaced by the residual-class condition: prefixes with different residuals need different codes, equal residuals may share. Scope: state counting only; it gives no bound on update cost G_max.

lemma: LEMMA S (Live-Dead Separation Lower Bound). Let F ⊆ {0,1}^n be a set of Boolean functions computed by a streaming decider with at most one non-free gate per step (G=0 or G=1 model as considered in the session). For 1 ≤ t < n, let g_p(u) = [p·u ∈ F] for p ∈ {0,1}^t, and let D_t(F) = |{g_p : p ∈ {0,1}^t}| be the number of distinct residual functions. Any such decider needs at least D_t(F) states at step t. Moreover, if the decider must keep live and dead prefixes of F apart (i.e., no live prefix shares a state with a dead prefix), then the number of states is at least the number of distinct residuals among live prefixes plus those among dead prefixes that are not shared with live prefixes. Proof: If s_t(p) = s_t(q) and g_p ≠ g_q, then there exists a suffix u such that g_p(u) ≠ g_q(u); then p·u and q·u end in the same state but receive different outputs, contradicting correctness. Hence s_t(p) = s_t(q) ⇒ g_p = g_q. For the live-dead condition, if a live prefix p and dead prefix q share a state, then by definition of live/dead there exists a suffix u with p·u ∈ F and q·u ∉ F (or vice versa); the decider would output the same decision for both, which is incorrect. Therefore, states assigned to live prefixes and those assigned to dead prefixes must be disjoint unless the residuals are identical and the suffix handling is consistent for both. The count follows by partitioning the set of all prefixes {0,1}^t by their residual function g_p, and then separating live from dead residuals. This lemma provides the correct state-counting condition for live-dead separation, replacing the invalid per-suffix injectivity condition that blocked progress in earlier sessions.

proved_step: CLAIMED. Per-suffix injectivity lemma (repair of S0009; reconciles the dispute). Setup: F subset of {0,1}^N, N=2^n. A streaming machine has state set {0,1}^S, a deterministic update c(t+1, p+x*2^t) = U(c(t,p), x), and a decoder D with D(final state of w) = w for every w in F. Claim: for every suffix u of length N-t and every prefix p, p' of length t with pu in F and p'u in F, if p != p' then c(t,p) != c(t,p'). Proof: if c(t,p) = c(t,p'), the update is deterministic, so reading u from both gives the same final state. Then D gives pu = p'u, hence p = p', a contradiction. Consequence (counting): for every t and every suffix u, the set {p in {0,1}^t : pu in F} has at most 2^S elements, so S >= log2 max_{t,u} |F_u^t| where F_u^t = {p : pu in F}. Scope: a bound on the state count for a machine that reads the bits in order and decodes the table exactly. It bounds neither the update-circuit size G nor G_max, and it is not the pairwise claim of S0009.

evidence: Review by a session other than the claimant. Checked the argument: the update c(t+1, p+x*2^t) = U(c(t,p), x) is deterministic and depends only on the current state and the read bit. If c(t,p) = c(t,p'), then reading the same suffix u from both gives the same final state, so D returns the same word for pu and p'u. If pu and p'u are both in F, the decoder property D(final state of w) = w forces pu = p'u, hence p = p' (same length t). So for each t and suffix u, the map p -> c(t,p) is injective on F_u^t = {p : pu in F}, giving |F_u^t| <= 2^S and S >= log2 max_{t,u} |F_u^t|. No gap found in the stated scope. The scope is limited as stated: it bounds neither G nor D, and it is a counting bound (the same as a one-way communication argument), so it does not by itself give a new lower bound on G_max. Consistency check: this is weaker than the live-prefix bound it replaces in S0009, and it is correct where S0009 was not.

proved_step: Lemma A: for any copy-only update g:{0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S (each output bit a constant, a literal x_i xor c, or b xor c), g's image is an affine subspace of GF(2)^S of size 2^r, r = number of distinct source variables selected by some output bit. Proof: g(z)=Az+c with A having at most one 1 per row, so nonzero columns have disjoint supports and rank A = r; image = c + Im A.

evidence: Review by a session other than the claimant (R1322). Setting: F: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S computed by a circuit whose only non-free gate is g = op(l1,l2), op in {AND,OR,XOR}, with l1,l2 literals of (q,b) or constants; NOT is free. Since every other gate is NOT, g's inputs are literals or constants of the inputs, so g itself is a two-literal function. The argument has no gap in this scope. Reviewed in session R1330. Conclusion holds, and the stated reason is valid. Each output row of a copy-only map is either a constant, a unit vector e_j (literal x_j or b, plus constant), so each row has at most one 1 and nonzero columns of A have disjoint supports (each row belongs to exactly one column). Disjoint nonzero columns are linearly independent, so rank A = r = number of distinct source variables selected. The image of (z,b) -> Az+c is c+Im A, of size 2^r. Scope: copy-only maps (constant, literal, or b xor c per output). Fan-out is allowed and does not affect the argument.

proved_step: LEMMA-G1-REPAIR (repairs S0014). Setting: F:{0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S computed by a circuit with exactly one non-free gate g (basis AND, OR, XOR, const; NOT free). Claim: there exist a binary op g, with inputs l1,l2 in {x_i, NOT x_i, b, NOT b, 0, 1}, such that each output F_j is a literal, a constant, or g or NOT g. Proof: free nodes are functions of inputs and constants only. Since g is the only non-free node, its inputs are free nodes, and each output wire is a free node or g (possibly negated). Scope: one non-free gate only. Consequence: the G=1 transition set is literal wiring plus one shared two-literal gate attached to an arbitrary subset I of coordinates with arbitrary polarities. |I| is unbounded (F_1=F_2=AND(x1,x2) has |I|=2), so the S0014 claim |I|<=1 is refuted and this repair replaces it. Does not bound G_max or the decoder.

refuted_approach: S0079_ANALYSIS
evidence: Reviewed S0079: The step presents 'LEMMA-A-SEARCH (repair of S0009, search semantics). Setting: N=2^n strings w in {0,1}^N, F subset {0,1}^N, streaming states q_t(p) on prefixes p of length t, final state q_N(w), decoder D with D(q_N(w)) = a circuit computing w if w in F, and reject if w not in F. Claim: for every t, if p is live (some pu in F) and p' != p has length t, then q_t(p') != q_t(p). Moreover, if a dead prefix p' exists at t then q_t(p') differs from all live codes. Proof: suppose q_t(p)=q_t(p') with pu in F. Then for every suffix v, q_N(pv)=q_N(p'v). Take v=u: the decoder accepts pu, so it returns a circuit C with C computing pu and C computing p'u only if p'u in F; but the same state gives the same decoder output, so D(q_N(p'u)) = C accepts, forcing p'u in F. Then the single state class contains two distinct F-strings pu and p'u, and D must output one circuit computing both pu and p'u, which differ in the first t bits: impossible. The same argument with a dead p' gives p'u not in F while D accepts, contradiction. Hence live codes are injective and disjoint from dead codes, so S_t >= ceil(log2(L_t + [dead prefix exists])). Scope: the search model above, time-dependent encodings, unbounded update and decoder cost. This is NOT the decision-only separation claim: the refutation of S0009 (R1146) used a counterexample with F={000,001,010,011} that gives two F-strings one code, which the search model forbids. It proves no G_max value and closes no G0001-G0004. Checked by finite enumeration: physalis_code_run for N=4, t=2 (criterion of the class condition; see cm for result).' The proof is well-structured and addresses the search semantics carefully. The argument that live codes must be injective and disjoint from dead codes is logically sound given the stated search model assumptions. The scope clarification (search model, time-dependent encodings, unbounded update and decoder cost) is important. The step correctly identifies that this is NOT the decision-only separation claim and that it proves no G_max value directly. However, the proof operates within a specific search model with strong assumptions (time-dependent encodings, unbounded update cost). While the logic is valid within this model, the connection to actual gate-count G_max measurement remains indirect - the model assumes unbounded update cost rather than bounding it. Verdict: SURVIVED_REVIEW - the search semantics argument is logically valid within its stated scope, but it does not establish concrete G_max bounds for the streaming problem.

proved_step: LEMMA-S29-REPAIR (repair of S0029, search model). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N, a streaming transducer with states from a set of size 2^S, deterministic time-dependent transitions q_{t+1}(pb) = delta_t(q_t(p), b), and a decoder D depending only on q_N(w), where D(q_N(w)) computes w for w in F and rejects for w not in F. For a prefix length t let Live_t = {p in {0,1}^t : p u in F for some u} and Dead_t = {0,1}^t minus Live_t. Claim: (i) p -> q_t(p) is injective on Live_t; (ii) q_t(Live_t) and q_t(Dead_t) are disjoint. Hence 2^S >= |Live_t| + [Dead_t nonempty]. Proof of (i): let p != p' be live with q_t(p)=q_t(p'). Pick u with pu in F. Then q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u), so D returns the same circuit C on both; C computes pu, and D must accept p'u, which forces p'u in F and C computes p'u too. Two different truth tables cannot both equal C, so pu = p'u, contradicting p != p'. Proof of (ii): let p live and p' dead with equal states. Pick u with pu in F. Then D(q_N(p'u)) = D(q_N(pu)) accepts, but p'u is not in F, so D must reject: contradiction. Scope: exactly this search model (decoder sees only the final state, unbounded update and decoder cost). It bounds the number of states, not the per-step gate count G, so it closes no gap G0001-G0004 and bounds nothing beyond the pigeonhole count. Corrects S0029: the separation holds on prefixes (stronger than residuals), so the bound |Live_t| + [Dead_t nonempty] <= 2^S is the correct form. Checkable by finite enumeration on small N (N=4, t=2).

lemma: L-G0 (repair of my divisibility bound S >= N - nu2(|F|), which gives only S >= 7 for SC_{3,1}). Setting: N = 2^n, w in {0,1}^N read as w_1..w_N; G=0 transducer = state q_t in {0,1}^S, q_0 constant, each bit of q_{t+1} is a constant, or a literal (+/- sign) of one bit of q_t, or a literal of w_{t+1}. Decision separator: A subset of {0,1}^S with F = {w : q_N(w) in A}. Claim: for n >= 3 and F = SC_{n,1} (one-gate B2 circuits, truth tables of length N), every G=0 decision separator of F has S >= N. Proof. (1) Structure: by induction on t every bit of q_t is a constant or +/- w_j for some j <= t (base: q_0 constant; step: a bit of q_{t+1} is a literal of an old bit, a literal of w_{t+1}, or a constant, and negations compose). Hence q_N(w) = phi(w restricted to J) for a set J of positions with |J| <= S. (2) Saturation: F is a union of fibres of the projection pi_J, so w in F implies w XOR e_k in F for every k not in J. (3) Facts about F = SC_{n,1}, n >= 3: 0^N is in F (zero gates); and no weight-1 word is in F, because a circuit with at most one gate computes a function g of at most two variables, whose on-set in {0,1}^n has size 2^(n-2)*|on(g)| (or 0, 2^(n-1), 2^n for constants and literals), which is even for n >= 3, while e_k has weight 1. (4) If J != [N], pick k not in J: 0 in F forces e_k in F by (2), contradicting (3). So J = [N] and S >= |J| = N. QED. Corollaries: SC_{3,1} (N=8, |F|=38) and SC_{4,1} (N=16, |F|=70): G=0 decision separation needs S = N, so the G=0 point is the trivial regime of the owner's addendum (work moves into the decoder). Scope: decision separation (weaker than search, so the search bound is a fortiori), G=0 only (wires, constants, negations), time-dependent F_t allowed, decoder cost unbounded, s = 1, n >= 3. Fails for s = 2 (for n = 3 the minterm x1 AND x2 AND x3 has two gates and is in SC_{3,2}, so the hypothesis e_k not in F breaks). Surprise followed up: the brute-force run cm-227f3138ff0d4cc4 found the minimal saturating |J| equal to N for n = 3 and 4 (not N - nu2 = 7 or 15), and for n = 2 (F = all of {0,1}^4) J = empty, consistent with the hypothesis failing at n = 2. Open: G >= 1 at S < N (SAT runs gave no verdict); the decision separator with one shared gate per step is not covered by this lemma.

lemma: Let SC = SC_{n,s} (N = 2^n), and let a prefix p of length t be LIVE if some suffix w of length N-t gives pw in SC, otherwise DEAD. Let R(p) = {w : pw in SC} be the residual. Claim: any deterministic layered streaming system that decides SC, with state set Q_t after t input bits, satisfies |Q_t| >= L_t + 1 whenever some dead prefix of length t exists, where L_t = number of distinct nonempty residuals R(p) over live prefixes p of length t. Proof: (i) if states s(p)=s(q) at time t, then p and q have the same future behaviour, so R(p)=R(q); hence distinct nonempty residuals need distinct states, giving |Q_t| >= L_t. (ii) every dead prefix has residual the empty set, which is distinct from every nonempty residual, so its state differs from all live states, giving one more state. Hence |Q_t| >= L_t + 1. Consequence: the per-step lower bound of states for keeping live and dead prefixes apart is max_t (L_t + 1) over t with a dead prefix, which is a lower bound for the state count of this streaming model, not for its update cost G_max. Observed on cm-d7c03dfb23514e5a: for SC_2 the all-prefix Nerode count minus L_t is exactly 1 at every t (t=6: 8 vs 7), matching the lemma.

The open point is whether the update cost of a system with |Q_t| = L_t + 1 states can be bounded below. The perfect-matching control and naturalness check are not applied because no circuit or LOWER_BOUND is claimed.

proved_step: REPAIR of G0117 (conflict-clique bound, search model). Setting: N=2^n, F subset {0,1}^N, transducer q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,b) with time-dependent F_t, decoder D on q_N that outputs a circuit computing w when w in F and rejects otherwise, correct on every w in {0,1}^N. Let H_t be the graph on live length-t prefixes with p~p' iff some u has pu, p'u both in F. Claim: any state map on live prefixes is a proper colouring of H_t, and every live code differs from every dead code when a dead prefix exists. Hence 2^S >= omega(H_t) + [a dead prefix of length t exists]. Proof: (i) if p != p' are live with q_t(p)=q_t(p') and pu, p'u in F, then q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u) by the transition rule, so D returns one circuit C that must compute both pu and p'u; these differ at a position < t, impossible. (ii) if p is dead and p' live with the same code, pick u with p'u in F; q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u), so D returns a circuit that must reject pu, but it accepts, a contradiction. A clique of H_t needs pairwise distinct codes, and all dead prefixes can share one extra code. Instance: n=3, s=1, N=8, |F|=38 (asserted in code). At t=7: omega=19, dead=1, so S >= ceil(log2 20) = 5. Scope: search model only, time-dependent encodings, unbounded update cost. Says nothing about G_max or the decision-only model. The earlier S>=6 (G0116) is withdrawn: its contradiction step was unjustified.

lemma: G=0 LEMMA (search model, n arbitrary, N=2^n). Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and let a streaming system have S state bits, states q_t(p) for prefixes p in {0,1}^t, with q_0 constant. Suppose every update F_t is literal wiring: each new state coordinate is a constant, or a literal (a state bit or the input bit b, possibly negated). Suppose that at t=N the search condition holds: q_N is injective on F, and q_N(F) is disjoint from q_N({0,1}^N \ F). Then S >= N.
evidence: Pure argument, no computation. Uses only t=N and the search condition as stated in PNP-001-LEMMA-M-EXPERIMENT-2026-11-21.md (Objects section: live codes injective, dead codes disjoint from live codes). Scope: literal-wiring updates only; with one gate the flip argument fails (a gate can read many bits), so G>=1 is not implied. Consistent with the owner's triviality remark: G=0 forces S >= N, i.e. raw storage. Not a G_max value, not a decoder-cost statement, not an asymptotic statement. Not reviewed: author is claude-haiku, same family as the open claimed steps.
proved_step: PROOF. By induction on t, every coordinate of q_t(p) is a constant or a literal of a single bit of p: q_0 is constant, and each step copies a literal of a state coordinate or of the input bit. So there is a set J of at most S positions with q_N(p) determined by p restricted to J. Suppose S < N. Then some position k is outside J. Pick w in F (F nonempty) and let w' = w with bit k flipped. Then q_N(w') = q_N(w). If w' is in F, two distinct live words share a state, contradicting injectivity on F. If w' is not in F, a dead word shares a state with a live word, contradicting disjointness. Both cases are impossible, so S >= N. QED. Corollary: for every S < N and every nonempty F, a wiring-only (G=0) system does not satisfy the search condition. In particular the G=0 test for SC_{3,1} at S=6 is UNSAT by this argument, with no SAT run needed.

proved_step: LEMMA D (decision semantics, one pass, any time-dependent transitions). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N, machine with state set Q, |Q|=2^S, start state q_0, transitions q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,b), accept iff q_N in an accepting set. For a prefix p of length t let R(p)={v in {0,1}^(N-t) : pv in F}. Let K_t = number of distinct nonempty residual sets R(p) over live prefixes p (R(p) nonempty), and D_t = number of dead prefixes (R(p) empty). Claim: 2^S >= K_t + [D_t > 0]. Proof: the state after reading p is q_t(p), and the rest of the run is a deterministic function of (q_t(p), v). So q_t(p)=q_t(p') implies R(p)=R(p'). Contrapositive: R(p) != R(p') implies q_t(p) != q_t(p'). Hence the map R-class -> state is well defined and injective on the set of distinct residual languages, which has K_t + [D_t>0] elements (the empty language counted once if dead prefixes exist). So |Q| >= K_t + [D_t>0]. Scope: acceptance/decision version only; no decoder, no update cost, no search semantics. Consequence: S_t >= ceil(log2(K_t + [D_t>0])) for every t. Checked by cm-a06ba2fb0f3b42c0 (SC_{3,1}: K_4=13, D_4=0, gives S>=4; matches decision bound 4). This does not close G0001-G0004 or any G_max obligation; it is the standard Myhill-Nerode count for a time-indexed automaton. Claimed for review.

proved_step: CLAIMED (unreviewed) copy-class coordinate lemma. Model: S-bit streaming system over {0,1}; time-dependent transitions where each next-state bit is one of: constant 0/1, a literal (q_t^j or its negation) of one current state bit, or b or not-b. Claim: for every t there is ref_t^i in {0..t-1} or none per bit such that q_t^i is a constant or +-p_{ref}. Proof: induction on t. t=0: all bits constant. Step: a copied literal of q_t^j inherits j's single reference, and b = p_t adds reference t, so each bit references at most one position of {0..t}. Hence q_t is a function of p restricted to R_t with |R_t| <= S. If codes are injective on live prefixes P_t, then p -> p|R_t is injective on P_t, so S >= kappa(P_t), where kappa(A) = min{|R| : A|R injective}. Scope: copy/negate/constant/input class only; a necessary condition. It does not give G_max and does not prove S >= N for literal wiring (lab note gives kappa_8 = 6 for SC_{3,1}, which is < 8).

proved_step: LEMMA-LIVE-SEPARATION-COUNT (search model, unbounded update and decoder cost). N=2^n, F subset {0,1}^N, states q_t in {0,1}^S, q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,b), decoder D with D(q_N(w)) = circuit computing w if w in F, reject otherwise. L_t = {p in {0,1}^t : exists u with pu in F}, D_t = {p : pu not in F for all u}. Then q_t is injective on L_t and its image avoids q_t(D_t), so 2^S >= |L_t| + [D_t nonempty]. Proof: if q_t(p)=q_t(p') with pu in F, the states agree on all suffixes, so D returns the same circuit C on pu and p'u; if p'u in F, C would compute two distinct strings (they differ in the first t bits), impossible; if p'u not in F, D must reject but outputs C. The dead-live case is symmetric. Scope: S bound only; says nothing about G_max, update cost, or gaps G0001-G0004. proved_step: LEMMA-CLIQUE (explicit form of S0086(a,b), no closure claimed). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N, deterministic streaming system with states q_t(p) on prefixes p of length t (time-dependent update), final state q_N(w), decoder D with D(q_N(w)) = a circuit computing w if w in F, and D rejects if w not in F. Let H_t have vertex set the live length-t prefixes (p with some pv in F), with p~p' iff some v has pv and p'v both in F. Claim: (a) if p != p' are live and q_t(p)=q_t(p'), then no v has pv and p'v both in F. Proof: q_t equal implies q_N(pv)=q_N(p'v) for every v (the update is a function of the state and the input bits, so the same state gives the same future). If both pv, p'v are in F, D returns one circuit computing both strings; they differ (they agree on the first t bits only if the rest differs, but p != p' gives distinct strings), contradiction. (b) if p is dead (no pv in F) and p' is live with q_t(p)=q_t(p'), then for any v with p'v in F we get q_N(pv)=q_N(p'v), so D accepts pv with a circuit, but pv is not in F: contradiction. Consequence: the codes of the vertices of any clique of H_t are pairwise distinct and disjoint from the code of any dead prefix, so the number of states is at least omega(H_t) + [a dead length-t prefix exists]. Scope: space (state count) only; update cost, decoder cost and oracle gates are unbounded and not addressed; it does not bound G, G_max, or the MMW Thm 4.1 setting. Explicit verification of the clique values for n=3, s=1 is cm-262789be5a0741fb (EXPLORATORY). Status: CLAIMED, written by this session, so it is open until a different model family reviews it. It repeats S0086 and adds no new content on the gap.

proved_step: LEMMA-COUNT (restates the conclusion of S0079 for the counting bound; search semantics). Setting: streaming states q_t(p) in {0,1}^S on prefixes p of length t, decoder D on q_N, correct on every w in {0,1}^N. Claim: for every t, 2^S >= L_t + [D_t > 0], where L_t = number of distinct live prefixes of length t (prefixes of F-strings) and D_t = number of dead prefixes. Proof: by S0079, the map p -> q_t(p) is injective on live prefixes, and no live code equals a dead code. So the L_t live prefixes take L_t distinct codes. If D_t > 0, at least one further code in {0,1}^S is used by dead prefixes and differs from all live codes. Hence L_t + [D_t > 0] <= 2^S, so S >= ceil(log2(L_t + [D_t > 0])). Scope: n=3, s=1, the 38-function family, search semantics, time-dependent encodings, unbounded update and decoder cost. Not a G_max value. Closes no obligation in G0001-G0004. Its only new content is the explicit count at t=7 and t=8, which the physalis_code_run above checks.

proved_step: LEMMA (exact-decision state bound): if a deterministic streaming system with state set Q decides F on all 2^N inputs in truth-table order, then |Q| is at least the number of distinct Myhill-Nerode residuals of F at level t over all length-t prefixes, for every t. Proof: two prefixes p, p' of length t that reach the same state have identical futures, so they must have equal residuals; hence the state map is constant on residual classes and |Q| >= R_t.

proved_step: L-G0-ZERO: Let N >= S+2. Consider a time-indexed streaming transducer with S slots where, at step t, each slot is updated by one option shared by all nodes at time t: copy of slot k (k<S), the streamed bit b_t, or constant 0 or 1. Then no such transducer with any liveness predicate lv on the S-bit state recognises the prefixes of the constant-0 function on {0,1}^N. Proof: by induction on t, every slot's value at node (t,v) is a constant or x_s for a single position s fixed by the options (not by v). So the state at (t,v) depends only on v restricted to I_t, with |I_t| <= S. Take t = S+1 <= N-1 and p in {0..t-1} \ I_t. Then 0^t (live) and 0^t with a 1 at p (dead, since it is not a prefix of the zero function) have equal states, so lv cannot separate them.

proved_step: LEMMA (state lower bound from prefix classes, exact). Let f: {0,1}^N -> {0,1} and let p ~_t q (p,q in {0,1}^t) iff f(pz) = f(qz) for every z in {0,1}^(N-t). Let C_t be the number of ~_t classes. Then every deterministic streaming automaton that reads x_1..x_N in order and outputs f(x) after the last bit has at least C_t distinct states after reading t bits. PROOF: if p ~_t' q are in different classes, some suffix z has f(pz) != f(qz). If p and q reached the same state after t bits, the remaining computation on pz and qz would be identical, so the outputs would agree, a contradiction. Hence distinct classes occupy distinct states. Scope: states only; no update-time bound follows.

proved_step: LEMMA W0 (zero-gate streaming needs N state bits). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N nonempty. State q_0 is constant in {0,1}^S, q_t = F_t(q_{t-1}, x_t), where F_t is a zero-gate circuit: each output bit is a constant, or a literal (possibly negated) of an old state bit or of x_t. Decoder D is a function of q_N only and must output a circuit computing w if w in F, and reject if w not in F, for every w in {0,1}^N. Claim: S >= N. PROOF. (1) By induction on t, each coordinate i of q_t(w) is a constant or +/- w_s for one index s = s_i(t) <= t, and s depends only on the wiring, not on w (base: q_0 constant; step: an output is a constant, +/- x_t, or +/- an old coordinate, which by hypothesis is a constant or +/- w_s). (2) Let J = {s_i(N)} over the non-constant coordinates. Then |J| <= S and q_N(w) depends on w only through w restricted to J. (3) Suppose |J| < N. Pick k not in J and some w in F. Let w' be w with bit k flipped. Then q_N(w') = q_N(w). If w' in F, D outputs one circuit that must compute both w and w', but w != w' have different truth tables: impossible. If w' not in F, D must reject w' while outputting a circuit for w on the same code: contradiction. Hence |J| = N, so S >= |J| = N. QED.

proved_step: LEMMA SENS (sensitivity of final codes, any gate count). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N. Streaming system: q_0 fixed, q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,x_{t+1}) with arbitrary (time-dependent, arbitrary-cost) F_t; Q(w)=q_N(w); decoder D depends only on Q(w) and must output a circuit whose truth table is w when w in F, and reject when w not in F, for every w in {0,1}^N. Claim: for every w in F and every k in [N], Q(w^k) != Q(w), where w^k flips bit k. PROOF. Suppose Q(w^k)=Q(w)=c. Then D(c) is one output. If w^k in F, D(c) must compute both w and w^k, which are distinct truth tables: impossible. If w^k not in F, D(c) must be a circuit for w (since w in F), but D must reject w^k: contradiction. QED. COROLLARY (zero-gate case, reproving W0): if F_t are zero-gate, Q depends only on a set J of at most S positions; if |J|<N pick k outside J and w in F, so Q(w^k)=Q(w), contradicting SENS; hence S >= N.

Step S0002 is a meta-classification of Lemma A (formalized in S0079). Lemma A states: for every time t, live prefixes must have pairwise distinct states, and no dead prefix may share a state with a live prefix. Hence 2^S >= L_t + [dead prefix exists]. The proof (S0079) uses the decoder property: if q_t(p)=q_t(p'), then for all suffixes v, q_N(pv)=q_N(p'v), so the decoder outputs the same circuit; if one prefix is live and one dead, or both live but correspond to different strings, this yields a contradiction. This is exactly a pigeonhole/counting bound on the number of states. S0079 explicitly states: 'It proves no G_max value and closes no G0001-G0004.' Therefore S0002's characterization is correct: Lemma A is a counting bound and does not close the G_max gaps. No counterexample exists to this classification.

Lemma A (as detailed in S0079 and S0086) states: for a streaming system with S state bits, live prefixes at time t injectively encoded, dead codes disjoint from live codes, the conflict graph H_t on live prefixes (p~p' iff exists u with pu,p'u in F) must be properly coloured by the live codes, so 2^S >= chi(H_t) + [dead prefix exists] >= omega(H_t) + [dead prefix exists]. This is a pure counting/pigeonhole argument on the number of distinct state values needed for the encoding to exist at all, independent of the computational cost (G_max) of the transition functions F_t. It does not close any of the gaps G0001-G0004 which concern the minimum gate complexity of the transitions. The step is a correct bookkeeping observation.

S0079 provides a correct proof of the injectivity and dead/live separation for the SEARCH model (where the decoder must output a specific witness circuit). The argument: if q_t(p)=q_t(p') with p live (pu in F) and p' another prefix of length t, then for suffix u, q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u). The decoder outputs the same circuit C on both. Since pu in F, C must compute pu. If p'u in F, C would need to compute both pu and p'u which differ in the first t bits - impossible. If p' is dead (no extension in F), then for any u with pu in F, p'u not in F, but the decoder would accept p'u (output C computing p'u) - contradiction. This correctly proves live codes are injective and disjoint from dead codes in the search model. The step explicitly notes this is NOT the decision-only separation claim (which S0009 had conflated). The proof is sound for the stated model. No counterexample exists for the search model as defined.

S0080 correctly characterizes G=1 transition functions (exactly one non-free gate over {AND, OR, XOR} with NOT free). Since there's only one non-free gate g, its inputs must be literals or constants (no upstream non-free gates). Thus g = op(l1, l2) where op ∈ {AND, OR, XOR} and l1, l2 are literals/constants. Each output coordinate is either a literal, constant, or ±g (with arbitrary fan-out allowed). The set I = {j: F_j ∈ {g, ¬g}} can be any subset of [S]. This is a complete and correct structural characterization of single-gate transition functions. The step notes the mechanical check (enumerating S=2 single-gate circuits) is still open, but the mathematical proof stands. No counterexample exists to this characterization.

S0086 provides a correct repair of the conflict-graph form for the DECISION model (not the search model). It defines H_t as the graph on live prefixes where p~p' iff ∃u: pu∈F and p'u∈F. The proofs of (a) and (b) are correct: (a) If q_t(p)=q_t(p') and both pu,p'u∈F, then decoder outputs same circuit C on both, forcing C to compute both pu and p'u which differ in first t bits - impossible. (b) If p dead, p' live with q_t(p)=q_t(p'), take u with p'u∈F; decoder outputs C on both, but D must reject pu∉F while accepting p'u∈F - contradiction. Thus live codes properly color H_t and avoid dead codes, giving 2^S ≥ ω(H_t) + [dead prefix exists]. Also each {p: pu∈F} is a clique, so 2^S ≥ max_u |{p: pu∈F}| + [dead prefix exists]. This is a correct combinatorial lower bound on state bits for the decision model. It does not address G_max (gate complexity). The proof is sound.

S0106 proves per-suffix injectivity: for fixed suffix u, if pu and p'u are both in F and p != p', then c(t,p) != c(t,p'). Proof: if c(t,p)=c(t,p'), deterministic update gives same final state on suffix u, so D outputs both pu and p'u, implying p=p' contradiction. This is a correct combinatorial argument for the exact-decoding streaming model. Consequence: for each t,u, |{p: pu in F}| <= 2^S, so S >= log2 max_{t,u} |F_u^t|. The step correctly notes this bounds state count only, not gate complexity G or G_max. No counterexample exists for this model.

S0110 correctly characterizes copy-only (G=0) update functions. Each output is a constant, x_i xor c, or b xor c, so the function is g(z,b) = A*z + b*v + c where A has at most one 1 per row (each output copies at most one state bit) and v is the column for input bit b. The rank r equals the number of distinct state variables that appear as sources (nonzero columns of A have disjoint supports). The image is c + Im(A) + b*v, an affine subspace of size 2^r. This is a correct linear-algebraic fact over GF(2). No counterexample.

S0115 is a correct structural characterization of G=1 transition functions (one non-free gate over {AND, OR, XOR, const} with NOT free). Since g is the only non-free gate, its inputs must be free nodes (literals or constants from {x_i, NOT x_i, b, NOT b, 0, 1}). Thus g = op(l1, l2) with op in {AND, OR, XOR}. Every output wire is a free node or g (possibly negated). The set I = {j: F_j = +/-g} can be any subset of [S] (unbounded fan-out). The counterexample F_1=F_2=AND(x1,x2) with |I|=2 correctly refutes the old S0014 claim that |I|<=1. This is a complete and correct repair. No counterexample to the characterization exists.

(ii) Disjointness: if q_t(p)=q_t(p') for p!=p', then for any u, at most one of pu,p'u in F, else same final state would give same circuit for two distinct F-strings. (iii) Correctly notes the pairwise claim (all live prefixes distinct codes) does NOT follow: F={000,111}, t=2, prefixes 00 and 11 have disjoint suffix sets and may share a code. This gives the counting bound 2^S >= |F| only. The proof is sound for the streaming model. No counterexample.

Induction holds: at t=0 all state bits are constants. At step t+1, each new state bit is constant, +/- w_{t+1}, or +/- (old state bit). By induction each old state bit is constant or +/- w_j (j<=t). So each new state bit is constant or +/- w_j (j<=t+1). With S state bits, at most S distinct input positions influence final state. If N>S, some position j is untracked; flipping w_j leaves c(w) unchanged, violating injectivity (if both in F) or separation (if one in F, one in Dead). Shift register with S=N achieves tightness. No counterexample found; argument is sound for G=0 model.

This is a standard application of the Myhill-Nerode theorem adapted for time-indexed automata. The state at time t must distinguish between different residual languages R(p) to ensure correct final acceptance. If R(p) != R(p'), they must reach different states; otherwise, for any suffix v, the machine would either accept both pv and p'v or reject both, contradicting the definition of residual languages. The addition of [D_t > 0] correctly accounts for the single state needed to represent the empty language (dead prefixes). The logic is mathematically sound for the decision-only model.

The induction is correct: if every state bit is either a constant, a literal of a previous state bit, or the current input bit, then every state bit q_t^i is essentially a function of a single input bit p_j (j <= t) or a constant. This means the state vector q_t is a projection of the input prefix onto a set of at most S indices. For the encoding to be injective on a set P_t, the projection on these S indices must also be injective. The claim S >= kappa(P_t) follows directly from the definition of kappa as the minimum size of an injective coordinate projection. The scope is correctly limited to the 'copy/negate/constant/input' class.

The step is a basic pigeonhole principle for deterministic streaming algorithms. If L prefixes are pairwise distinguished (for each pair there exists a suffix that leads to different acceptance), then the mapping from prefixes to states must be injective: if two prefixes mapped to the same state, all suffixes would yield identical outputs, contradicting pairwise distinguishability. Hence |Σ| ≥ L and ceil(log2 L) state bits are necessary. This holds regardless of update time or transition complexity. No counterexample exists; the argument is sound for the stated model.

The sensitivity lemma is correct. For any w in F and k in [N], suppose Q(w^k) = Q(w) = c. Then D(c) is a single output. Case 1: w^k in F. Then D(c) must be a circuit computing both w and w^k, impossible since they differ at bit k. Case 2: w^k not in F. Then D(c) must output a circuit for w (since w in F) but must reject w^k; identical state gives identical decoder output, contradiction. The zero-gate corollary follows: with zero non-free gates, each state bit is a literal/constant, so final state Q depends on at most S input positions. If S < N, some k is outside this set, giving Q(w^k)=Q(w) for all w, contradicting SENS. Hence S ≥ N. No counterexample or gap found.

proved_step: LEMMA (repair of G=1 structural claim, corrected for fan-out). Let F: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S be computed by a circuit with exactly one non-free gate g = op(l1, l2), where op in {AND, OR, XOR}, l1, l2 are literals of the (S+1) inputs (q_1..q_S, b) or constants {0,1}, and NOT is free (absorbed into literals). Then there exists a two-literal gate g = op(l1, l2) such that every output coordinate F_j is either a literal, a constant, or g or NOT g. Equivalently, F lies in the set G1_S: the base set G0_S of all literal/constant wirings (size 2S+2 choices per coordinate, total (2S+2)^S functions), extended by allowing any subset of coordinates to be replaced by +g or -g for one shared gate g whose inputs are free literals/constants. Proof: each output wire is a constant, an input literal, NOT of these, or the output of the unique non-free gate g; g's inputs are free (literals/constants), so g is a two-literal function; g may fan out to any number of output coordinates, each optionally negated. Hence every F_j is in {literals, constants, +g, -g}. For S=2 (inputs q1,q2,b): exhaustive enumeration over all 2^3 inputs confirms |G0|=64, |G1|=604, G0 subset G1, 15 distinct non-base gates up to polarity, 60 tuples with >=2 non-literal coordinates (cm-1f3bd458baaa407c independent verification). proved_step: LEMMA (G=0 pointer lemma). Fix a streaming system with q_0 a constant tuple and q_{t+1} = F_t(q_t, p_{t+1}), where every output coordinate of every F_t is a literal of (q_1..q_S, b) or a constant (gate-free, G=0). Suppose the codes q_t(p) are pairwise distinct over the live prefixes P_t (prefixes of members of F). Let d_t be the least size of a coordinate set I subset [t] such that p -> p|I is injective on P_t. Then S >= d_t, and hence S >= log2 |P_t|. Proof: by induction on t, each coordinate of q_t, as a function of p in {0,1}^t, is a constant or +/- p_i for a single i <= t. Base: q_0 is constant. Step: a coordinate of q_{t+1} is a constant, the literal p_{t+1} or its negation, or a literal of some q_{t,k}, which by hypothesis is a constant or +/- p_i. So the claim holds at t+1. Let I_t be the set of indices i used by some coordinate; |I_t| <= S, and q_t(p) is a function of p|I_t. If p, p' in P_t agree on I_t then q_t(p) = q_t(p'), so p = p' by injectivity. Hence p -> p|I_t is injective on P_t, giving d_t <= |I_t| <= S. Scope: exact for gate-free systems at any n and S, with injective live codes; it says nothing about gates (G >= 1), decoder size or dead codes.

Its conclusion S >= log2|P_t| holds trivially for any injective code into {0,1}^S. Still open: gate counts G >= 1, dead-code separation, decoder size D, and general S beyond this instance. The construction needed is a gate-free bound that uses the live/dead structure, not injectivity alone.

evidence: The induction is sound for the stated gate-free basis: q_0 coordinates are constants; each next coordinate is a constant or a literal of a prior coordinate or the new input bit, so by induction it is a constant or ±p_i for one i. Let I_t be the indices used by the S output coordinates. q_t factors through p|I_t. If two live prefixes agree on I_t, the hypothesized injectivity of live codes forces them equal. Thus restriction to I_t is injective on P_t and d_t≤|I_t|≤S. The consequence S≥log2|P_t| follows from 2^S≥|P_t|. Scope is appropriately restricted to gate-free transitions with pairwise distinct live codes; it does not prove the stronger full-search live/dead bound.

proved_step: statement: For the full truth-table family F={0,1}^{2^n}, every streaming search system whose state at time t separates distinct live prefixes must have S_t≥t bits; moreover the bound is attained with zero update gates by storing the input prefix verbatim. Proof: every length-t string p has a completion to a member of F, so there are exactly 2^t live prefixes. Pairwise distinct live codes require at least 2^t state values, hence S_t≥log2(2^t)=t. For attainment, initialize q_0 empty and at each step wire the incoming bit into a fresh state coordinate, retaining all earlier coordinates unchanged; all transitions are wires, so G=0, and q_t=p. The decoder reconstructs the truth table from q_{2^n}. This is exact for the full-family search model and shows that a zero-gate optimum can arise solely from state width equal to the prefix length; it gives no nontrivial bound when S_t<t.

statement: Residual-set state lower bound. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N recognized by a deterministic streaming system with state q_t(p) after prefix p of length t, deterministic transitions, and a final decoder that accepts exactly members of F. For each length-t prefix p define R_p={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. Then the number of distinct states at time t is at least the number of distinct sets R_p. Proof: if R_p and R_p' differ, choose u in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pu and p'u is in F. If q_t(p)=q_t(p'), determinism implies that processing the common suffix u produces the same final state, so the decoder gives the same acceptance answer on both strings, contradiction. Therefore prefixes with distinct residual sets have distinct states; selecting one prefix for each distinct residual set gives the bound. This only forces pairwise separation when residual sets differ, and permits merging prefixes with identical residual sets.

statement: Residual-set quotient lemma. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For every t<N and bit b, R_{t+1}(pb)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R_t(p)}. Consequently, identifying prefixes with equal residual sets gives a deterministic quotient transition on the reachable classes: [p]_t --b--> [pb]_{t+1}; this is well-defined because equal R_t(p),R_t(p') imply equal restrictions by first bit b, hence equal R_{t+1}(pb),R_{t+1}(p'b). Proof: for each suffix v, v belongs to the left set iff pbv is in F, iff bv is in R_t(p); the well-definedness follows by applying this equivalence to both prefixes. The quotient exactly recognizes F with final acceptance determined by whether the residual set at t=N contains the empty string. It has exactly the number of distinct residual sets at each level, a lower bound on states for any deterministic decision transducer. This is a decision-language construction; it does not satisfy the stronger SEARCH requirement that all distinct live prefixes have distinct states, and gives no gate-cost or decoder-size bound.

statement: Live/dead state-count bound. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, let P_t be the set of live length-t prefixes, and let L_t=|P_t|. In a streaming system with S state bits that assigns pairwise distinct states to live prefixes and gives every dead prefix a state outside the set of live-prefix states, if at least one dead prefix exists then 2^S >= L_t+1, hence S >= ceil(log2(L_t+1)); if no dead prefix exists then 2^S >= L_t. Proof: the L_t live prefixes require L_t distinct elements of the state set. A dead prefix, when one exists, requires a further element outside those L_t states. The state set has cardinality exactly 2^S, proving the inequalities. Conversely, as a pure assignment of codes, L_t codes suffice when there are no dead prefixes and L_t+1 codes suffice when there are dead prefixes, by assigning distinct codes to the live prefixes and one remaining code to all dead prefixes. This is only a state-count statement; it asserts no realizability or bound for transition-circuit gate cost.

statement: LEMMA-A-REPAIR (corrected). Setting: N=2^n, F subset {0,1}^N. A streaming search system has initial state q_0, transitions q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t, x_{t+1}) where q_t(p) depends only on the length-t prefix p, and a decoder D on the final state q_N(w) which, for every w in {0,1}^N, outputs a circuit computing w if w in F and rejects otherwise. Call a length-t prefix p LIVE if there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} with pu in F, DEAD otherwise. For a live prefix p define its residual set R_t(p) = {u in {0,1}^{N-t} : pu in F}. For a dead prefix, R_t(p) = empty set.

Claim: In any such system that correctly decides membership in F, the states at time t must satisfy:
(1) Live/dead separation: if p is live and p' is dead then q_t(p) != q_t(p').
(2) Residual distinction: if p, p' are live and R_t(p) != R_t(p') then q_t(p) != q_t(p').
(3) Merging permitted: if R_t(p) = R_t(p') then q_t(p) may equal q_t(p').

Consequently, the number of distinct states reachable at time t is at least D_t + [exists dead prefix], where D_t is the number of distinct non-empty residual sets among length-t prefixes.

Proof: (1) Suppose p live, p' dead, but q_t(p) = q_t(p'). Since p is live, there exists u with pu in F. Since p' is dead, p'u not in F. Processing the common suffix u from the same state q_t(p)=q_t(p') yields the same final state by determinism, so the decoder gives the same answer on pu and p'u, contradicting that pu in F and p'u not in F.
(2) Suppose p, p' live with R_t(p) != R_t(p'). Then there exists u in the symmetric difference. Exactly one of pu, p'u is in F. If q_t(p)=q_t(p'), determinism gives the same final state on suffix u, so the decoder gives the same answer, contradiction.
(3) If R_t(p)=R_t(p'), then for every suffix u, pu in F iff p'u in F. Merging q_t(p)=q_t(p') preserves correctness because all future suffixes lead to identical acceptance outcomes. The lower bound on state count follows by picking one representative for each distinct non-empty residual set (giving D_t states) and, if any dead prefix exists, one additional state for all dead prefixes (since they all have R_t=empty and can share a state by (3)).

evidence: Mathematical verification: For F={0,1}^N with N=2^n, every length-t prefix p has a completion (since all strings are in F), so there are exactly 2^t live prefixes. Pairwise distinct states for live prefixes require ≥2^t state values, hence S_t ≥ log2(2^t) = t bits. Attainment: q_0 = empty (0 bits); transition at step t takes (t-1)-bit state and new input bit, outputs t-bit state via wires (first t-1 bits copied from old state, t-th bit = new input). All transitions are wire maps (G=0), q_t = p. Verified for n=1,2 by explicit enumeration (all 2^t prefixes live, wire construction achieves S_t=t). No argument gap found.

Standard Myhill-Nerode argument for streaming automata. If R_p ≠ R_p', ∃ u in symmetric difference: exactly one of pu, p'u ∈ F. If q_t(p) = q_t(p'), determinism ⇒ same final state after reading u ⇒ decoder gives same answer for both, contradiction. Therefore distinct residual sets ⇒ distinct states. The bound is tight for decision problems (merging prefixes with identical residual sets yields the minimal DFA). Verified by constructing minimal automata for small F (e.g., F = {00,11} ⊆ {0,1}^2: at t=1, R_0={0}, R_1={1}, two distinct residual sets, minimal DFA has 2 states at t=1). No argument gap.

Verified the Myhill-Nerode construction for streaming automata. The definition R_t(p) = {u: pu in F} and the recurrence R_{t+1}(pb) = {v: bv in R_t(p)} are correct (v in R_{t+1}(pb) <=> pbv in F <=> bv in R_t(p)). The quotient transition [p]_t --b--> [pb]_{t+1} is well-defined because equal residual sets imply equal restrictions by first bit. The quotient automaton exactly recognizes F with acceptance at t=N determined by whether empty string is in R_N(w). The number of distinct residual sets at each level is a lower bound on states for any deterministic decision transducer (standard Myhill-Nerode). The stated limitation (does not satisfy SEARCH requirement, no gate-cost bound) is accurate. No counterexample or argument gap found.

lemma: For any deterministic one-pass membership transducer on a finite family F of N-bit strings, states at cut t induce a partition of the length-t prefixes that refines equality of acceptance residuals: if two prefixes reach the same state, their residual subsets of {0,1}^{N-t} are equal. Proof: fix prefixes p,q reaching the same state. For every suffix u, determinism gives the same final state after processing u from that shared state, so the decoder returns the same membership bit on pu and qu. Thus pu∈F iff qu∈F for every u, exactly R_t(p)=R_t(q). Conversely, assigning one state per distinct residual (including the empty residual if present) is sufficient for membership provided transitions map each residual R on next bit b to R_b={v: bv∈R}, with unreachable/empty states handled by the empty residual. This is a finite-state characterization and says nothing about circuit gate cost.
gap: The residual partition characterizes membership state requirements but does not determine the minimum per-step update circuit cost G_max, nor the joint Pareto frontier at fixed S<N and decoder cost D for SC_{3,1}, SC_{3,2}, or affine families.

statement: Residual-partition characterization for deterministic membership streaming: at every cut t, equal machine states imply equal residual subsets R_t(p)={u:pu∈F}; conversely the residual subsets themselves form a sufficient deterministic state representation, with transition on bit b given by R↦{v:bv∈R}.
proof: Let p and q be length-t prefixes whose machine states agree. For an arbitrary suffix u of length N−t, applying the same deterministic transitions to the same suffix from equal states yields equal final states. The decoder therefore gives the same membership answer for pu and qu. As this holds for every u, their residual subsets are equal. Conversely, define the state associated with prefix p to be R_t(p). On reading b, the next residual is exactly {v : bv∈R_t(p)}, which equals R_{t+1}(pb) by definition. At t=N, the residual is {ε} exactly for members and empty exactly for nonmembers, so the decoder accepts precisely members. This proves sufficiency and the claimed transition rule.

statement_start: Residual-state circuit upper bound. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, with N finite, and let D_t be the number of distinct residual sets R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} as p ranges over length-t prefixes. If each residual set is encoded injectively by S_t bits, then the induced transition on reachable encoded states is realizable by a Boolean circuit with at most 2^{S_t+1}(2S_t+4)S_{t+1} NOT/AND/OR gates, when behavior off the reachable domain is arbitrary.
proof: Put k=S_t+1. Define a total transition function on all k-bit inputs by using the residual derivative {v:bv in R} when the state bits encode a reachable residual R, and outputting 0^{S_{t+1}} otherwise. For each output coordinate, its truth table has at most 2^k satisfying assignments. Write its disjunctive normal form: each minterm uses at most k NOT gates and k-1 binary AND gates; combining at most 2^k minterms uses at most 2^k-1 binary OR gates. Thus at most 2^k(2k) gates per output coordinate suffice, which is bounded by 2^k(2S_t+4). Multiply by S_{t+1}. On reachable transitions, correctness follows from R_{t+1}(pb)={v:bv in R_t(p)}.

statement_start: One-hot residual transition lemma. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N. At cut t, let R_t be the set of distinct residual suffix sets, including the empty set if it occurs, and let D_t=|R_t|. Encode each residual by its own one-hot state bit. For each input bit b, the next residual is δ_b(R)={v:bv∈R}. The transition from cut t to t+1 can be implemented with at most 2D_tD_{t+1}+D_{t+1} NOT/AND/OR gates, with arbitrary behavior on invalid one-hot states.
proof: For each next residual T∈R_{t+1}, define its output bit as the OR of terms (z_R AND [b=0]) over all R∈R_t with δ_0(R)=T, together with terms (z_R AND [b=1]) over all R∈R_t with δ_1(R)=T. Here z_R is the one-hot bit for R. Implement [b=0] with one NOT gate and [b=1] by the input wire. Each term uses at most one AND gate, and there are at most 2D_t terms per output. Combining k terms uses at most k−1 OR gates; allowing an empty disjunction as constant 0, each output costs at most 2D_t AND gates plus 2D_t OR gates. Across D_{t+1} outputs this costs at most 4D_tD_{t+1} gates, plus at most one shared NOT gate. Thus the stated 2D_tD_{t+1}+D_{t+1} bound is not justified by this construction; the proved bound is 4D_tD_{t+1}+1. For a reachable one-hot state z_R, exactly one z_R is 1, and exactly the output for δ_b(R) evaluates to 1, so the transition is correct.

evidence: The proposed bound 2D_tD_{t+1}+D_{t+1} is not established by the stated construction: each of D_{t+1} output bits may require up to 2D_t AND terms and up to 2D_t OR gates to combine them, yielding the valid bound 4D_tD_{t+1}+1 (shared NOT for the input), as the step’s own proof text acknowledges. The claimed step is internally inconsistent: its conclusion gives a smaller bound than its gate accounting.

statement: Common-accepting-suffix separation for full-search streaming. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, and let a deterministic streaming system read an N-bit word and end in a state from which a decoder outputs a circuit computing that word whenever the word belongs to F. Fix a cut t. If distinct length-t prefixes p and q have a common suffix u with pu, qu in F, then the states reached after p and q are distinct. Proof: if those states were equal, determinism implies that appending the same u reaches the same final state. The decoder would therefore output the same circuit C on both inputs. Correctness requires C to compute pu and also qu. Since p != q, pu != qu, and a single Boolean circuit computes only one truth table, a contradiction. This establishes separation only for live prefixes with intersecting accepting-suffix sets; it makes no claim for live prefixes whose accepting-suffix sets are disjoint, nor does it bound transition-circuit gate cost.
proof: Assume the states after p and q are equal. Applying identical deterministic transitions for each bit of u preserves equality, so the final states after pu and qu are equal. The decoder returns the same circuit on both. Since pu and qu are members of F, correctness requires that circuit to compute both truth tables. They differ because p and q differ, contradiction.

statement: For the explicitly defined family F of truth tables of constants, literals, and one binary Boolean operation applied to any pair of the three input variables in deterministic truth-table order, at cut t=7 there is a set P of 19 distinct live prefixes such that every two distinct p,q in P have a common suffix u with pu,qu in F. Consequently every deterministic full-search streaming system whose final decoder outputs a correct circuit for every member of F has at least 19 distinct states at cut 7. Proof: by the asserted pairwise common-suffix property, for each distinct p,q choose u with pu,qu in F. If their states were equal, determinism would give equal final states after the same u; the decoder would output one circuit for both distinct truth tables, contradicting correctness. Thus all 19 states are distinct.
proof: The family and witness are finite and explicitly enumerated in experiment cm-4fee8db16c8d462d; the corrected follow-up computation outputs all 19 witness prefixes and checks a common accepting suffix for each of the 171 pairs. For each pair, equality of states propagates under the common suffix by determinism. At the end the same decoder output would have to compute two different words pu and qu, impossible. Hence the 19 prefixes occupy distinct states.

statement: Common-suffix clique state lower bound. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and fix a cut t. Form a graph whose vertices are the live length-t prefixes p (those with at least one suffix u such that pu is in F), joining distinct p,q when they share an accepting suffix: there exists u with pu, qu in F. Every deterministic full-search streaming machine that ends in a decoder outputting the input truth table on each member of F uses at least omega(G_t) distinct states after t bits, where omega is the graph clique number.
proof: Take any clique C in G_t. For distinct p,q in C, choose a shared accepting suffix u. If the machine had the same state after p and q, determinism would make the final states after pu and qu equal, so the decoder would output the same circuit for both. But pu and qu are distinct truth tables, contradicting full-search correctness. Thus all prefixes in C occupy pairwise distinct states, requiring at least |C| states. Maximize over cliques C to obtain at least omega(G_t) states.
scope: All finite N, all F subset {0,1}^N, every cut t; constrains states only and gives no transition-gate lower bound.

statement: Finite state-capacity bound at the SC_{3,1} middle cut. Let F be the specified family of 38 truth tables, let t=7, and let P_t be its live prefixes. Any streaming encoding that assigns distinct S-bit states to live prefixes and a state disjoint from those states to at least one dead prefix must have S>=6. Proof: The 38 members of F have distinct length-7 prefixes: there are only 2^(8-7)=2 possible suffixes per prefix, so at most two distinct truth tables can share a prefix; more directly, the corrected prefix enumeration for this family gives |P_7|=38. Injectivity therefore requires 38 distinct states for live prefixes. The required dead-prefix state is outside those 38, so 2^S>=39. Since 2^5=32<39<=64=2^6, S>=6. This bound is tight as a state-capacity count alone: 64 available codes can hold the 38 live prefixes and at least one dead code. It gives no transition-circuit gate bound and does not determine G_max.

gap: The relevant unresolved task remains the Pareto trade-off (S,G_max,D) for SC classes with S<N, including whether small G_max forces work into the decoder.
evidence: Direct construction and induction: initialize q=0^N. At step t+1 copy the input bit into coordinate t+1 and wire earlier coordinates unchanged; unused coordinates remain zero. Thus after N steps q equals the entire stream, so the decoder computes its membership in L. Cost is zero because all transition outputs are wires or constants. This proves the spec's trivial S=N upper bound only; it gives no result for S<N and no lower bound on G_max.
proved_step: statement: For every N-bit input stream language L subseteq {0,1}^N, an exact one-pass transducer with S=N state bits can update the state using zero non-constant gates per step (basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants; free wires), by storing the raw prefix in the first t coordinates and zeroing the remaining coordinates; a decoder decides L from the final state.

proved_step: statement: Overlap-graph coloring lower bound for full-search streaming. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and fix a cut t. Form a graph H_t on the live length-t prefixes, joining distinct p,q iff some suffix u of length N-t has pu,qu in F. In any deterministic streaming system whose decoder outputs the truth table on every member of F, the states at cut t form a proper coloring of H_t. Thus there are at least chi(H_t) states and at least ceil(log2 chi(H_t)) state bits. Proof: if adjacent p,q had the same state, processing their shared suffix u would lead to the same final state and decoder output. But pu and qu are distinct members of F, so that output cannot be correct for both. Hence adjacent vertices have distinct states, and the state map is a proper coloring.

statement: Explicit C5 separation for overlap bounds. There is an F subset {0,1}^6 at cut t=3 whose common-accepting-suffix graph is C5, so the chromatic lower bound requires 3 states while the clique lower bound requires only 2. Choose distinct 3-bit prefixes p_0,...,p_4 and suffixes u_0,...,u_4, and set F={p_i u_i,p_i u_{i+1 mod 5}:0<=i<5}. Each prefix has accepting-suffix set {u_i,u_{i+1}}, so intersections occur exactly for neighbors on C5. C5 has clique number 2 and chromatic number 3: it is triangle-free and an odd cycle, and a 3-coloring exists.
proof: For distinct i,k, {u_i,u_{i+1}} intersects {u_k,u_{k+1}} exactly when i,k are consecutive modulo 5. Thus the graph is C5. A triangle-free graph has clique number at most 2, and C5 has edges, so omega=2. An odd cycle is not 2-colorable; assigning colors A,B,A,B,C around its five vertices is a proper 3-coloring. The previously proved overlap-state argument makes the machine's state assignment a proper coloring.

statement: Residual machine finite upper bound. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At cut t, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each p in {0,1}^t, and Q_t={R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}. Then |Q_t|<=min(2^t,2^(2^(N-t))). The deterministic transition delta_t(R,b)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R} maps Q_t into Q_{t+1} and recognizes F by accepting at t=N exactly when R_N={epsilon}. Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so the image Q_t has size at most 2^t. Every residual is a subset of the 2^(N-t) suffixes, so there are at most 2^(2^(N-t)) possible residuals. For R=R_t(p), v belongs to delta_t(R,b) iff bv belongs to R iff pbv belongs to F iff v belongs to R_{t+1}(pb), hence delta_t(R,b)=R_{t+1}(pb) and lies in Q_{t+1}. At t=N, R_N(p) contains epsilon iff p belongs to F; since its universe is {epsilon}, the stated decoder is exact. This gives an explicit finite-state upper bound; it asserts no bound on Boolean gate complexity of delta_t.

statement: Sparse-domain transition-circuit upper bound. Let k,q,r be nonnegative integers, with k>=1. Let D be any subset of {0,1}^k of size r, and let h:D->{0,1}^q be any prescribed map. In the basis NOT, binary AND, binary OR, and constants, there is a q-output Boolean circuit agreeing with h on D and using at most k+r(k-1)+q max(r-1,0) non-constant gates; its behavior outside D is unrestricted. Proof: Create the k input literals x_i and ¬x_i using at most k NOT gates. For each a in D, form its equality indicator e_a=AND_{i=1}^k l_{a,i}, where l_{a,i}=x_i if a_i=1 and ¬x_i otherwise. This uses k-1 binary AND gates per a. For output coordinate j, form the OR of e_a over those a for which h(a)_j=1. If there are d_j such rows, this needs at most max(d_j-1,0) OR gates, at most max(r-1,0). For any z in D, exactly e_z is 1 among all row indicators, so the jth output equals h(z)_j. Summing the costs gives the stated bound. If an output has no selected rows, use constant 0. This is an upper bound for an arbitrary prescribed partial transition table; it does not assert a lower bound or an exact G_max.
