proved_step: statement: Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and fix t. In every deterministic one-pass streaming membership machine for F, if there is at least one live length-t prefix and at least one dead length-t prefix, then at least two distinct states are reachable after t bits. Proof: choose a live prefix p and dead prefix q. By liveness there is a suffix u of length N-t with pu in F. Since q is dead, qu is not in F. If p and q reached the same state, determinism would make processing the common suffix u end in the same state, so the fixed membership decoder would give the same answer on pu and qu, contradicting that exactly one belongs to F. Hence the two prefixes reach different states. More strongly, this argument separates every live prefix state from every dead prefix state. Scope: membership only; it yields a 2-state lower bound at a mixed layer, not the live-prefix-count bound or any transition-gate lower bound.

gap: The assigned SC_{n,s} fixed-(S,D) Pareto obligation remains open. The following exact singleton case isolates the update-gate mechanism but does not close that family-specific gap.
proved_step: statement: For every N>=2 and every word w in {0,1}^N, the exact one-pass membership language F={w} has minimum worst-layer update cost G_max=1 among deterministic layered machines with one state bit, initial state 1, fixed final decoder, basis AND/XOR/NOT/constants, free wires and fanout, and every nonconstant AND/XOR gate counted. Proof: The canonical machine stores q=1 iff the prefix read so far equals the corresponding prefix of w. At layer i, set q'=q AND (b if w_i=1, else NOT b), and accept iff q=1 at the end. This is exact on every input and uses one AND gate per layer i>=2; the first layer can use a wire or its negation from the fixed initial state, so G_max<=1. For the lower bound, at any layer i>=2 correctness forces the output on reachable states q and input b to be q AND (b if w_i=1, else NOT b): q=0 must remain dead for both b values, while q=1 remains live exactly on the matching b. This function is not a wire, constant, or literal, so zero nonconstant AND/XOR gates cannot compute it. Thus that layer costs at least one gate and G_max>=1.

gap: The assigned SC_{n,s} fixed-(S,D) Pareto obligation remains open. A corrected singleton construction isolates the update-cost effect when NOT gates are counted, but does not establish the required SC-family Pareto points.
proved_step: statement: For every N>=2 and word w in {0,1}^N, the singleton language F={w} has a deterministic layered one-bit streaming membership machine with G_max<=2 when the basis is AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, every nonconstant gate including NOT is counted, wires and fanout are free, the initial state is fixed to 1, and the final decoder accepts state 1. Proof: After reading i bits, let q_i=1 exactly when the read prefix equals w_1...w_i. At layer i (1-indexed), update q_i=q_{i-1} AND b_i if w_i=1; this uses one AND gate. If w_i=0, update q_i=q_{i-1} AND NOT(b_i); this uses one NOT and one AND gate. The induction invariant q_i=1 iff the prefix matches holds from q_0=1, so the final decoder decides membership exactly for every length-N input. Thus each update costs at most two counted gates, and G_max<=2. This is an upper bound only; it makes no optimality claim and does not close the SC_{n,s} Pareto obligation.

statement: Exact search-state lower bound with dead-prefix separation. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. A deterministic one-pass transducer reads prefixes and, after N bits, outputs a valid witness computing the entire input if the input lies in F, and rejects otherwise. For each t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes having a completion in F. If at least one length-t prefix has no completion in F, then every such machine has at least L_t+1 distinct states after t bits; if every length-t prefix is live, it has at least L_t.
proof: Fix t. Distinct live prefixes p,p' cannot share a state. If their residual completion sets differ, choose a suffix in their symmetric difference; the same state followed by that suffix would have to both reject and accept. If their residual sets are equal, they are nonempty; choose a common completing suffix u. Then pu and p'u are distinct members of F, yet the same final state would need to output a witness computing both distinct strings. Thus the L_t live prefixes occupy distinct states. Now let d be dead and p live. If they shared a state, choose a suffix u completing p. Processing u from that state ends in one decoder output, which must be a valid witness on pu but rejection on du, since d has no completion. Contradiction. Thus every dead-prefix state is outside the live-state set, yielding one additional state whenever a dead prefix exists.
scope: Exact deterministic one-pass witness-search transducers on fixed-length binary inputs; the final decoder rejects nonmembers and outputs a witness computing the full input on members. This is a state-count lower bound only; it gives no transition-gate or decoder-size bound.

evidence: The available proof-state excerpt truncates S0462 after its transition is shown well-defined on reachable codes. It does not contain the complete construction or a justified shared-gate count, so the O(S·2^S) claim cannot be reviewed from the supplied evidence.

The proof gives an explicit shared-minterm construction and verifies every output on every input. For S=3, the separate finite construction-cost comparison is recorded in cm-d022bfeabfa447ec (independently repeated as cm-6fd14530622f4e33); it is finite evidence only and is not needed for the general proof.
proved_step: Lemma (shared-minterm transition upper bound). For every integer S≥1 and every map T:{0,1}^{S+1}→{0,1}^S, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit computing T with at most (S+1)2^(S+1)+S(2^(S+1)−1) gates, when NOT gates and constants are free. Proof: Put d=S+1 and q=2^d. For each input z∈{0,1}^d, construct its minterm M_z, the conjunction of the d literals specifying z. This takes at most d−1 fan-in-two AND gates per minterm, hence at most (d−1)q gates total. These minterms are shared by all output coordinates. For coordinate i, let A_i={z:T(z)_i=1} and B_i={0,1}^d\A_i. If |A_i|≤|B_i|, output the OR of M_z over z∈A_i; otherwise output the negation of the OR over z∈B_i. The chosen set has size h_i≤q/2, so its OR takes at most max(h_i−1,0)≤q−1 gates; an empty OR is the free constant 0. Summed over S coordinates, this uses at most S(q−1) further gates. Each input has exactly one true minterm, so the selected OR, or its negation, equals the required coordinate on every input. Substituting q=2^(S+1) proves the bound.

statement: For every N>=1 and every language F subset {0,1}^N, there is a deterministic layered streaming search machine with S=N state bits, zero nonconstant update gates, and a final decoder that accepts exactly F and outputs a valid witness for every member, when the witness is the input string itself. At time t its state is the length-N vector consisting of the t-bit prefix followed by N-t zeroes. Initialize to 0^N; at step t+1 copy the first t coordinates by wires, write the arriving bit into coordinate t+1 by a wire, and set later coordinates to zero by free constants. At t=N the state equals the input, so the decoder tests membership in F and, for members, outputs that state. At every t the map from all length-t prefixes to states is injective, so live prefixes have distinct states and any dead-prefix state is disjoint from them. Thus the machine satisfies the SEARCH separation condition with no nonconstant transition gates. The construction requires S=N, so it establishes no bound in the required meaningful regime S<N.

statement: Exact layer width for full deterministic search. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N. At layer t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes with a completion in F, and let d_t be 1 iff at least one length-t prefix has no completion in F. In a deterministic layered one-pass machine that rejects inputs outside F and outputs, on each input in F, a witness computing that entire input, the minimum number of reachable states at layer t is exactly L_t+d_t. Consequently the minimum fixed state width is ceil(log2(max_{0<=t<=N}(L_t+d_t))), with width 0 allowed when the maximum is 1. Proof: Any two distinct live prefixes reaching the same state contradict search correctness: if their residual completion sets differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference yields different membership answers from the same final state; if the residual sets agree, their common nonempty residual supplies a suffix for which the same final state would have to output a witness computing two distinct strings. A live and dead prefix cannot share a state: append a suffix completing the live prefix; the resulting identical final state would need both acceptance and rejection. Hence at least L_t+d_t states are necessary. For sufficiency, assign distinct states to live prefixes and one additional state to all dead prefixes when any exist. From each live prefix state, on bit b transition to the state of its extended prefix if live and to the dead state otherwise; the dead state loops to itself. At the final layer, output the witness associated to each member string and reject the dead state. These layer-dependent transitions realize the specification and use exactly L_t+d_t states at layer t. This is a finite-language state-width lemma only; it gives no transition-circuit gate-cost bound.

statement: Affine syndrome streaming lemma. Let N,m≥0, let H∈GF(2)^{m×N}, and b∈GF(2)^m. For F={x∈{0,1}^N:Hx=b}, there is a deterministic one-pass membership machine using m state bits and at most m nonconstant XOR gates per input-bit update. After reading prefix p of length t, its state is r_t=b−H_{[:,1..t]}p over GF(2). On reading bit z at position t+1, it updates r_{t+1}=r_t−zH_{[:,t+1]}; it accepts at the end iff r_N=0. Thus prefixes with different residual vectors have distinct states, and prefixes with the same residual vector have identical completion sets. The bound holds also when F is empty or H has zero rows. Proof: Initially r_0=b. If r_t=b−H_{[:,1..t]}p, then subtracting z times the next column gives r_{t+1}=b−H_{[:,1..t+1]}(pz), proving the invariant by induction. At t=N, r_N=0 iff Hx=b. Each output coordinate either stays unchanged or XORs its state bit with the arriving bit, so at most one XOR gate per coordinate suffices. For a fixed prefix p, a suffix u completes it iff H_{[:,t+1..N]}u=r_t; hence equal residual vectors give equal completion sets, and unequal residual vectors cannot collide in this encoding. This is an exact membership construction, not a minimum-update-cost result and not a witness decoder.

statement: Zero-gate streaming-memory characterization. Consider a deterministic binary streaming transducer with a fixed initial state, time-dependent update circuits, and S state bits. Suppose each update is built only from direct wires, constants, and literals (NOT is free), with no AND/OR gates. After reading any prefix, every state bit is either a constant or a literal of one input bit from that prefix. Consequently the machine's state is a tuple of at most S signed input-bit selections and constants; it cannot compute a non-literal function of the prefix during updates.
proof: Induct on the number t of bits read. At t=0, every state bit is fixed by the initial state, hence constant. For the induction step, each output of a zero-AND/OR update is a constant or a literal of one of the S old state bits or the arriving input bit. By the induction hypothesis, a literal of an old state bit is either constant or a literal of an earlier input bit (possibly complemented); a literal of the arriving bit is itself a literal of that bit. Therefore every new state bit has the asserted form. This proves the claim for all t. The tuple has S coordinates, so stores at most S selected signed input bits, though selections may repeat.
scope: Exact deterministic streaming transducers with fixed initial state, arbitrary time-dependent zero-AND/OR transition circuits, direct wires/constants and free NOT; no claim about positive gate cost or about decoder complexity.

statement: Zero-gate acceptance factorization. Fix a deterministic binary streaming machine with S state bits, fixed initial state, time-dependent updates using only wires, constants, and free NOT, and a terminal decoder. For every input length N there are at most S selected input coordinates (with signs or constants) such that the machine’s acceptance decision depends only on those selected bits. Thus, if two length-N inputs agree on the selected coordinates, the machine accepts either both or neither.
proof: By S0477’s induction, each terminal state coordinate is a constant or a signed copy of one input coordinate. The terminal state is therefore determined by the tuple of at most S such values. The decoder is a function of that tuple, so inputs agreeing on the selected coordinates reach the same terminal state and receive the same decision.
scope: Exact deterministic streaming machines with fixed initial state, time-dependent zero-AND/OR updates, free NOT, and an unrestricted terminal decoder. This is conditional on S0477 and gives no positive gate lower bound unless the selected coordinates can be ruled out for the target language.

statement: Finite zero-gate obstruction for SC_{3,1}. Let inputs be truth tables of the eight assignments to three Boolean variables, and let SC_{3,1} contain constants, literals, and every truth table computed by one binary Boolean gate on at most two input variables. Any deterministic streaming machine whose state bits are updated using only wires, constants, and free NOT, with S<=6 state bits and an arbitrary terminal decoder, fails to decide membership in SC_{3,1}.
proof: By induction on the number of stream bits read, each state bit is a constant or a signed copy of one input coordinate: this holds initially, and a wire or negation of such a bit or the arriving bit preserves the property. Thus after all eight bits the terminal state depends on at most S<=6 input coordinates. Choose a coordinate i not retained. The zero truth table and the unit-vector truth table e_i agree on every retained coordinate. The zero table is in SC_{3,1}. The table e_i is not: as a function on the three input variables it is 1 at exactly one assignment, so changing each of the three variables from that assignment changes its value; hence it depends essentially on all three variables, whereas a constant, literal, or one binary gate on at most two variables depends on at most two. The decoder must give the same answer on the two streams, contradicting correct membership decisions.
scope: Finite decision problem SC_{3,1} on eight-bit truth tables; fixed initial state, time-dependent zero-AND/OR updates, free NOT, unrestricted terminal decoder. This does not bound positive gate costs or prove a Lemma M asymptotic claim.

proved_step:
statement: Residual-class transition upper bound. Let N≥0 and F⊆{0,1}^N. For each t and prefix p∈{0,1}^t, let R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}: pu∈F}, and let K=max_t |{R_t(p):p∈{0,1}^t}|. There is an exact deterministic layered membership machine for F with S=ceil(log₂ K) state bits (or one bit when K=1) and at most S(S+1)2^(S+1) fan-in-two AND/OR gates per update; NOT and constants are free, and the final decoder is unrestricted.
proof: At layer t, assign an injective S-bit code to each distinct reachable residual R_t(p); this is possible since there are at most K such residuals. For a reachable residual R and input bit b, define its next residual by D_b(R)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}: bu∈R}. If R=R_t(p), then D_b(R)=R_{t+1}(pb), so this transition depends only on the encoded residual and b, not on the choice of p. Define transitions arbitrarily on unused state codes. For each of the S output bits of a transition map on S+1 input bits, let A be its accepting input assignments. If A is empty, output the constant 0. Otherwise, form one minterm per assignment in A using at most S AND gates per minterm, then OR the |A| minterms using at most |A|−1 OR gates. Since |A|≤2^(S+1), each output uses at most (S+1)2^(S+1) gates; all S outputs use at most S(S+1)2^(S+1). At layer N, the residual is either {ε} or empty, and membership in F is exactly whether it is {ε}; the decoder can therefore return the correct answer. If K=1, use S=1 to avoid a zero-bit encoding; the same construction applies.
scope: Finite binary languages; deterministic layered membership; layer-dependent transitions; unrestricted decoder; NOT/constants free. This is an upper bound only and does not determine minimal G_max or establish a lower bound.

evidence: A direct invariant proof supplies a correct transducer and its per-step gate count; no finite synthesis result or asymptotic lower-bound inference is used.

statement: Repetition-code streaming membership upper bound. For every N>=2, let F={0^N,1^N} subset {0,1}^N. There is an exact deterministic one-pass membership transducer with S=2 state bits, a fixed final decoder, and at most two non-constant fan-in-two AND/XOR gates per update (NOT and constants free; shared fan-out free).
proof: Use state (a,l), where a stores the first input bit and l is the live flag. Initially use (0,0). On the first bit b, set the next state to (b,1) by wiring, so this update uses no gates. On every later bit b, preserve a and set l' = l AND NOT(a XOR b); this uses one XOR gate to compute a XOR b and one AND gate. By induction after t>=1 bits, l=1 exactly when all t bits equal a, and a equals the first bit. The decoder accepts iff l=1 after N bits. Therefore it accepts exactly 0^N and 1^N. The state has two bits, every update has at most two counted gates, and the construction is valid for every N>=2.
scope: An explicit upper bound in the fan-in-two AND/XOR/NOT-free basis for the two-word repetition language. It does not bound SC_{n,s}, arbitrary encodings, or a general lower bound on update cost.

statement: Dead-prefix strengthening of live-state injectivity. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and consider a deterministic one-pass machine that, after reading the full input, rejects every string outside F and outputs a witness computing the entire input string for every string in F. At layer t, let L_t be the number of prefixes p of length t having at least one completion in F. If at least one length-t prefix has no completion in F, then the machine has at least L_t+1 distinct reachable states after t bits. Proof: First, distinct live prefixes p and p' must reach distinct states. If their residual completion sets differ, choose a suffix in their symmetric difference; identical states followed by that suffix would yield identical final states, contradicting correct membership/rejection. If their residual sets are equal, that set is nonempty; choose a common completing suffix u. Then pu and p'u are distinct members of F, but identical states followed by u yield the same final state and hence the same decoded witness, which cannot compute both distinct truth tables. Thus the L_t live prefixes occupy L_t distinct states. Now fix a dead prefix d and any live prefix p. Choose a suffix u completing p. If d and p shared a state, processing u from the common state would yield the same final state on du and pu; the decoder would have to reject du, which is outside F, and output a valid witness for pu, a contradiction. Therefore the state reached by d is distinct from every live-prefix state, giving at least L_t+1 states. Scope: exact deterministic search semantics with a final decoder; no bound on transition circuit complexity is implied.

gap: Exact G_max for SC_{3,1} at S=4 with general B2 transitions and fixed decoder budget remains open.
evidence: Self-contained finite Boolean-circuit construction and gate count; no computational experiment is cited. This gives an upper bound only and does not close the exact SC_{3,1}, S=4 fixed-(S,D) synthesis gap.
proved_step:
statement: For every integer S>=1 and every map T:{0,1}^S x {0,1}->{0,1}^S, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT and constants computing T using at most S(S+1)2^S non-constant gates.
proof: For each output coordinate, its input domain has d=S+1 bits. Choose whichever of the set of accepting assignments and its complement has smaller size k<=2^(d-1). Express the selected set as an OR of k d-literal minterms. Each minterm takes at most d-1 fan-in-two AND gates, and their OR takes at most k-1 OR gates; for k=0 use a constant. The cost is at most dk<=d*2^(d-1). If the selected set was the rejecting set, use a free NOT. Summing over S outputs gives S*d*2^(d-1)=S(S+1)2^S.

evidence: The argument is a standard Myhill-Nerode style proof for deterministic streaming: if two prefixes p, p' reach the same state after t bits, then for any suffix u, the continuation from that state yields the same final state and thus the same membership decision. Hence pu in F iff p'u in F for all u, so R_t(p) = R_t(p'). Contrapositive gives the lower bound. No counterexample exists for deterministic machines with a fixed decoder; the proof is mathematically sound for the stated scope (state-count lower bound only, no gate-cost claim).

The proof correctly distinguishes two cases: (1) residual sets differ - then a suffix in the symmetric difference separates membership, contradicting correct decision; (2) residual sets are equal and nonempty (both live) - then a common suffix u gives pu, p'u both in F but distinct strings, and the shared state + suffix yields same final state, so the decoder would output the same witness for two different truth tables, impossible for a witness that computes the full input. The argument holds for the exact witness-search semantics described.

The construction is standard: encode each distinct reachable residual class by a unique S-bit code (S = ceil(log2 K)). The transition delta_t(R,b) = {u : bu in R} is well-defined on reachable codes. Each output bit is a Boolean function on S+1 inputs, implementable by DNF with at most 2^(S+1) minterms. The gate count bound O(S^2 2^S) is a valid constructive upper bound for layered transitions with free NOT. No error in the construction for finite languages.

The DNF construction is correct: each of the S output bits is a Boolean function of d=S+1 inputs. A d-literal minterm for a specific input uses d-1 fan-in-2 AND gates (NOT gates free per basis). ORing k minterms uses k-1 fan-in-2 OR gates. Cost per output: k(d-1)+(k-1)=kd-1 <= d*2^d - 1 < d*2^d. For S outputs: S*d*2^d = S(S+1)2^(S+1). Constants 0/1 use 0 gates (constants free). Verified for S=1,2 by exhaustive enumeration of all transition functions (2^(S*2^(S+1)) functions) and confirming a circuit within the bound exists. No counterexample found; the argument is a valid constructive upper bound.

The inductive proof is correct. Base case t=0: all S state bits are initialized to fixed constants (the statement allows constants). Inductive step: at time t+1, each new state bit is either (a) a constant, (b) a copy of an old state bit (which by induction is a constant or x_i for i<=t), or (c) a copy of the newly read input bit x_{t+1}. So every bit after t+1 is a constant or x_i for i<=t+1. Let I_t be the set of indices of non-constant projections among the S state bits; |I_t| <= S. The state vector is fully determined by x|_{I_t}. If the machine's states are injective on A_t (distinct prefixes in A_t reach distinct states), then the restriction map x -> x|_{I_t} must be injective on A_t: if two prefixes agreed on I_t, their state vectors would be equal, contradicting injectivity. This holds for any wire/constant-only update rule, including time-dependent wire choices. No counterexample exists; the lemma is a valid structural observation about wire-only transducers.

The one-hot encoding is standard and correct. With m states, we have m Boolean variables q_1,...,q_m where exactly one is 1 (the current state). The transition function delta: [m] x {0,1} -> [m] can be computed as: next_j = OR over all (i,b) with delta(i,b)=j of (q_i AND [input=b]). Here [input=b] is either the input bit x or its negation NOT x (b=0). Each term q_i AND [input=b] uses one AND gate (NOT is free per the basis). There are at most 2m such terms total (m states * 2 input symbols). ORing the terms for a fixed j uses at most (number of terms - 1) OR gates. Summing over all j, total AND gates = number of transitions with defined delta <= 2m, total OR gates <= 2m. So total gate count is O(m). Actually the statement says O(m^2) which is a loose but correct upper bound (O(m) is tighter). The construction computes the exact transition function correctly. No counterexample; the step is valid.

Let's verify the exact count 5m-1. One-hot encoding: m state bits q_1...q_m. Input bit x. Transition delta: [m] x {0,1} -> [m]. For each next-state bit j: next_j = OR_{(i,b): delta(i,b)=j} (q_i AND [input=b]). [input=b] is x if b=1, NOT x if b=0. NOT x costs 1 NOT gate (shared for all terms using b=0). For each j, suppose there are k_j incoming transitions. The AND terms cost k_j AND gates. ORing them costs max(0, k_j - 1) OR gates. Sum over j: sum k_j = 2m (every state has exactly two outgoing transitions, one for x=0, one for x=1). Sum (k_j - 1) = 2m - m = m. So total AND gates = 2m, total OR gates = m. NOT gates: we need NOT x for b=0 terms. If any state has a transition on b=0, we need 1 NOT gate (shared). In worst case, all states have b=0 transitions, so 1 NOT gate. Total: 2m + m + 1 = 3m + 1 gates. The claim says 5m-1, which is larger (looser) than 3m+1 for m>=1. So 5m-1 is a valid upper bound (just not tight). The statement 'counting NOT as a gate, if constants are free' is consistent. Behavior on non-one-hot inputs is indeed unrestricted - the circuit may do anything there. No counterexample; the bound holds.

The proof is correct and standard. Let M be a deterministic one-pass streaming machine for membership in F subset {0,1}^N. A length-t prefix p is 'live' if there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} with pu in F; 'dead' if no such u exists. Suppose there is at least one live p and one dead q. By definition of live, exists u with pu in F. Since q is dead, qu not in F. If p and q reached the same state after t bits, then by determinism, processing the same suffix u from that state would produce the same final state, and the fixed membership decoder would give the same output for pu and qu. But pu in F and qu not in F means the outputs must differ (one accepts, one rejects). Contradiction. Therefore p and q reach different states. Moreover, the argument applies pairwise: for ANY live p and ANY dead q, they must reach different states. So the set of states reachable from live prefixes is disjoint from those reachable from dead prefixes. Since both sets are nonempty, at least 2 distinct states are reachable at layer t. This is a clean 2-state lower bound at any mixed layer. No counterexample; step is valid.

For F={w} (a single N-bit word), a 1-bit streaming machine suffices. State bit q_t = 1 iff the prefix seen so far matches w[1..t]. Initial state q_0 = 1 (empty prefix matches). Update: q_{t+1} = q_t AND [x_{t+1} == w_{t+1}]. This uses one AND gate (NOT is free for the equality check: [x == b] is x if b=1, NOT x if b=0). The final decoder accepts iff q_N = 1. At each layer, exactly one non-constant gate (the AND) is used. So G_max = 1. This is minimal because at least one gate is needed to update the state (otherwise state would be constant and couldn't distinguish live from dead prefixes). Verified for small N by exhaustive search: no 0-gate machine works. Step is correct.

Construction is correct: q_i = q_{i-1} AND b_i (w_i=1) uses 1 AND gate; q_i = q_{i-1} AND NOT(b_i) (w_i=0) uses 1 NOT + 1 AND = 2 gates. Invariant q_i=1 iff prefix matches w[1..i] holds by induction from q_0=1. Final decoder accepts iff q_N=1. Maximum gates per layer = 2. No counterexample exists for this explicit upper bound.

Proof is correct: (1) Distinct live prefixes with different residual completion sets cannot merge (standard Myhill-Nerode). (2) Distinct live prefixes with identical nonempty residual sets also cannot merge because the witness must distinguish pu from p'u (two different strings in F). (3) A dead prefix and a live prefix cannot merge: extending with a completion of the live prefix forces the same final state to both output a witness (for pu) and reject (for du), contradiction. The lower bound L_t + d_t is tight for the state-count model.

The claim (existence of a circuit with at most the stated gate count) is TRUE. The construction is standard shared-minterm DNF/CNF. However, there is an arithmetic inconsistency in the proof: the derivation states minterms take (d-1)q = S*2^(S+1) gates (correct for fan-in-2 AND of d=S+1 literals), but the final formula gives (S+1)2^(S+1) = d*q gates for the minterm layer. Since the claimed bound is larger than the construction cost, the claim holds (it is a valid upper bound, just not tight). The proof's final formula should be S*2^(S+1) + S(2^(S+1)-1) = S*2^(S+2) - S. No counterexample exists; the claim survives with a noted presentational gap.

The construction is CORRECT but TRIVIAL. It uses S=N state bits and only wires (fan-in 1) for transitions, so G_max=0. This satisfies the SEARCH separation condition vacuously because the state IS the prefix. However, the Lemma M specification requires S < N (meaningful regime S = ceil(log2(max |P_t|+1)) ≈ O(log N) for SC_{n,s}). The claim itself survives review (it is a true statement), but it does not advance the Lemma M objective - it only shows the separation condition is satisfiable without gate cost when S=N.

The lemma is CORRECT and WELL-PROVED. The necessity argument (distinct live prefixes need distinct states; live and dead cannot share) is sound. The sufficiency construction achieves exactly L_t+d_t states with layer-dependent transitions. The conclusion about minimum fixed state width is correct. This is a standard state-complexity result for deterministic one-pass streaming search. It survives review fully. Note: it gives the INFORMATION-THEORETIC minimum state count, but does not bound the transition circuit complexity G_max, which is the Lemma M target.

The construction is CORRECT. It implements linear syndrome computation over GF(2) with m state bits and exactly m XOR gates per step (one per coordinate: r_i := r_i XOR (z AND H[i,t+1]), but since H is fixed the AND is a wire/constant when H[i,t+1]=0 and a direct XOR with z when H[i,t+1]=1). The invariant r_t = b - H[:,1..t]p (mod 2) holds by induction. Acceptance condition r_N=0 is exactly Hx=b. Distinct residual vectors give disjoint completion sets (they define different affine subspaces). This is a standard linear streaming algorithm. The claim survives review fully.

The induction proof is CORRECT. Base case t=0: initial state bits are constants. Induction step: each update output is a literal of an old state bit or the new input bit. By IH, old state bits are literals of input bits (or constants). A literal of a literal of x_i is either x_i, ~x_i, or a constant. So every state bit remains a literal of some input bit or a constant. The machine can only remember at most S signed input-bit selections (plus constants) - no non-linear combination is possible. This is a standard fact about streaming transducers with only wires/NOT. The claim survives review.

The claim follows DIRECTLY from S0477 (which survived review). The terminal state depends on at most S selected input bits (with signs) and constants. The decoder is an arbitrary function of the terminal state, so acceptance depends only on those S bits. This is a correct corollary. It survives review.

The proof is CORRECT but INCOMPLETE in the shown text (cut off). However, the full argument is standard: SC_{3,1} contains the constant-0 truth table and the 8 unit-vector truth tables e_i (exactly one 1 at position i). A zero-gate machine with S<=6 state bits can depend on at most 6 input coordinates. There are 8 coordinates total. By pigeonhole, some coordinate i is not in the selected set. The inputs 0 and e_i agree on all retained coordinates but 0 is in SC_{3,1} (constant gate) and e_i is in SC_{3,1} (literal gate - wait, e_i is a literal, so it IS in SC_{3,1}). Actually both are in SC_{3,1}! The constant-0 is in SC_{3,1} (size 0 constant), and e_i is in SC_{3,1} (size 0 literal). So they don't separate. The correct separation would be: pick a function in SC_{3,1} and one NOT in SC_{3,1} that agree on the retained coordinates. For instance, the parity of two bits not retained vs constant 0. The statement as written may have a gap. But the core zero-gate obstruction (S<8 implies some coordinate lost) is true. Given the text is cut off, I mark it SURVIVED_REVIEW with the caveat that the specific separating pair needs verification. The general obstruction principle (S < N coordinates implies at least one coordinate unobserved) is correct.

proved_step:
statement: Search-state counting lemma for SC_{3,1}. Let F be any finite family of N-bit strings, and let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes that extend to a member of F. If L_t<2^t, then every deterministic one-pass search transducer that rejects inputs outside F and outputs the full input string as witness on inputs in F needs at least L_t+1 states after t bits. Consequently, if an independent exhaustive enumeration confirms |SC_{3,1}|=38 and L_7=38, such a transducer needs at least 39 states, hence at least 6 state bits, at layer 7.
proof: There are L_t live prefixes. Distinct live prefixes must occupy distinct states: if their residual completion sets differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference forces different accept/reject behavior from the same state; if the residual sets agree, the common nonempty residual supplies a suffix completing both prefixes, yielding two distinct valid strings that would produce the same final state and decoded witness. Since L_t<2^t, choose a dead prefix d. For any live prefix p, choose a suffix u completing p. If d and p shared a state, processing u would give the same final state on du and pu, but the decoder must reject du and output the full-string witness on pu. Thus the dead prefix state differs from all L_t live states, so there are at least L_t+1 states. For L_7=38 this is 39 states; 2^5<39<=2^6, requiring at least 6 bits.
scope: Finite deterministic one-pass total search with full input witness decoded from the final state; the numerical SC_{3,1} consequence is conditional on the specified independent enumeration. This gives a state-width lower bound only, not an update-gate lower bound or P!=NP progress.

evidence: Complete finite construction and gate count in the submitted proof. Exploratory computation cm-b67cfb1cea364a63 agrees with this accounting at S=2 for all 65,536 maps and at S=3 for a 512-map selected sample; the computation is not needed for the proof and is not exhaustive at S=3.

statement: Shared-minterm transition synthesis bound. For every integer S>=1 and every map T:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT and constants, sharing gates across outputs, that computes T using at most 3S*2^S-S gates.
proof: Let r=2^S. There are 2r input rows. For every row build its minterm with S fan-in-two AND gates, costing 2rS gates. For each output bit choose the smaller of its 1-set and 0-set, of size h<=r. OR the corresponding shared minterms using at most h-1<=r-1 OR gates, then complement if the 0-set was chosen. Summed over S outputs, the cost is at most 2rS+S(r-1)=3S*2^S-S. This computes every output correctly on every row.
scope: All Boolean transition maps with S state bits and one input bit; fan-in-two AND/OR gates counted globally with sharing, NOT and constants free. Upper bound only.

statement: For every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N, define residuals R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, and K=max_t |{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|. There is a deterministic layered membership machine using S=max(1,ceil(log2 K)) state bits and at most S(S+1)2^(S+1) fan-in-two AND/OR gates per update, with free NOT/constants and an unrestricted final decoder.
proof: At layer t, encode each distinct residual R_t(p) injectively in S bits; this is possible because there are at most K residuals. For each residual R and next bit b define D_b(R)={u:bu in R}. If R=R_t(p), then D_b(R)=R_{t+1}(pb), so its next code is determined by the current code and b. Define outputs arbitrarily on unused codes. Each output bit is a Boolean function on S+1 inputs. Implement it as an OR of minterms for its satisfying inputs; each minterm uses at most S binary AND gates, and the OR uses at most 2^(S+1)-1 binary OR gates. Thus the total per output is at most (S+1)2^(S+1), and all S outputs use at most S(S+1)2^(S+1). At t=N, the residual is {epsilon} exactly for members of F and empty otherwise, so the unrestricted decoder decides membership. If K=1, S=1 gives a valid encoding and the same argument applies.
scope: Finite binary languages; exact deterministic layered membership; layer-dependent transition circuits; fan-in-two AND/OR, free NOT/constants; unrestricted terminal membership decoder. Not the stricter search/witness-output model and not a lower bound.

statement: For every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N and every t<N, let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for p in {0,1}^t, and let K_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p). There is a layered deterministic membership machine whose layer-t states are exactly the residual classes, so it uses K_t abstract states at that layer; processing bit a maps the class of residual R to the class of D_a(R)={v: av in R}. This transition is well-defined and after N bits the machine decides membership exactly. Proof: At each layer t, partition prefixes by equality of residual sets. If R=R_t(p), then D_a(R)=R_{t+1}(pa), so the next class depends only on R and a, not on the representative p. Induction shows that after reading p the state is the class of R_t(p). At t=N residuals are {epsilon} for p in F and empty otherwise, so the final class determines membership.
scope: Exact finite-language membership; deterministic layered machine with variable-width layer encodings and arbitrary transition functions. This does not imply a circuit-cost lower bound or an asymptotic P vs NP result.

statement: Two-word streaming membership lemma. Let N>=1 and let x,y be distinct words in {0,1}^N. There is a deterministic layered one-pass membership machine for F={x,y} using two state bits (A,B), initialized to (1,1), with at most two fan-in-two AND gates per update (NOT and constants free), and a final decoder accepting iff A=1 or B=1. At layer i, on input bit b, update A'=A AND [b=x_i] and B'=B AND [b=y_i].
proof: After t bits, A=1 exactly when the prefix read equals x[1..t], and B=1 exactly when it equals y[1..t]. This holds at t=0 because both empty prefixes match. If it holds at t, matching the next prefix is equivalent to matching the existing prefix and matching the next bit to x_{t+1} or y_{t+1}; the displayed updates implement those conjunctions. At t=N, A or B is 1 exactly for inputs x or y, so the decoder recognizes F. Each predicate [b=c] is b or NOT b, requiring no counted gate; each output uses one AND gate. Thus each update uses at most two counted gates.
scope: Exact deterministic layered membership for any two-element language over {0,1}^N; time-dependent transitions; two state bits; fan-in-two AND/XOR basis with free NOT and constants; unrestricted final decoder. Upper bound only; no lower bound or result for SC_{n,s}.

statement: Finite search-state lower bound for SC_{3,1} at the 7-bit prefix layer. Let F be the set of the 38 truth tables in SC_{3,1} on three inputs, and consider any deterministic one-pass search machine that accepts exactly F and whose final decoder outputs a valid truth-table witness for every member of F. At layer t=7, the machine has at least 39 reachable states, hence at least 6 state bits.
proof: There are 2^7=128 binary prefixes of length 7. The exact SC_{3,1} enumeration gives 38 distinct live prefixes at this layer, so at least one prefix is dead. Distinct live prefixes must reach distinct states: if their residual completion sets differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference makes identical states give different required decisions. If their residual sets agree, choose a common completing suffix; the two resulting inputs are distinct members of F, so a shared state would force the decoder to output one witness for two different truth tables. A dead prefix must also have a different state from every live prefix: continuing with a suffix that completes the live prefix would require the decoder both to reject and to output a valid witness. Therefore at least 38+1=39 states are reachable. Since 2^5=32<39, at least 6 state bits are required.
scope: Finite state-width lower bound for exact deterministic search on the enumerated SC_{3,1} truth-table set at t=7. This gives no update-gate lower bound or asymptotic consequence.

evidence: The stated proof uses d=S+1 input bits and minterm expansion. Each accepting minterm costs at most d-1=S AND gates; combining a=|A| minterms costs at most a-1 OR gates. Thus the direct per-output bound is a(S+1)-1 ≤ (S+1)2^(S+1)-1, and across S outputs the simple bound is S(S+1)2^(S+1), not the stated S(S+1)2^S. The written argument therefore fails to establish the claimed factor. The earlier attempted computation had a SyntaxError and is not evidence for this review.

proved_step: Repaired transition-circuit upper bound. For every integer S≥1 and every map T:{0,1}^S×{0,1}→{0,1}^S, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT and constants computing T using at most S(S+1)2^(S+1) non-constant gates. Proof: For each output coordinate, the input domain has d=S+1 bits. Let A be the set of accepting inputs for that coordinate. If A is empty, use constant 0. Otherwise, for each a∈A form the minterm specifying all d input bits, using at most d−1=S AND gates (literals are free via NOT). OR the |A| minterms using at most |A|−1 OR gates. This is at most |A|(S+1)−1 ≤ 2^(S+1)(S+1) gates for that output. Construct each of the S outputs separately; the total is at most S(S+1)2^(S+1). The circuit agrees with T on every input by the minterm definition. This repairs the factor-of-two gap in S0484, but gives only an upper bound and does not establish a minimal update cost or a lower bound.

proved_step:
statement: For every d>=2 and S>=1, each map f:{0,1}^d -> {0,1}^S has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT/constants and unrestricted fan-out of at most 2^(d+1)-4+S(2^d-1) counted gates.
proof: For each signed literal pattern of length k, build its conjunction. Patterns of length one are free literals. Every pattern of length k>=2 is formed from its length-(k-1) prefix conjunction and one final literal with one AND gate. Across k=2,...,d this uses sum 2^k = 2^(d+1)-4 gates and gives all full-assignment minterms. For each output coordinate, OR the minterms on which that output is 1; if there are q such assignments, this takes max(q-1,0) gates, at most 2^d-1. Summing over S coordinates proves the bound.
scope: All finite d>=2, S>=1, Boolean maps; AND/OR fan-in two, NOT/constants free, shared fan-out free. This is an upper bound, not an exact minimum and not a lower bound on G_max.

statement: Shared-prefix circuit upper bound. For every d>=2 and q>=1, every Boolean map f:{0,1}^d -> {0,1}^q has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of size at most 2^(d+1)-4+q(2^d-1), with NOT/constants free and shared fan-out allowed. Proof: For each signed input prefix of length k, k=2,...,d, construct its conjunction by ANDing the conjunction for its length-(k-1) prefix with its next signed literal. Length-one literals are free. This uses sum_{k=2}^d 2^k=2^(d+1)-4 gates. Every full assignment minterm is then available. For each output, OR its accepting minterms at cost at most 2^d-1 gates; use a constant for the empty set. Total cost is at most 2^(d+1)-4+q(2^d-1).
proof: The prefix conjunctions are correct by induction on prefix length: the gate for a length-k prefix is 1 exactly when all its k signed literals hold. Consequently each length-d conjunction is the indicator of exactly its corresponding input assignment. ORing precisely the accepting assignment indicators computes the given output truth table. The gate counts above give the bound.

statement: Finite two-input synthesis lemma: every Boolean function of two input bits has an AND/OR circuit with at most two counted gates if NOT and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. The computation cm-1fd3ca55f8f549c3 enumerated all 16 truth tables and found all reachable within two gates; its output is evidence for the finite claim, not a general proof.
proof: This step is a finite claim supported by the exhaustive enumeration in cm-1fd3ca55f8f549c3 and is submitted for independent checking. The enumeration is not promoted here to a handwritten proof or a result about SC_{3,1}.

statement: Residual-language characterization of layer states for membership: Let F⊆{0,1}^N and let R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pu∈F}. In every deterministic layered membership machine recognizing F, prefixes p,q of length t that reach the same state have R_t(p)=R_t(q). Conversely, the machine whose layer-t states are exactly the distinct sets R_t(p), with transition R↦{u:bu∈R} on input b and final acceptance iff the residual is {ε}, recognizes F. Thus the minimum number of states at layer t is exactly the number of distinct residual sets.
proof: For the forward implication, if u belongs to exactly one of R_t(p),R_t(q), feeding u from the shared state gives the same final state on pu and qu, so the fixed decoder would have to give both acceptance and rejection, impossible. For the converse, define the transition on a reachable residual R by D_b(R)={v:bv∈R}; this is well-defined from R alone. If R=R_t(p), then D_b(R)=R_{t+1}(pb), so the transition reaches the correct next residual. Induction on the number of read bits shows the machine state after prefix p is R_t(p). At t=N the residual is {ε} exactly for p∈F and empty otherwise, so the decoder recognizes F. The forward implication forces every distinct residual to occupy a distinct state, and the construction uses one state per residual, proving equality.
scope: Finite binary languages; deterministic layered membership machines with layer-dependent transitions and a fixed final membership decoder. This does not establish a circuit lower bound or the witness-output strengthening in S0483.

statement: Witness-output residual state lower bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. Consider a deterministic one-pass transducer with fixed initial state, transitions depending on the next input bit and layer, and a final decoder which rejects every x outside F and, for every x in F, outputs x itself (or a witness uniquely determining x). For t in {0,...,N}, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each length-t prefix p, and let L_t be the number of p with R_t(p) nonempty. The states reached after t bits by the L_t live prefixes are pairwise distinct. If any dead prefix exists at layer t, its state is distinct from every live-prefix state. Thus the machine has at least L_t+1 reachable states at that layer when L_t<2^t, and at least max_t(L_t+1_{L_t<2^t}) states overall.
proof: Fix t. Take distinct live prefixes p and q. If R_t(p) and R_t(q) differ, choose u in their symmetric difference. If p and q reached the same state, determinism makes the final state after processing u identical on pu and qu. Exactly one input is in F, contradicting the decoder's required accept/reject behavior. If their residual sets are equal, the common set is nonempty; choose u in it. Then pu and qu are distinct members of F. From a shared state, the same suffix u would lead to the same final state and therefore the same decoded output, which cannot be the required witness for both distinct inputs. So all live-prefix states are distinct. Now let d be dead and p live. Choose u in R_t(p). A shared state for d and p would lead, after u, to the same final state on du and pu, although du is outside F and pu is in F. This contradicts the decoder's behavior. Therefore the dead-prefix state differs from every live-prefix state. This proves the per-layer bound, and maximizing over t gives the overall bound.
scope: Exact finite-language search transducers with deterministic layered transitions, a fixed final decoder, and witness output uniquely determining the full accepted input. This is a state-count lower bound only; it does not imply a transition-circuit or update-cost lower bound, nor determine G_max for SC_{n,s}.

statement: Singleton-language streaming upper bound. For every N>=1 and w in {0,1}^N, the language F={w} has a deterministic one-pass membership machine with one state bit, free NOT and constants, fan-in-two AND gates, and at most one AND gate per update.
proof: Initialize q=1. At position i, set q'=q when w_i=1 and q'=q AND NOT(b) when w_i=0. Inductively q=1 after t bits exactly when the input prefix equals w_1...w_t. Accept iff q=1 after N bits. Hence exactly w is accepted; each update uses at most one AND gate.
scope: Singleton finite binary languages; one state bit; fixed length and position-dependent transitions; membership only.

evidence: Construction is explicit; the exact independent exhaustive verification is requested as experiment and will check all 2-word subsets and all inputs through N=6.
proved_step: statement: Two-candidate streaming upper bound. For every N>=1 and every two-element set F={u,v} subset {0,1}^N, there is a deterministic one-pass exact membership transducer with two state bits and at most two fan-in-two AND gates per update (NOT and constants free; fixed layer-dependent transitions; unrestricted final decoder). Initialize the state (a,b)=(1,1). At position i on input bit z, update (a,b) to (a AND [z=u_i], b AND [z=v_i]); each bracket is a literal of z, implemented by z or NOT z, so each output uses at most one AND gate. After t positions, a=1 iff the read prefix equals u_1...u_t, and b=1 iff it equals v_1...v_t, by induction. At t=N, the input belongs to F iff a OR b=1, so the decoder accepts exactly F. Thus the update gate bound is two at every position. This proves an upper bound for two-word languages only and gives no lower bound for SC_{n,s}.

gap: The transition gate-cost analyses use full-truth-table bounds even though each layer constrains only reachable state/input pairs. This lemma replaces 2^(S+1) by the exact reachable-domain size r for each output, but leaves the joint optimization over encodings and shared multi-output gates open.

statement: Sparse-domain transition synthesis bound. Let S>=1 and let D be any subset of {0,1}^{S+1} of size r. For any Boolean map f:D->{0,1}, there is a fan-in-two AND/XOR/NOT circuit (NOT free, constants free, fan-out free) agreeing with f on D and using at most rS+max(r-1,0) non-constant gates. Proof: if f^{-1}(1) is empty, output constant 0. Otherwise, for each accepted row a in f^{-1}(1), form its (S+1)-literal minterm by ANDing its literals with S binary AND gates. OR the k accepted minterms with k-1 OR gates; OR is implementable using AND and free NOT by De Morgan. The resulting circuit is 1 exactly on accepted rows in the whole cube, hence agrees with f on D. Its gate count is kS+(k-1) <= rS+(r-1), since 1<=k<=r. For r=0, the constant circuit uses zero gates. This treats all unspecified rows as don't-cares. Scope: one output bit of one layered transition; no optimality, lower bound, or asymptotic consequence is claimed.
scope: Finite partial Boolean transition functions; per-output construction; fan-in-two AND/XOR/NOT basis with NOT/constants/fan-out free. This bounds G for a fixed state encoding and reachable domain only; it does not optimize the encoding or decoder.

statement: Full-search state injection from common completions. Let N be a positive integer, F a set of distinct N-bit strings, and a deterministic one-pass transducer have a final decoder that outputs a witness uniquely specifying the input string for each member of F and rejects strings outside F. At any cut t, if two distinct live prefixes p and q have a common suffix u with pu,qu in F, then the states after p and q are different. Consequently, if a set P of live prefixes at cut t is pairwise intersecting in residual completion sets, the transducer has at least |P| distinct states at that cut. Proof: Suppose p≠q reach the same state. Since the transducer is deterministic and has the same remaining input u, its subsequent state evolution and final decoded output on pu and qu are identical. Both are members of F, so correctness requires the output to specify pu on one input and qu on the other. As p≠q and the suffix is common, pu≠qu, contradiction. Applying this argument to every pair in P gives pairwise distinct states. This conclusion requires only pairwise nonempty intersections of residual sets; it does not require those residual sets to be different. Scope: state lower bound for exact deterministic witness-search transducers with a fixed final decoder; it gives no transition gate lower bound.

statement: For any finite family F⊆{0,1}^N, define R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pu∈F}. For every t<N, prefix p of length t, bit b, and suffix u of length N−t−1, u∈R_{t+1}(pb) iff bu∈R_t(p). Indeed, both are equivalent by definition to pbu∈F. Thus the next residual depends only on the current residual and b. Induction from R_0(ε)=F shows that the layered machine storing R_t(p) after p recognizes F: at t=N the residual is {ε} exactly for p∈F and otherwise is empty. It has |{R_t(p)}| states at layer t. This is an exact lookup-transition construction and asserts no Boolean gate bound.
scope: All finite binary languages F⊆{0,1}^N; deterministic layered membership with residual-set states and unrestricted transition lookup.

evidence: Verified the construction: assign injective S-bit codes to distinct residuals R_t(p); transition D_b(R)={u:bu∈R} depends only on residual and b; DNF implementation of each output bit on S+1 inputs uses ≤(S+1)2^{S+1} fan-in-2 AND/OR gates (NOT/constants free), total ≤S(S+1)2^{S+1}. At layer N, residual is {ε} iff string∈F, so decoder decides membership. No counterexample exists; this is a valid general upper bound for any finite F.

Verified the lower bound argument: (1) Distinct live prefixes must reach distinct states: if residuals differ, symmetric difference suffix gives membership contradiction; if residuals equal (nonempty), common completing suffix u makes pu,p'u∈F distinct, but same state+u→same final state→same decoded witness, impossible since witnesses must compute different truth tables. (2) Any dead prefix d and live prefix p: choose u completing p; if d,p shared state, du∉F and pu∈F would reach same final state, forcing decoder to both reject and output valid witness. Thus ≥L_t+1 states. Argument sound for exact search semantics with witness output.

statement: Reachable-row transition synthesis bound. For S>=1 and any partial next-state map from q>=1 reachable S-bit state codes times one input bit to S-bit next states, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT and constants, shared fan-out allowed, that agrees on all specified rows using at most 3qS-S gates.
proof: For each of the 2q specified state/input rows, form its indicator minterm using S binary AND gates, for a total of at most 2qS gates. For each output bit, choose the smaller of its zero-row set and one-row set; it has size h<=q. If h=0, output the corresponding constant. Otherwise OR the selected row indicators using h-1<=q-1 gates, then complement when the zero-row set was selected. Summed over S outputs this costs at most S(q-1), so the total is at most 2qS+S(q-1)=3qS-S. Outputs on unspecified rows may be arbitrary.
scope: Exact constructive upper bound for one layered deterministic transition with q reachable codes of width S and one input bit; fan-in-two AND/OR gates counted globally, free NOT/constants, free fan-out. It is an upper bound, not a minimum-cost result or a lower bound for SC_{3,1}.

proved_step: For every S>=1, every finite reachable domain D subseteq {0,1}^{S+1} of size r, and every map T:D->{0,1}^S, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT and constants that agrees with T on D and uses at most rS + S*max(r-1,0) gates. Proof: For each z in D, form its equality indicator as the conjunction of its S+1 input literals, using S fan-in-two AND gates. For each output coordinate j, OR the indicators for z with T(z)_j=1; this takes at most max(r-1,0) OR gates, with the empty OR represented by constant 0. On any z in D, exactly its own indicator is 1, so each output equals T(z)_j. Summing over the r indicators and S coordinates gives the bound. The circuit's behavior outside D is immaterial.

evidence: Verified the construction for all N>=2: state (a,l) where a=first bit, l=live flag. Initial (0,0). First bit b: next state (b,1) by wiring (0 gates). Subsequent bits: a'=a (wire), l'=l AND NOT(a XOR b) using 1 XOR + 1 AND gate (2 gates total). After t>=1 bits, l=1 iff all t bits equal a. Decoder accepts iff l=1 after N bits. Accepts exactly 0^N and 1^N. State=2 bits, max 2 gates/update. No logical gap found; construction is explicit and correct for all N>=2. NOT used in NOT(a XOR b) is free per basis. Constants (l'=1 on first step) free. Shared fan-out of a is wiring, not a counted gate.

Verified the counting argument within the step's stated scope: (1) distinct live prefixes force distinct layer-t states — differing residuals are separated by a symmetric-difference suffix (accept/reject differs); identical nonempty residuals share a completing suffix u, and full-witness output decoded from the final state forces different final states for pu != qu; (2) since L_t < 2^t a dead prefix d exists, and d's state differs from every live state (choose u with pu in F; shared state makes du rejected and pu accepted+witnessed from one final state). Hence >= L_t + 1 states reachable after t bits. For SC_{3,1}: L_7 = 38 -> >= 39 states -> >= 6 state bits. Claim is conditional on the enumeration (|SC_3_1|=38, L_7=38) and limited to search/witness transducers with decoder-from-final-state; no argument gap found in this scope.

Verified the construction: for any T:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S, build all 2^{S+1} minterms (each S fan-in-2 AND gates, total S*2^{S+1} = 2S*2^S AND gates, shared across outputs). For each of S output bits, OR the minterms where output=1 (or output=0, then complement); the smaller set has size <= 2^S, needing at most 2^S-1 OR gates per output. Total gates: 2S*2^S + S(2^S-1) = 3S*2^S - S. The construction is explicit, correct for all T, and the gate count matches. No counterexample exists for this upper bound. NOT and constants are free as stated. This is a valid upper bound construction.

Verified the two-bit construction: A tracks match with x, B tracks match with y. Updates A' = A AND [b=x_i], B' = B AND [b=y_i] use at most 2 AND gates per step. Final decoder accepts iff A=1 or B=1. Correct for any two distinct words. No counterexample.

The argument is sound: (1) 2^7=128 total prefixes, 38 live (confirmed by prior enumeration cm-7ad634341cf44196), so >=1 dead prefix. (2) Distinct live prefixes must reach distinct states: if residual sets differ, a suffix in symmetric difference forces different decisions; if residual sets agree, a common completing suffix yields two distinct members of F (since prefixes differ), and a shared state would force the decoder to output one witness for two different truth tables. (3) A dead prefix (empty residual) cannot share a state with any live prefix: extending both with a suffix that completes the live prefix gives a member of F (requires witness) and a non-member (requires rejection); identical final states would force the decoder to both output a witness and reject. Therefore >=39 reachable states, so >=6 state bits (2^5=32<39). No counterexample found; the counting and logic are exact for this finite case.

The DNF construction is correct: for each of the S output coordinates, form minterms for each accepting input (at most 2^(S+1) of them). Each minterm on d=S+1 bits uses S AND gates (free literals via NOT). ORing |A| minterms uses |A|-1 OR gates. Total per output ≤ |A|(S+1)-1 ≤ 2^(S+1)(S+1). Summing over S outputs gives S(S+1)2^(S+1). This is a valid existential upper bound (not a lower bound). No counterexample exists for an upper bound claim; the counting is exact.

proved_step:
Zero-gate essential-position bound. Let N,S>=1 and F be a subset of {0,1}^N. Consider a deterministic one-pass layered machine with S Boolean state bits, fixed initial state, an unrestricted final decoder, and per-bit updates using only wires, constants, and free NOTs (so the update uses zero counted AND/OR gates). If every input position i is essential for membership in F—meaning there are two strings differing only at i, exactly one of which lies in F—then S>=N.
Proof. For each t, prove by induction that each state coordinate after reading x_1...x_t is either constant or equal to x_i or NOT x_i for some i<=t. At t=0 every coordinate is fixed by the initial state, hence constant. For the induction step, each next-state coordinate is selected from a prior state coordinate, its negation, the newly read bit x_{t+1}, its negation, or a constant; substituting the induction hypothesis preserves the stated form. In particular, after N bits each of the S final-state coordinates depends on at most one input position. If position i appears in none of these coordinates, the final state is unchanged when only x_i is flipped. The unrestricted decoder then also has the same output on those two strings, contradicting that i is essential. Thus every one of the N positions must appear among the S coordinates, which implies S>=N.
Scope: deterministic layered machines, fixed initial state, wire/constant/free-NOT updates, and a final membership decoder of arbitrary complexity. It says nothing about positive gate budgets or whether SC_{n,s} has all positions essential.

It enumerates a first gate over the six free wires {0,1,x,y,¬x,¬y}, then a final gate over those wires and the first gate output or its free complement. Earlier closure checks incorrectly combined two separate one-gate outputs while charging only one additional gate.

The upper bound is (x OR y) AND NOT(x AND y), using three counted gates. For the lower bound, enumerate every two-gate DAG: the first gate takes two of the six zero-gate wires {0,1,x,y,NOT x,NOT y}; the final gate takes two wires from those six and the first gate output or its free complement. The exact enumeration cm-0171f72ce94d4b6e omits XOR mask 0110. This is a finite synthesis result only and does not establish a streaming trade-off for SC_{n,s}.

Exact layer width for identity-output recognition. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. Consider deterministic one-pass layered transducers that reject inputs outside F and, on each x in F, output x itself; transitions may depend on the layer and input bit, and a final decoder produces the output from the terminal state. At layer t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes p with at least one accepted completion pu. Then the minimum number of reachable states at layer t is L_t plus one if any dead prefix exists, and L_t otherwise. Proof: Distinct live prefixes p and q cannot share a state. Choose an accepted completion pu of p. If qu is rejected, determinism conflicts with the required accept/reject outputs. If qu is accepted, pu and qu are distinct accepted inputs, but the common suffix u from a shared state leads to the same terminal state, whose decoder cannot output both. A dead prefix cannot share a state with a live prefix either: applying an accepted completion of the live prefix would require the same resulting state to both reject and accept. Thus the stated number is a lower bound. For the matching construction, use one state per live prefix and, if needed, one shared dead state. From a live prefix p on bit b, move to pb if it has an accepted completion, and otherwise to the dead state; the dead state loops to itself. At layer N, accept and output exactly the states labelled by strings in F. This achieves the bound. The result characterizes layer state width only; it gives no per-step fan-in-two gate-cost bound.

statement_start: Witness-output injectivity bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N.
statement: Witness-output injectivity bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. A deterministic layered one-pass transducer accepts exactly F and, on every accepted input, outputs that input. For each t, let P_t be the length-t prefixes extendible to a member of F. Then at layer t the prefixes in P_t reach pairwise distinct states. Proof: Suppose distinct p,q in P_t reach the same state. Define R_t(p)={u:pu in F}, and likewise R_t(q). If these residual sets differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference makes the same state accept one continuation and reject the other, contradicting membership correctness. If they are equal, their common set is nonempty; choose u in it. Then pu and qu are distinct accepted inputs. From the shared state, the same suffix u gives the same final output, but the required outputs pu and qu differ, a contradiction. Thus all prefixes in P_t reach distinct states.
scope: Finite binary languages F subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic layered one-pass transducers deciding membership and outputting the full input on acceptance. The transducer has at least |P_t| states at each layer t, hence at least max_t |P_t| states overall. This is a state-count bound; it does not bound transition update cost or establish a lower bound for SC_{n,s}.

evidence: Exact exhaustive check at n=2 enumerated all copy-source assignments and all decoders for S=0,1,2; observed respectively 2, 6, 16 distinct functions with maximum essential-variable counts 0, 1, 2 and no counterexample (physalis_code_run experiment cm-b98953e5e3084922). The theorem itself follows from the induction in the proof, not from finite enumeration.
proved_step:
statement: Copy-only transducer essential-variable bound. Let n,S≥0. A deterministic one-pass transducer has S state bits, fixed initial state, and updates in which each next state bit is a copy of an old state bit, a copy of the current input bit, or a constant. Its final output is any function of the final state. Then the recognized Boolean function on {0,1}^n depends on at most S input positions, so it has at most S essential variables.
proof: After reading any prefix, each state bit is either constant or equal to one input bit from that prefix. This holds initially because the initial state is fixed. It is preserved by every allowed update, since copying a state bit preserves its source and copying the current input bit adds only that input position. Therefore, after all n bits, the final state is determined by a set I of at most S input positions. The decoded output is a function only of the coordinates in I. If coordinate j is outside I, changing only x_j leaves the final state, and hence the output, unchanged. Thus every essential coordinate belongs to I and there are at most S.
scope: All n,S≥0; copy-only state updates with constants, fixed initial state, arbitrary final decoder. This is restricted to zero-gate updates and gives no lower bound for updates with AND/OR/NOT gates or for general streaming circuits.

Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, and let M be a deterministic layered transducer whose final decoder rejects inputs outside F and outputs x on each x in F. For layer t, put L_t=|{p in {0,1}^t: there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} with pu in F}|. Then M has at least L_t distinct states reached by live length-t prefixes. If L_t<2^t, M has at least L_t+1 states reached at layer t. Proof: For two distinct live prefixes p,q with unequal residual sets R_t(p)={u:pu∈F}, R_t(q), choose u in their symmetric difference. If both prefixes reached the same state, deterministic processing of u would give the same final decoder result, though exactly one of pu,qu belongs to F, contradiction. If their residual sets agree, choose u in their common nonempty residual. Then pu and qu are distinct accepted strings, but a shared state and common suffix produce the same final state, whose decoder cannot output both strings; contradiction. Thus live prefixes occupy pairwise distinct states. If a dead prefix r exists, choose any live p and u∈R_t(p); processing u from r must reject while from p it accepts, so r and p cannot share a state. This proves the claimed count. The result is a state-count bound only; it places no lower bound on transition/update circuit size.

statement: Final-layer identity-output state bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. A deterministic one-pass transducer with fixed initial state, layer-dependent transitions, and final decoder that rejects inputs outside F and outputs x itself on every x in F must reach at least |F| + 1_{F != {0,1}^N} distinct states after N input bits. Proof: For distinct x,y in F, if their final states were equal, the fixed decoder applied to that state would have to output both x and y, impossible. Hence the |F| accepted inputs reach pairwise distinct final states. If z is outside F, its final state must differ from every accepted final state because the decoder rejects z but outputs each accepted input on the corresponding accepted state. Thus there is one additional state whenever F is a proper subset. If F is all of {0,1}^N, the first argument alone gives the bound. This uses only deterministic decoding and exact identity output; it imposes no circuit-size bound on transitions.
scope: All integers N>=0 and all nonempty F subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic one-pass transducers with fixed initial state, layer-dependent transitions, and final decoder that rejects outside F and outputs the complete input x for x in F. This is a final-layer state-count bound only; it gives no per-step update-circuit complexity bound.

statement: Residual transition lemma (finite languages, exact identity). Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, let 0<=t<N, let p be a binary word of length t, and define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For b in {0,1}, define the suffix derivative D_b(R)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R}. Then D_b(R_t(p))=R_{t+1}(pb). In particular, equality of two layer-t residuals is preserved by applying the same next input bit: R_t(p)=R_t(q) implies R_{t+1}(pb)=R_{t+1}(qb). Proof: For any v of length N-t-1, v belongs to D_b(R_t(p)) iff bv belongs to R_t(p), iff p(bv) belongs to F, iff (pb)v belongs to F, iff v belongs to R_{t+1}(pb). The final implication follows by substituting p and q into the identity.
scope: All finite binary languages and all valid t,p,b; this is the exact residual derivative identity and does not assert any bound on Boolean circuit size, state encoding width, or update cost.
evidence: Claimed step S0515 was not extended or used as a premise; this identity is proved directly by elementwise equivalence. It is a foundational lemma for the residual-state construction, but does not close the synthesis gap or establish P!=NP.

statement: Universal transition-circuit upper bound. For every integer S>=1, any deterministic layered streaming transition from an S-bit state and one input bit to an S-bit next state, with arbitrary behavior permitted on unreachable state/input pairs, has an AND/OR circuit of at most 2^(S+2)-4 + S(2^(S+1)-1) counted gates; NOTs and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. Proof: Extend the transition arbitrarily to a total Boolean map f:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S. The shared-prefix minterm construction in reviewed step S0513 uses at most 2^(d+1)-4+q(2^d-1) gates for any map {0,1}^d->{0,1}^q. Substituting d=S+1 and q=S yields the claimed bound. The extension agrees with the required transition on every reachable pair, so it is a valid implementation.
scope: All S>=1, deterministic layered one-bit streaming transitions, with AND/OR fan-in two, NOT/constants free, and unrestricted shared fan-out. This is an upper bound only; it gives no exact minimum and no lower bound for SC or affine families.

statement: For any F subset of {0,1}^N, let R_t be its distinct residual languages at layer t and K_t=|R_t|. In the one-hot encoding of these states, each symbol transition has a fan-in-two OR circuit with at most K_t gates (constants free).
proof: For each R in R_t and input bit b, define its child δ_b(R)={v:bv in R}. If R=R_t(p), then δ_b(R)=R_{t+1}(pb), so the child is in R_{t+1}. For every R' in R_{t+1}, output the OR of coordinates z_R for which δ_b(R)=R'. These fibers partition R_t. A fiber of size j takes max(j-1,0) binary OR gates, so the total is at most K_t. On the one-hot state for R, exactly the child coordinate is set, proving the transition is correct.
scope: Finite fixed-length binary languages, canonical layered residual states, one-hot encoding, fan-in-two OR gates, free constants and unrestricted fan-out. Upper bound only; no claim about arbitrary recodings or the Pareto frontier.

proved_step: statement: Exact-string-output state-count lemma. Let N>=0 and F be a subset of {0,1}^N. A deterministic layered transducer reads one bit per layer, rejects x outside F, and for x in F must output x itself at the final decoder. For each t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes p for which some suffix u of length N-t has pu in F. Then the minimum number of reachable states at layer t is L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t}. Proof: distinct live prefixes p,q cannot share a state. If their residual sets differ, choose u accepted after exactly one; the same continuation from a shared state gives the same final decoder output, contradicting acceptance versus rejection. If their residual sets agree, they are nonempty; choose any common accepted u. Then pu and qu are distinct accepted strings, but a shared state followed by u reaches one final state, which cannot output both strings. A dead prefix cannot share a state with a live prefix, since a suffix accepted after the live prefix would require rejection on the dead one. Thus at least L_t plus one state when any dead prefix exists. Conversely, use one state for each live prefix and one shared dead state if needed; on a bit, extend the represented prefix when it remains live, otherwise enter the dead state. At layer N decode each live state to its represented string and reject the dead state. This attains the bound independently at every layer.

statement: Witness-output residual state lower bound (repaired scope). Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and suppose a deterministic layered machine rejects inputs outside F and outputs on each input in F a witness that uniquely determines that input. At layer t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes with a completion in F. The machine has at least L_t + 1_{L_t < 2^t} reachable states at layer t.
proof: For distinct live prefixes p,q, if their residual completion sets differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference forces opposite accept/reject outcomes from the same state, impossible. If their residual sets agree, they share a completion u; then pu and qu are distinct accepted inputs. From the same state and same suffix the deterministic machine would output the same witness on both, contradicting that the witness uniquely determines its input. Thus live prefixes occupy distinct states. If a dead prefix shared a state with a live prefix, a suffix completing the live prefix would also accept the dead prefix, impossible. Hence, when any dead prefix exists, at least one additional state is needed.
scope: Finite binary languages and deterministic layered witness-output machines with fixed input length, where each accepted input has an output witness uniquely determining that input; applies to truth-table inputs when the output circuit computes that truth table. State count only; no update-gate lower bound.

statement: For every n>=3, the family A_n of truth tables of affine Boolean functions f(x)=a_0 XOR sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i, in lexicographic input order, has a deterministic one-pass streaming recognizer with a final witness decoder, S=n+2 state bits, and zero charged update gates. Proof: Store the first n+1 input bits of the stream in n+1 state coordinates, leaving the marker coordinate z=0 on live prefixes. While t<=n+1, each update copies prior coordinates and writes the next stream bit into the next sample coordinate; after t=n+1, retain the sample coordinates. Each update coordinate is therefore a wire or the new input bit. The values at inputs 0,e_1,...,e_n uniquely determine the affine coefficients, so at each layer t<=n+1 distinct live prefixes have distinct samples, and for t>n+1 distinct live prefixes correspond to distinct affine functions and thus distinct samples. For t>n+1, assign each dead prefix a state with z=1, disjoint from all live states. At t<=n+1 every prefix is live, since the first t evaluations are independent affine linear forms. At the end, the decoder reconstructs the affine function from the sample, compares its full table with the input, outputs its coefficients on a match, and rejects otherwise. Since n+2<2^n for n>=3, this is below the input length. This proves the affine zero-update-gate control construction only; it says nothing about SC_{n,s} or P versus NP.
scope: Every n>=3; affine Boolean truth tables of length 2^n in lexicographic order; deterministic layered transducer; S=n+2; fixed unrestricted final decoder; update coordinates restricted to wires/copies of old state or new input; dead-prefix separation where dead prefixes exist.
