statement: Distinct nontrivial output-coordinate functions force distinct gates. Let X be a finite input domain, and let z_1,...,z_q:X->{0,1} be the required output-coordinate functions of a multi-output Boolean circuit with fan-out allowed. Let B be the set of distinct functions among the z_i that are neither constants nor input-coordinate projections nor their negations. Any circuit over AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, with each nonconstant gate counted once and unrestricted fan-out, has at least |B| gates.
proof: Each required output coordinate is delivered by an input, a constant, or a gate output. For each distinct f in B, choose one output coordinate equal to f. Because f is neither a constant nor an input projection or its negation, that coordinate requires a gate computing f. A gate computes one Boolean function, so distinct functions in B require distinct gates. Therefore the circuit has at least |B| nonconstant gates.
scope: Any finite Boolean multi-output function with full truth-table semantics; basis AND/XOR/NOT/constants, fan-in two for AND and XOR, unrestricted fan-out, shared gates counted once.

statement: Support-size lower bound for a fixed total transition map. Let C be a fan-in-at-most-two Boolean circuit over AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, with unrestricted fan-out and g counted gates. If an output function of C depends essentially on k distinct primary input variables, then g >= k-1.
proof: Take the ancestor subcircuit of the output and remove constant sources and branches that do not lie on a path from an essential primary input to the output. The remaining graph contains the k essential inputs and h gates, is connected as an undirected graph, and has at most 2h edges because every gate has indegree at most two. A connected graph on h+k vertices has at least h+k-1 edges. Hence h+k-1 <= 2h, so h >= k-1. Since h <= g, g >= k-1. Unary NOT gates contribute at most one incoming edge, so the edge upper bound still holds.
scope: A fixed total Boolean output function computed by a fan-in-at-most-two circuit; AND/XOR binary gates, NOT unary gates, constants, unrestricted fan-out. The bound is on counted gates and depends on essential primary-input support; it does not optimize across SC encodings.

statement: Fixed-width residual-state characterization for layered membership machines. For F subset {0,1}^N, let w_t count distinct residuals R_t(p)={u:pu in F} over length-t prefixes. In deterministic layered membership machines with layer-dependent transitions and common S-bit state, the minimum S is ceil(log2 W), W=max_t w_t (taking log2(1)=0). Lower bound: distinct residuals at one layer differ on some suffix u; merging their prefixes would force identical acceptance after u, contradicting membership. Hence 2^S>=w_t for each t. Upper bound: injectively label each layer's residuals using W labels. On bit b, map residual R to D_b(R)={v:bv in R}; this is the next residual, so the transition is well-defined for reachable labels. Define transitions arbitrarily on unused labels. At layer N accept only residual {epsilon}. This machine recognizes F. The result characterizes state width, not AND/XOR update-circuit cost G_max.
scope: All finite binary languages F subset {0,1}^N; deterministic layered membership machines, layer-dependent transitions, shared fixed-width state register, no witness output.

statement: Reachable-residual update-circuit bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, and let K_t be the number of distinct nonempty residual sets R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} at layer t, for 0<=t<N. Encode the reachable residual states injectively in S bits at each layer, where S>=1 and every layer width fits in S bits. For each t<N, the transition on reachable states can be implemented by a fan-in-two AND/XOR circuit with free NOTs and constants and unrestricted fan-out using at most 4 S K_t gates. The circuit may be defined arbitrarily on unreachable state/input pairs.
proof: Fix t<N. There are h<=2K_t reachable state/input pairs. For each pair, construct its indicator minterm on the S state bits and input bit; this takes S AND gates per pair, and these minterms are mutually exclusive. For each of the S output bits, XOR the minterms whose pair transitions to a next-state code with that bit set. This costs at most h-1 XOR gates per output, hence at most hS additional gates. Total cost is at most 2hS<=4SK_t. Correctness follows because after prefix p and bit b the suffixes accepted are exactly {v:bv in R_t(p)}. No optimality claim is made.

statement: Repaired reachable-residual update-circuit bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For 0<=t<N, let K_t be the number of distinct nonempty residuals R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}:pu in F}. Suppose each layer's nonempty residuals are injectively encoded in S bits, S>=1, and whenever an empty residual is reachable after one input bit, it is assigned a separate rejecting code in the same S-bit space. Then the transition on reachable state/input pairs at layer t has a fan-in-two AND/XOR circuit of size at most 4 S K_t, with free NOTs/constants and unrestricted fan-out. The circuit may be arbitrary on unreachable pairs.
proof: There are h<=2K_t reachable state/input pairs. For each such pair, construct its indicator minterm over the S state bits and input bit using S AND gates; literals and constants are free. These indicators are mutually exclusive. For each of the S output coordinates, XOR the indicators whose pair transitions to a next-state code having that coordinate set. At most h indicators are selected, so at most h-1 XOR gates are needed per coordinate (zero or one selected indicator costs zero). The total is at most hS+hS=2hS<=4SK_t. The assigned rejecting code handles the empty derivative when it occurs; for every nonempty residual R and input b, the next residual is exactly {v:bv in R}.
scope: Finite deterministic layered membership machines over fixed-length binary strings; this is an update-circuit upper bound, not an optimality or lower-bound claim. The separate rejecting-code capacity condition is necessary when dead transitions occur.

statement: Zero-gate coordinate-projection lemma. In a layered transducer whose update circuits use AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, with NOTs and constants free, every zero-gate update outputs only constants or signed copies of its input coordinates. Starting from a constant initial state, after t input bits every state bit is a constant or a signed copy of one of the t prefix bits. Hence if the transducer distinguishes all live prefixes at layer t, its signed coordinate projection on those prefixes is injective.
proof: A circuit with zero non-constant gates has no computed intermediate values. Each output can therefore only be wired from an input, complemented by a free NOT, or set to a constant. This proves the one-step assertion. Initially every state coordinate is constant. Assume every state coordinate after t steps is a constant or a signed copy of one of the first t bits. At step t+1, each output is a constant or a signed copy of an old state coordinate or the new input bit, so the same property holds for t+1. Induction proves the state-coordinate description. If two live prefixes agree on every coordinate selected by the state, their state vectors are equal; thus any requirement to distinguish all live prefixes forces the signed coordinate projection to be injective.
scope: Zero-gate updates in the specified AND/XOR basis with free NOTs and constants; arbitrary deterministic layered transducers and all finite prefix lengths. Structural reduction only; no SC-specific projection result or optimality claim.

statement: For every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N and every prefix length t, the residual derivative maps the residual of prefix p after one input bit b to the residual of pb: R_{t+1}(pb)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R_t(p)}. Consequently the residual-class automaton has a well-defined deterministic transition at every layer.
proof: By definition, v belongs to the right-hand side exactly when bv belongs to R_t(p), which holds exactly when p(bv) belongs to F. This is equivalent to (pb)v belonging to F, hence to v belonging to R_{t+1}(pb). The transition depends only on the residual set, so equal residuals have equal derivatives.
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N, integers 0<=t<N, prefixes p of length t and bits b.

statement: Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, and let K_t be the number of distinct residual sets R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} at layer t. Put S=max(1, ceil(log2(max_t K_t))). There exists a deterministic layered membership machine for F with S state bits at every layer, a terminal decoder, and each layer update implementable by at most 2^(S+2)-4 + S(2^(S+1)-1) fan-in-two AND/XOR gates (free NOTs and constants, unrestricted fan-out). Proof: Encode each distinct residual at layer t injectively by an S-bit word. By the derivative identity, for each reachable code and input bit, the next residual depends only on that code and bit. Define the update map on those reachable input pairs accordingly and arbitrarily on all other (S+1)-bit inputs. Apply the shared-minterm construction: for d=S+1 inputs and q=S outputs it uses at most 2^(d+1)-4 + S(2^d-1) gates, which is the stated bound. The terminal decoder accepts exactly the code of residual {epsilon}; the residual construction recognizes F. This gives a constructive finite upper bound on G_max, but does not establish an optimal (S,G_max,D) point or a lower bound.
Scope: Every finite nonempty binary language F of fixed length N; fan-in-two AND/XOR basis, free NOTs/constants, unrestricted fan-out; terminal decoding cost D is not bounded here.

statement: For every N>=1 and fixed w in {0,1}^N, the singleton language {w} has a deterministic layered recognizer with one state bit and at most one AND gate per update. Initialize s=1; on input x_i set s'=s AND (x_i if w_i=1, otherwise NOT x_i). Inductively, after i bits s=1 iff the observed prefix equals w[1..i]. Hence the final state accepts exactly {w}. NOT and constants are free. This establishes an upper bound for singleton languages only; it does not determine G_max for SC_{n,s} or its controls.
proof: At i=0 the empty prefix matches. If the state after i-1 bits indicates precisely that the prior prefix matches w[1..i-1], AND with the literal testing x_i=w_i leaves state 1 exactly when both the prior prefix and this bit match. This is equality of length-i prefixes. Induction to N proves exact acceptance. Each update uses one AND gate.

proved_step: statement: For every N≥0 and sets A_1,…,A_N⊆{0,1}, the language F={x∈{0,1}^N: x_i∈A_i for all i} is recognized by a layered one-bit deterministic machine with q_0=1, update q_i=q_{i-1}∧[b_i∈A_i], and final acceptance iff q_N=1. Each update has AND/XOR/NOT circuit cost at most one AND gate (NOTs and constants are free). Proof: By induction on i, after reading prefix b_1…b_i, q_i=1 iff b_j∈A_j for every j≤i. The base i=0 holds vacuously since q_0=1. The update equation gives the induction step by conjunction with the condition b_i∈A_i. Thus q_N=1 exactly for words in F. If A_i={0}, the membership predicate is ¬b_i; if A_i={1}, it is b_i; if A_i={0,1}, it is 1; if A_i=∅, it is 0. Accordingly each update is q, q∧¬b, q∧b, or 0, realizable with at most one AND gate in the stated basis.

statement: For every N≥0 and 0≤t≤N, the maximum, over all languages F⊆{0,1}^N, of the number of distinct length-(N−t) residual sets R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pu∈F} as p ranges over {0,1}^t is exactly min(2^t,2^(2^(N−t))). Proof: There are 2^t prefixes and 2^(2^(N−t)) possible subsets of suffixes, so this is an upper bound. For attainability, choose k=min(2^t,2^(2^(N−t))) distinct subsets A_1,...,A_k of {0,1}^{N−t}, assign them to k distinct prefixes, and assign the empty set to all remaining prefixes. Define F as the set of concatenations pu for which u belongs to the subset assigned to p. The assigned residuals are exactly the chosen subsets together with possibly the empty set; choose the k subsets to include the empty set whenever k<2^t, or choose k distinct subsets when k=2^t. Thus the number of distinct residuals is k. This characterizes the extremal width of the canonical residual machine over all finite languages, but gives no transition-circuit lower bound for SC_{n,s}.

proved_step:
statement: If a layered transducer starts in a fixed state, has S bits, and every transition output is a constant or a literal of one state bit or the incoming bit, then after t updates each state bit is a constant or a literal of one of the t input bits. Therefore, if every length-t prefix is live and distinct live prefixes require distinct states, S>=t.
Proof: Induct on updates. Substitution of a constant or literal into a constant-or-literal transition preserves that form. Hence the S state bits together depend on at most S input positions. If S<t, one position is absent from every state bit; flipping it preserves the state, contradicting injectivity on all 2^t live prefixes.
Scope: Fixed initial state, literal/constant transitions, full live layer, SEARCH semantics. No positive gate lower bound for SC families or decoder bound follows.
scope: Finite layered transducers at a specified layer t.

statement: Bounded-gate support lemma. Let a layered transducer have S state bits, a fixed initial state, and at most G fan-in-two gates per update; NOTs and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. After t updates, each state bit depends on at most (G+1)^t input positions. Therefore, if every length-t prefix is live and live prefixes must have distinct states, then t <= S(G+1)^t.
Proof: An output of a circuit with g fan-in-two gates depends on at most g+1 distinct primary inputs: its ancestor circuit is connected, and adding each binary gate can introduce at most one new input leaf. Thus each next-state bit depends on at most G+1 previous state bits or the new input. At t=0 its support is empty. Inductively, its support after t updates is a union of at most G+1 earlier supports, each of size at most (G+1)^(t-1), so has size at most (G+1)^t. Across S coordinates, at most S(G+1)^t input positions affect the state. If this is less than t, some position affects no coordinate; flipping it leaves the state unchanged, contradicting injectivity on all 2^t live prefixes. Hence the necessary inequality.
Scope: Finite layered transducers under the stated gate basis, fixed initial state, and SEARCH injectivity on a full live layer. This weak bound does not establish a positive gate lower bound for SC instances or constrain decoder cost.
scope: All integers S>=1, G>=0, t>=1 in the stated finite transducer model.

statement: Corrected bounded-gate support lemma. Let a layered transducer start in a fixed state and use S state bits. Each update computes each next-state bit with a fan-in-two circuit containing at most G counted gates; NOTs and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. If A_t is the maximum, over state bits after t updates, of the number of input positions on which that bit depends, then for G>=1, A_t <= ((G+1)^t-1)/G. Consequently, if all 2^t length-t prefixes are live and must have distinct states, then t <= S*((G+1)^t-1)/G. For G=0, each state bit after t updates is a constant or a literal of one input bit, so injectivity requires S>=t.
Proof: A circuit with at most G binary gates has at most G+1 distinct primary inputs in the ancestor set of any output: tracing backward from that output gives a connected binary-gate graph, and each gate can add at most one new input leaf. Thus one next-state bit depends on at most G+1 prior state bits and the newly read bit. If each prior state bit depends on at most A_(t-1) input positions, the next bit depends on at most (G+1)A_(t-1)+1 positions. Since A_0=0, induction gives A_t <= 1+(G+1)+...+(G+1)^(t-1)=((G+1)^t-1)/G. Across S state bits, at most S*A_t positions can affect the state. If this is less than t, an input position is absent from every state bit, so flipping that position preserves the state, contradicting injectivity over all 2^t prefixes. For G=0, every output is a constant or a literal of one state bit or the new input; induction shows each final coordinate is a constant or a literal of one input position, and the same absent-position argument gives S>=t.
Scope: Finite layered transducers in the stated circuit basis, fixed initial state, and SEARCH injectivity on a full live layer. This necessary condition does not establish a positive gate lower bound for SC instances or constrain decoder cost.
scope: All integers S>=1, G>=0, t>=1 in the stated finite transducer model.

statement: Let F be a proper subset of {0,1}^N. A deterministic streaming transducer that, after reading each length-N word, outputs a circuit computing that word when it belongs to F and rejects otherwise must have at least |F|+1 distinct final states. Thus if its state has S bits, 2^S >= |F|+1.
proof: For each f in F, let q_f be the final state reached on input f. If distinct f,g in F reached the same state, the deterministic decoder would return the same circuit on both inputs. A circuit computes one fixed truth table, so it cannot be a valid witness for both distinct tables; contradiction. Since F is proper, choose h outside F. If h reached q_f for some f in F, the decoder would have to both output a valid witness and reject on that same state; contradiction. Therefore the |F| states q_f are pairwise distinct and are distinct from the state reached on h, giving at least |F|+1 states. An S-bit state space has at most 2^S states.
scope: Finite truth-table witness-output transducers with deterministic final decoder, correct on every length-N input, and F a proper subset of all length-N Boolean tables. This is a necessary final-state bound only; it gives no transition-gate or decoder-size bound.
evidence: Direct argument; no experiment is needed for the general statement. The cited finite recount cm-3dbdfac4ac3547a7 checks |SC_{3,1}|=38 only and is not used as proof.

statement: Let A be a deterministic layered transducer whose output depends only on its final state. If equal-length prefixes p and q reach the same state, then for every suffix z such that both pz and qz are accepted, their valid-witness sets intersect.
proof: Starting from the same state and processing the same suffix follows identical transitions, so both completed inputs reach the same final state. The final-state-only decoder returns the same output w for each. Soundness on both accepted inputs implies w is a valid witness for both, so the two valid-witness sets intersect.
scope: Finite deterministic layered search transducers with final-state-only decoding and sound outputs on accepted inputs. This qualitative criterion alone gives no SC_{n,s} state or update-cost lower bound.

statement: Let F be a finite search language with a deterministic layered transducer and a final-state-only sound decoder. At cut t, form a graph H_t whose vertices are accepted length-t prefixes; join p and q if some common suffix z makes both pz and qz accepted and their valid-witness sets disjoint. Then the number of states used at layer t is at least chi(H_t).
proof: For any edge {p,q}, choose its witnessing suffix z. If p and q reached the same state at layer t, determinism implies that after reading z they reach the same final state. The decoder then returns the same output w on pz and qz. Soundness makes w a valid witness for both accepted completions, contradicting that their valid-witness sets are disjoint. Hence every edge has endpoints assigned distinct layer-t states. The state assignment is a proper coloring of H_t, so the layer uses at least chi(H_t) states.
scope: Any finite search language and deterministic layered transducer with final-state-only decoding, sound on every accepted input. This is conditional on H_t; it gives no numerical lower bound for SC_{n,s} until H_t is computed or bounded there.

statement: Let F be a finite search language with accepted length-t prefix set P_t and a sound deterministic layered transducer with a final-state-only decoder. Suppose that for every distinct p,q in P_t there is a suffix z such that both pz and qz are accepted and W(pz) intersect W(qz) is empty. Then the transducer has at least |P_t| states at layer t.
proof: Take distinct p,q in P_t and choose the suffix guaranteed by the hypothesis. If p and q reached the same layer-t state, deterministic processing of the identical suffix would lead to the same final state. The decoder would return one output w on both completions. Soundness requires w to belong to both valid-witness sets, contradicting their empty intersection. Thus distinct prefixes reach distinct states, so there are at least |P_t| states at layer t.
scope: Finite search languages with deterministic layered transitions, a final-state-only decoder, and sound outputs on accepted inputs. The pairwise suffix condition is a hypothesis; this does not assert it for SC_{n,s} or imply an update-gate lower bound.

statement: Residual automaton construction. Let N>=0 and F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For 0<=t<=N and each prefix p in {0,1}^t, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}; let K_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p). There is a layered deterministic membership transducer with exactly K_t states at layer t, transition delta_t(R,b)={u in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bu in R}, and an accepting decoder at layer N, hence at most ceil(log2(max_t K_t)) state bits. Proof: The transition is well-defined on every residual R at layer t: it depends only on R and b, and its result is a residual at layer t+1, since if R=R_t(p), then {u:bu in R_t(p)}=R_{t+1}(pb). Thus equal residuals transition to equal residuals. Starting from R_0(empty)=F, induction on t shows the state after prefix p is R_t(p). At t=N each residual is either {empty} or empty, and it is {empty} exactly when p in F; decode accordingly. Encoding the K_t residuals injectively as bit strings gives the asserted state-bit bound. The empty residual is a single rejecting state at each layer whenever it occurs, and its transitions remain empty.
scope: Finite nonempty membership languages F subset {0,1}^N, N>=0; arbitrary layered transition maps with no circuit-size restriction. This is a membership result only, not a witness-output SEARCH construction and not an update-circuit lower bound.

statement: For every nonempty F subset {0,1}^N, at each layer t let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes extendible to F and let delta_t be 1 iff at least one length-t prefix is not extendible to F. The minimum number of bits needed to assign distinct codes to every live prefix and, when delta_t=1, a separate common code to all dead prefixes is ceil(log2(L_t+delta_t)); hence all layers admit such assignments with S=max_t ceil(log2(L_t+delta_t)) bits.
proof: There are exactly L_t required live codes and, iff delta_t=1, one further code for the dead class. Thus the number of required codes is L_t+delta_t. s bits supply exactly 2^s codes, so feasibility is equivalent to 2^s>=L_t+delta_t, whose least integer solution is ceil(log2(L_t+delta_t)). Choosing codes independently at each layer and taking the maximum width proves the simultaneous layered assignment.
scope: Finite membership languages F subset {0,1}^N, N>=1, with live prefixes distinguished individually and all dead prefixes merged when present. This is a state-capacity lemma only; it does not bound transition gate count or decoder size.

statement: Sparse reachable-row extension lemma. Let d,q>=1 and let R be a specified subset of {0,1}^d of size r. Let g:R->{0,1}^q be any partial Boolean map. In the fan-in-two AND/OR basis with free NOT and constants and unrestricted fan-out, g has a total extension circuit of size at most r(d-1)+q max(r-1,0), with size 0 when r=0. Proof: For each a in R construct its exact minterm m_a(x)=AND_{i=1}^d (x_i if a_i=1 else NOT x_i) using a binary AND tree with d-1 gates (for d=1 this is a literal and uses 0). For output j, OR the minterms m_a with g(a)_j=1; if there are k_j such rows, this uses max(k_j-1,0) OR gates when k_j>0, and the empty OR is the free constant 0. Since k_j<=r, summing over j costs at most q max(r-1,0). For x in R exactly one minterm is true, so every output equals g(x); outside R the circuit simply chooses the all-zero extension. The stated gate bound follows. For r=0 the empty-domain map extends to the zero constant map. This is an upper bound for partial maps; it says nothing about a minimum circuit size or lower bound.
scope: All finite d,q>=1, every specified partial map g on R subset {0,1}^d, fan-in-two AND/OR, free NOT/constants, unrestricted fan-out. For layered transducers, R must include every reachable state/input pair whose next state is constrained; the lemma does not itself supply a code or establish the witness-output condition.

statement: For F subset {0,1}^N, let R_t(p)={u:pu in F} for each length-t prefix p, and let K_t be the number of distinct residuals. Every deterministic layered membership transducer recognizing F has at least K_t reachable states at layer t.
proof: If two prefixes p,q reach the same layer-t state, then for every suffix u the deterministic continuation from that state on u is identical. Hence pu is accepted iff qu is accepted, so R_t(p)=R_t(q). Distinct residuals therefore require distinct states, giving at least K_t states.
scope: Finite membership recognition languages F subset {0,1}^N; this does not bound update gates or decoder cost and does not establish witness-output complexity.

gap: This gives a decoder-independent state lower bound when suffix witness sets are disjoint, but does not yet exhibit a nontrivial packing for SC_{n,s} or bound update gate cost G_max at fixed (S,D).
proved_step: Let W be a witness relation on length-N inputs with witness universe Y. In a deterministic one-pass transducer with a common final decoder, if length-t prefixes p and q reach the same state, then for every suffix u of length N-t the decoder output belongs to W(pu) intersect W(qu). Therefore, if each pair in a set P of prefixes has at least one suffix u for which those two witness sets are disjoint, all prefixes in P have distinct states, requiring at least |P| reachable states (ceil(log2 |P|) state bits). Proof: equal states followed by the same suffix yield equal terminal states by determinism; the common decoder returns the same y, and correctness places y in both witness sets. Empty intersection contradicts this. Pairwise application gives injectivity on P.

gap: The continuation-separation lemma is only CLAIMED and its application currently has exploratory finite evidence. Need independent review of the generic lemma; determine whether any nontrivial witness-output packing can improve on the binding live-prefix bound for SC_{3,1}, then address fixed-(S,D) update-gate minima. The attempted t=4 packing has size 11, below the required 17 states from 16 live prefixes plus dead separation.
evidence: cm-fc2413c67c204afb reported packing sizes 1,2,3,4,11,8,4,2,1 for SC_{3,1}; this is exploratory and no packing certificate was emitted.

proved_step: statement: Final-state witness counting bound. Let F be a set of M distinct valid truth tables, and suppose a deterministic streaming transducer reads each full truth table and then a deterministic decoder outputs a witness that correctly represents that table. Then the transducer has at least M distinct final states on inputs from F, and therefore at least ceil(log2 M) state bits. Proof: If two distinct tables f,g in F reached the same final state, the deterministic decoder would return the same witness w on both inputs. Correctness requires w to represent f and also g, impossible because f != g. Thus the map from F to final states is injective. A machine with S bits has at most 2^S states, so 2^S >= M and S >= ceil(log2 M). Scope: fixed-length inputs, deterministic transitions, deterministic decoder, and a witness whose correctness identifies the represented truth table. This is a state lower bound only; it gives no per-step gate lower bound and no P != NP consequence.

statement: For every deterministic binary transition system on r>=1 states, its one-hot next-state map is computable with at most 4r-1 fan-in-two AND/OR gates, with NOT gates and fan-out free.
derivation: For each state q form u_{q,0}=x_q AND NOT a and u_{q,1}=x_q AND a, using 2r AND gates. For each destination j, OR exactly those u_{q,b} for which delta(q,b)=j. The 2r terms are partitioned among destination groups, so all nonempty groups need at most 2r-1 fan-in-two OR gates. On a valid one-hot input exactly the term for the current state and input symbol is true, hence the outputs encode its deterministic destination. Total at most 4r-1 gates.

statement: Zero-gate coordinate lemma. Let a deterministic layered transducer start in a fixed state and have S state bits. Suppose every transition output is computed with zero counted gates in the basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants, where NOT and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. Then after reading any prefix x_1...x_t, each state bit is either constant or a literal x_i or ¬x_i for some i≤t. Proof: With zero counted gates, an output wire can only be a constant, a state/input wire, or its free negation; AND and XOR outputs would each require a counted gate. Thus each next-state coordinate is constant or a literal of one current-state or current-input coordinate. Induct on t. At t=0 every state coordinate is constant because the initial state is fixed. If the claim holds at t, substituting those constant-or-literal expressions into each zero-gate transition coordinate yields a constant or a literal of one among x_1...x_t and x_{t+1}; negating a literal only changes its sign. This proves the claim for t+1.
scope: Deterministic layered transducers with fixed initial state, arbitrary time-dependent transitions, S state bits, and zero counted AND/XOR gates per transition; NOT/constants and fan-out are free. The lemma does not characterize positive-gate transitions or establish a lower bound for SC_{n,s}.
barrier_diagnostic: Relativizing: no oracle argument. Natural: no circuit lower-bound measure is claimed. Algebrizing: no algebraic oracle argument. Localizing: no proof-complexity localization argument.

statement: Let N>=1 and F subset {0,1}^N. Say F depends on coordinate i if there are two strings differing only at i with exactly one in F. Suppose F depends on every coordinate. Any deterministic layered transducer with a fixed initial state, S state bits, and zero counted AND/XOR gates in every transition in the basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants (NOT/constants free; unrestricted fan-out) that decides membership in F, using an arbitrary fixed final decoder, must have S>=N. Proof: A zero-counted-gate transition output is a constant or a wire or its negation: any nonconstant AND or XOR requires a counted gate. Inductively, after t input bits, every state coordinate is constant or a literal of one of x_1,...,x_t. At t=0 this holds because the initial state is fixed. At t+1, each next-state coordinate copies or negates one current state/input coordinate or is constant; substituting the induction hypothesis shows it is constant or a literal of one of x_1,...,x_{t+1}. At t=N, the state therefore depends on at most S distinct input coordinates. If S<N, choose coordinate i absent from all state bits. The final state, and hence its fixed decoder output, is identical on any pair differing only at i. This contradicts that F depends on i. Thus S>=N.
scope: Zero-gate membership transducers only; arbitrary layered wiring, fixed initial state and arbitrary final decoder. This does not establish coordinate-essentiality of SC_{n,s}, the witness-output version, or any positive-gate lower bound.
barrier_diagnostic: Relativizing: no oracle argument. Natural: no circuit lower-bound measure claimed. Algebrizing: no algebraic oracle argument. Localizing: no proof-complexity localization argument.

statement: Decision-residual width theorem. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each prefix p of length t define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu is in F}, and let K_t be the number of distinct such residuals. Every deterministic layered transducer deciding membership in F exactly must assign different states to prefixes with different residuals, and therefore needs at least K_t states at level t. Conversely, one state per distinct residual suffices: on input bit b, update residual R to R'={u: bu is in R}; this is well-defined because R is the residual of the current prefix, and the resulting state is the residual of the extended prefix. At level N, the decoder accepts exactly the residual {empty}. Thus K_t is the exact minimum state count at level t for DECISION semantics. Proof of the lower bound: if R_t(p) and R_t(p') differ, select a suffix u in their symmetric difference. Starting from the same state and reading u must produce the same final decision, contradicting that exactly one of pu and p'u belongs to F. The construction proves the upper bound by induction on prefix length.
scope: All finite F subset {0,1}^N and deterministic layered membership transducers with arbitrary transitions and final Boolean decoder. This establishes the exact state-width characterization for DECISION only; it does not address SEARCH witness-output semantics, gate count G, or decoder cost D.

statement: Residual derivative-pair identity. Let N>=0 and F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each 0<=t<=N and p in {0,1}^t define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu is in F}, and let K_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p). For every t<N, K_t equals the number of distinct ordered pairs (R_{t+1}(p0),R_{t+1}(p1)) as p ranges over {0,1}^t; hence K_t<=K_{t+1}^2.
proof: For any p of length t, each suffix in R_t(p) has a first bit b and remaining suffix v, and pv is in F exactly when v is in R_{t+1}(pb). Therefore R_t(p) is the disjoint union {0v:v in R_{t+1}(p0)} and {1v:v in R_{t+1}(p1)}. The ordered child pair determines R_t(p) by this union. Conversely, from R_t(p), the first-bit-0 suffixes with their first bit removed recover R_{t+1}(p0), and the first-bit-1 suffixes recover R_{t+1}(p1). Thus two parent residuals are equal iff their ordered child pairs agree, yielding the identity after counting distinct values. There are at most K_{t+1}^2 ordered pairs, proving the inequality.
scope: All finite Boolean languages F subset {0,1}^N, N>=0; all 0<=t<N. This concerns only the canonical residual quotient; it implies no circuit update-cost lower bound under arbitrary recodings and no fixed-(S,D) Pareto result.

statement: For finite F subset {0,1}^N in a fixed order, let R_t be its distinct residual languages and K_t=|R_t|. The canonical residual automaton has a one-hot encoding of width K_t. Its layer-t transition has an AND/OR circuit with free NOTs/constants, fan-in two and unrestricted fan-out, of size at most 4K_t+K_{t+1}. Proof: for each bit b and target r', OR the source coordinates in the fiber delta_b^{-1}(r'); the fibers partition R_t, so this costs at most K_t per bit. AND each bit-specific indicator with its input literal (at most 2K_t gates), then OR the two cases for each target (at most K_{t+1}). Equal residuals have equal children, so this implements the transition on every valid one-hot state.

statement: Let k≥0 and let f:{0,1}^d→{0,1} be f(x)=b⊕⊕_{i∈I}x_i, where |I|=k. In the circuit basis consisting of fan-in-two XOR gates, free NOT gates and constants, and unrestricted fan-out, the minimum number of counted XOR gates computing f on the full domain is max(k−1,0).
proof: If k≤1, f is a constant, an input, or its free negation, so its cost is zero. If k≥2, a chain of k−1 XOR gates computes the parity, with a free NOT if b=1. For the lower bound, consider the XOR gates in the output’s dependency graph and initially regard each distinct input variable x_i, i∈I, as a separate component. A binary XOR gate can join at most two components, so reducing k separate input components to one output component requires at least k−1 joining gates. Gates whose inputs are already in the same component, and NOTs or constants, cannot join components. Since the output depends on every variable in I, all k input components must be joined in its dependency graph. Thus at least k−1 XOR gates are required.
scope: One full-domain affine Boolean output; XOR-only counted gates, with free NOTs and constants. This does not cover AND gates, multi-output sharing, or arbitrary state recodings.

statement: For every N>=0, F subset {0,1}^N, and layer t, the minimum state count of a deterministic layered membership transducer recognizing F equals the number K_t of distinct residual sets R_t(p)={u:pu in F} among length-t prefixes.
proof: If two prefixes reach one state, determinism gives the same final state after every common suffix, so the decoder agrees and their residual sets are equal; hence at least K_t states are necessary. Conversely assign one state per residual set. On bit b, transition R_t(p) to its section {v:bv in R_t(p)}; this is well-defined since equal sets have equal sections. At layer N accept residual {epsilon} and reject the empty residual. This recognizes F using exactly K_t states.
scope: Finite deterministic layered membership transducers only; no update-gate bound or witness-output claim.

statement: Finite relation witness transducer with explicit Pareto coordinates. Let N>=2, r>=0, and R be any subset of {0,1}^N x {0,1}^r. There is a deterministic length-N transducer with N state bits, zero counted update gates, and a final decoder with at most 2^(N+1)-4+(r+1)(2^N-1) fan-in-two AND/OR gates (NOTs, constants, and fan-out free), which on input x outputs the lexicographically least y such that (x,y) is in R, or outputs a distinguished invalid flag if no such y exists.
proof: Use state q in {0,1}^N initialized to 0^N. On input b update q=(q_2,...,q_N,b), wiring existing state lines and b directly, so the update has zero counted gates. After reading t bits, q consists of N-t zeros followed by the t-bit prefix read so far; induction on t proves this invariant. Thus after N bits q=x. Define decoder outputs h_1(x),...,h_r(x) as the bits of the lexicographically least y with (x,y) in R, taking y=0^r when no witness exists, and define h_0(x)=1 exactly when at least one witness exists. These are Boolean functions on the finite domain. For all 2^N assignments x, construct every full-assignment minterm by building all signed prefix conjunctions of lengths 2 through N: at length k there are 2^k conjunctions, each formed with one AND gate from its length-(k-1) prefix and the next signed literal. This costs sum_{k=2}^N 2^k=2^(N+1)-4 gates. For each of the r+1 decoder outputs, OR the minterms on which it is 1 using at most 2^N-1 binary OR gates; use constant 0 or 1 for the empty or full set. The total decoder size is at most 2^(N+1)-4+(r+1)(2^N-1). The outputs have the stated semantics by their definition.
scope: Finite relation witness-output streaming only; S=N is explicitly the trivial-width regime in the Lemma M specification. This does not establish any S<N point or the SC_{n,s} fixed-(S,D) Pareto frontier.

statement: Common-completion incompatibility lemma. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and consider a deterministic length-N streaming machine whose transition at each layer is a function of its current state and next input bit, and whose final decoder outputs a valid witness for every x in F such that the witness uniquely determines x (for example, a circuit with truth table x), while correctly rejecting x outside F. For 0<=t<=N, form a graph H_t with vertex set P_t={p in {0,1}^t : p extends to an element of F}; join distinct p,p' when there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} such that pu and p'u both belong to F. Then every correct machine assigns different layer-t states to the endpoints of every edge of H_t. Consequently it uses at least chi(H_t) distinct states at layer t and at least ceil(log2 chi(H_t)) state bits.
Proof: Suppose adjacent p,p' receive the same state at layer t. By the edge definition choose a common suffix u with pu,p'u in F. Starting from equal states and feeding the same suffix u, determinism implies by induction over its bits that both computations reach the same final state. The final decoder therefore outputs the same witness on pu and p'u. But p != p', so pu != p'u; the witness uniquely determines the input truth table, and hence cannot be valid for both. This contradicts correctness. Thus adjacent vertices have different states; the state assignment is a proper coloring of H_t, so the number of available states is at least chi(H_t), yielding the bit bound.
Scope: Arbitrary finite F, arbitrary state recoding, layer-dependent transitions, and any uniquely identifying witness semantics. This is a state-width lower bound only; it gives no update-gate or decoder-cost lower bound and does not by itself establish a nontrivial value for SC_{n,s}.

statement: For every N>=1 and every F subset {0,1}^N, a layered deterministic membership transducer can store each length-t prefix literally in an N-bit state, update with zero counted gates in the fan-in-two basis with free wires/constants, and accept exactly F using a final decoder.
proof: At layer t, encode p in the first t state coordinates and set the remaining coordinates to 0. On input b, the next state is (p_1,...,p_t,b,0,...,0), which is obtained by wiring old coordinates 1 through t and the input b to the corresponding output coordinates; no counted gate is used. Distinct prefixes at a layer have distinct encodings, so all live prefixes are distinct and every dead prefix is distinct from them, satisfying full SEARCH separation. At layer N the state is exactly the input word, so a decoder whose accepting states are the words in F recognizes F. The construction uses S=N bits and has G_max=0. This is the trivial S>=N regime and makes no claim about the binding S<N frontier.
scope: All N>=1 and F subset {0,1}^N; state width S=N; layered transitions; free wires/constants; final decoder unrestricted. This is only a zero-update-gate upper bound.

gap: This gives the exact state-capacity component of the live/dead prefix separation problem: the relevant layer count is the number of distinct residual continuation sets, not the number of live prefixes plus one. It does not resolve the remaining transition-gate minimization or the required family/control G_max comparison.
proved_step:
statement: Exact residual-state characterization. Let N>=0, F subset {0,1}^N, and for each t and p in {0,1}^t define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}; let K_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p). In a deterministic layered membership transducer whose acceptance after N bits depends only on its state, the minimum number of states available at layer t sufficient to recognize F is exactly K_t. Consequently the minimum uniform state-bit count is ceil(log2(max_t K_t)), with log2(1)=0.
proof: Lower bound: if p,p' reach the same state at layer t, then determinism implies that for every suffix u of length N-t, the transducer has the same acceptance result after reading u from that state. Hence pu is in F iff p'u is in F for every u, so R_t(p)=R_t(p'). Distinct residual sets therefore require distinct layer-t states, giving at least K_t states. Upper bound: assign one state to each distinct residual set at each layer. For a residual R at layer t and bit b, define the next state to be R'={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R}; this is the residual of any prefix p with R_t(p)=R after appending b, so the transition is well-defined independent of the representative p. At layer N, residuals are either {epsilon} or the empty set; accept precisely the state {epsilon}. Induction on the number of input bits shows the state reached after prefix p represents exactly R_t(p), proving recognition of F. Thus K_t states suffice at each layer. A uniform state register can encode the largest layer's state set, requiring exactly ceil(log2(max_t K_t)) bits, and the lower bound applies at a layer attaining the maximum.
scope: Finite Boolean membership languages of fixed length N, deterministic layered transitions allowed to vary by t, acceptance determined by the terminal state. No restriction or bound on transition circuit size; this does not determine G_max for SC_{n,s}.

statement: Singleton-language recognizer bound. For every integer N>=2 and word w in {0,1}^N, the language F={w} is recognized by a deterministic layered transducer with one state bit and at most one counted fan-in-two AND gate per update, when NOTs and constants are free. Initialize q=1. At step t, set q'=q AND x if w_t=1, and q'=q AND NOT(x) if w_t=0. Accept iff the final state is 1. Proof: After t updates, induction gives q=1 exactly when the input prefix of length t equals the prefix of w: this holds initially for the empty prefix; the update preserves 1 exactly when the next input bit agrees with w_t, and once q=0 it remains 0. Thus the final state is 1 exactly on input w. Each update uses one AND gate, with the required literal supplied using the free NOT operation. Since N>=2, the state-bit count S=1 satisfies S<N. This is an update upper bound for singleton membership languages only; it does not prove minimality or the SC witness-output requirement.
scope: All N>=2 and all singleton binary languages of fixed length N; layered transitions; one state bit; counted fan-in-two AND gates with free NOT/constants. Not a lower bound, exact G_max result, SC witness-output result, or P-vs-NP progress.

statement: Residual-language characterization of layer state width. Let N≥0 and F⊆{0,1}^N. For 0≤t≤N and p∈{0,1}^t, define R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pu∈F}, and let K_t be the number of distinct such residual sets. Among deterministic layered membership transducers that decide F on every length-N word, the minimum number of reachable states at layer t is exactly K_t; equivalently the minimum state-bit width there is ⌈log₂K_t⌉ (with width 0 when K_t=1).
proof: If two prefixes reach the same layer-t state, every suffix induces identical subsequent computation, so correctness implies their residual sets are equal. Thus distinct residuals require distinct states. Conversely, represent each prefix by its residual R. On input b, transition to R_b={u:bu∈R}, which depends only on R, not on the prefix realizing it. Initialize with F. At layer N, residuals are either {ε} or ∅; accept exactly {ε}. Induction shows the state after p is R_t(p), using exactly K_t reachable states. Injectively coding them requires ⌈log₂K_t⌉ bits. This is decision-only and establishes no update-circuit, decoder-cost, or witness-output bound.
scope: All finite languages F⊆{0,1}^N, every layer t, deterministic layered transducers correct on every length-N input; exact reachable-state minimum per layer.

statement: Residual-language state lower bound (decision variant). Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and for each length-t prefix p define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. In any deterministic layered streaming machine that decides membership in F, if two prefixes p,p' reach the same state at layer t, then R_t(p)=R_t(p'). Consequently the machine needs at least K_t distinct layer-t states, where K_t=|{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|, and at least ceil(log2 K_t) state bits.
proof: Suppose p and p' reach the same state q at layer t. For any suffix u of length N-t, determinism and identical transition maps imply that processing u from q yields the same final state in both runs. The final decoder therefore gives the same accept/reject answer on pu and p'u. Since this holds for every u, pu is in F iff p'u is in F for every suffix u, so R_t(p)=R_t(p'). Thus distinct residual sets require distinct states, giving at least K_t states; S bits encode at most 2^S states, so S>=ceil(log2 K_t).

evidence: The statement and scope give incompatible gate-count conventions: the scope includes counted NOT gates, but the bound counts only XOR gates and the proof treats NOT as free. Under the counted-NOT reading, the one-bit affine map F(x)=NOT x (d=q=1, I={1}, b=1) has claimed upper bound max(1-1,0)=0 although it requires a NOT gate. The construction is valid if NOT is explicitly free; alternatively, if NOT is counted, the bound must include the cost of outputs with b_j=1 (or an equivalent accounting).

proved_step: Repaired affine transition construction. Let d,q>=1 and F:{0,1}^d->{0,1}^q have coordinates F_j(x)=b_j XOR (XOR_{i in I_j} x_i), where b_j in {0,1} and I_j subseteq {1,...,d}. In the basis with fan-in-two XOR gates counted, NOT gates counted, and constants and input wires free, F has a circuit of size at most sum_{j=1}^q (max(|I_j|-1,0) + b_j). Proof: For each output j with k=|I_j|=0, output the free constant b_j, costing zero; the displayed summand is b_j in this case, so this bound remains valid. For k>=1, compute the parity of the k selected inputs with a binary XOR chain using k-1 XOR gates. If b_j=0, this is the output. If b_j=1, apply one NOT gate. Thus the cost for this output is k-1+b_j, equal to its summand. Constructing these circuits separately for all q outputs and summing their costs proves the bound; input sharing is free and can only reduce cost. In particular, size is at most q(d-1)+q. Scope: all affine Boolean maps over GF(2), in the explicitly stated basis. This repairs the prior claim's mismatch between a counted-NOT scope and a proof treating NOT as free; it is an upper bound only.

statement: Witness-output terminal state lower bound. Let I be a finite set of valid instances encoded by streams of a fixed length N, and let W be a finite set of correct witness strings. Suppose a deterministic streaming transducer processes the stream in order, ends in a state q in Q, and its fixed final decoder D:Q->{rejection} union W is correct on every valid and invalid stream. If two valid streams x,y encode instances whose sets of correct witnesses are disjoint, then their terminal states are distinct. Moreover, the terminal state of any invalid stream is distinct from that of every valid stream. Hence the number of terminal states is at least the number of pairwise witness-incompatible valid streams plus one when an invalid stream exists.
proof: If two streams end in the same state q, the fixed decoder returns the same value D(q) on both. Correctness requires D(q) to be a correct witness for each associated valid instance. If their correct-witness sets are disjoint, no such output exists, a contradiction; therefore their terminal states differ. For an invalid stream z, correctness requires D(q_z)=rejection. For a valid stream x, correctness requires D(q_x) in W, so q_z cannot equal q_x because D is a function. Counting these pairwise distinct terminal states proves the bound.
scope: Finite fixed-length streaming SEARCH transducers with deterministic transitions, a single fixed terminal decoder, and correctness on every valid and invalid stream; it gives a state lower bound only and no update-gate lower bound.

statement: Residual-separation lemma. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and let E_t map length-t prefixes to states in any deterministic exact membership transducer. If E_t(p)=E_t(q), then the residual sets R_t(p)={u:pu in F} and R_t(q)={u:qu in F} are equal. Hence every such transducer has at least K_t distinct reachable states at layer t, where K_t is the number of distinct residuals. Proof: If the residuals differed, choose a suffix u in their symmetric difference. Starting from equal states, determinism gives identical state sequences on the common suffix u, and the final decoder must give the same accept/reject result, contradicting that exactly one of pu, qu belongs to F. Therefore equal states imply equal residuals; distinct residuals require distinct states, giving the bound. Conversely, assigning one state per residual and transitioning R_t(p) on bit b to R_{t+1}(pb) is well-defined because R_t(p)=R_t(q) implies R_{t+1}(pb)=R_{t+1}(qb); final acceptance is whether the residual contains the empty suffix. Thus K_t states are sufficient as well. This gives an exact layer-by-layer state characterization, but no update-circuit cost bound.
scope: Finite F subset {0,1}^N; deterministic layered transducers with exact membership output; N>=0.
proof: As stated in the step; complete argument included.

statement: Adjacent residual-count lemma. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each 0<=t<=N, let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, and let K_t be the number of distinct residuals R_t(p) over prefixes p of length t. For every 0<=t<N, K_{t+1}<=2K_t and K_t<=K_{t+1}^2. Proof: For each residual R at layer t, its two derivatives R_0={u:0u in R} and R_1={u:1u in R} are layer-(t+1) residuals. Every layer-(t+1) residual arises as one of these derivatives from its parent prefix, so there are at most two children per distinct parent, proving K_{t+1}<=2K_t. Also R is exactly the disjoint-prefix union {0u:u in R_0} union {1u:u in R_1}; hence the ordered pair (R_0,R_1) uniquely determines R. Distinct layer-t residuals therefore give distinct ordered pairs of layer-(t+1) residuals. There are at most K_{t+1}^2 such pairs, proving K_t<=K_{t+1}^2.
scope: Finite languages F subset {0,1}^N; residuals are sets of suffixes at each fixed layer; all integers 0<=t<N. No circuit-cost conclusion.
proof: For any prefix p of length t, its two extensions p0 and p1 have residuals R_{t+1}(p0) and R_{t+1}(p1), which are respectively the 0- and 1-derivatives of R_t(p). This gives at most two child residuals per parent. Conversely, a residual R_t(p) is reconstructed uniquely as {0u:u in R_{t+1}(p0)} union {1u:u in R_{t+1}(p1)}. Therefore the map from distinct parent residuals to ordered pairs of child residuals is injective, yielding the square bound.

statement: Fixed-layer residual extremum is attainable. For integers N>=0 and 0<=t<=N, let F range over subsets of {0,1}^N, and let K_t(F) be the number of distinct sets R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, for p in {0,1}^t. Then max_F K_t(F)=min(2^t, 2^(2^(N-t))). Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so K_t(F)<=2^t. Each residual is a subset of a suffix universe of size 2^(N-t), so K_t(F)<=2^(2^(N-t)). Put k=min(2^t,2^(2^(N-t))). Choose k distinct subsets A_1,...,A_k of the suffix universe and assign them to k distinct prefixes. Assign the empty subset to any remaining prefixes. Define F to contain exactly the concatenations pu for which the suffix u belongs to the subset assigned to p. The residual of each selected prefix is its assigned A_i, hence these k prefixes have pairwise distinct residuals and K_t(F)>=k. The upper bound gives equality. This is an extremum for one fixed layer; it does not assert simultaneous attainment at all layers or bound transition cost.
scope: All finite Boolean languages of word length N, including N=0; every fixed layer t in [0,N]. Membership residuals only; no circuit or witness-output cost conclusion.

statement: Residual automaton theorem. Let N>=0 and F be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each t and prefix p in {0,1}^t define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, and let K_t be the number of distinct residual sets. There is a deterministic layered membership transducer with exactly K_t states at layer t, and no deterministic layered membership transducer can use fewer than K_t states at that layer. For every residual R at layer t<N and bit b, define delta_t(R,b)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R}. This is well-defined and equals R_{t+1}(pb) for any p with R_t(p)=R. Assign one state to each distinct residual and use delta_t as transition. At layer N accept precisely the state whose residual is {empty string}, if present; reject the empty residual. For the lower bound, prefixes with different residual sets cannot share a state, since a suffix in their symmetric difference must be accepted after one prefix and rejected after the other. Scope: finite deterministic layered membership transducers with unrestricted transition functions; no gate-cost or witness-output conclusion.
proof: For a residual R realized by prefix p, its transition on b must represent precisely the suffixes v for which pbv is in F, namely {v:bv in R}. This is independent of the chosen representative p. Induction on t shows that after reading p the state represents R_t(p). At t=N, the only possible residuals are empty and {empty string}; accepting exactly the latter recognizes F. Conversely, if prefixes with different residuals shared a state, determinism would give the same final decision on every common suffix. A suffix in the symmetric difference of the residuals must instead be accepted after one prefix and rejected after the other, a contradiction. Thus at least K_t states are necessary, and the construction attains the bound.

statement: SEARCH transducer construction with explicit transition and decoder bounds. Let F subset {0,1}^N, N>=1, and designate for each x in F a valid witness w(x) in {0,1}^r. At each layer t let L_t be the number of live length-t prefixes and d_t=1 iff a dead length-t prefix exists. Put S=max_t ceil(log2(L_t+d_t)). There is a deterministic layered transducer with S state bits, distinct states for all live prefixes at each layer, dead states disjoint from live states, acceptance exactly F and output w(x) on every x in F. In the AND, XOR, NOT, constant basis with shared gates and free fan-out, each transition has at most 2^(S+2)-4 + S(2^(S+1)-1) nonconstant gates, and the final decoder has at most 2^(S+1)-4 + r(2^S-1) nonconstant gates. Proof: At each layer injectively assign S-bit codes to live prefixes and, if dead prefixes exist, one further code disjoint from them; the definition of S guarantees enough codes. Define transitions on reachable live codes by mapping (code(p),b) to code(pb) when pb is live and to a dead code otherwise; map dead codes to dead codes, and define unused inputs arbitrarily. For any Boolean map on d input bits, build all full-assignment minterms using shared signed-prefix conjunctions, costing sum_{k=2}^d 2^k=2^(d+1)-4 AND gates. Each output is the XOR of its accepting minterms, costing at most 2^d-1 XOR gates. With d=S+1 and S outputs this gives the transition bound. At layer N, each live state identifies a unique x in F, so define the decoder there to output w(x) and reject on dead codes. Apply the same minterm construction on S bits with r outputs for the decoder bound. Induction on prefix length proves the assigned state invariant and hence acceptance and witness correctness for all inputs. Scope: finite F, N>=1, fixed designated r-bit witness per accepted word, layered deterministic transducers, injective live-prefix states, one disjoint dead state when needed, AND/XOR/NOT/constants, free fan-out. Constructive upper bound only; not an optimal Pareto result and not P-versus-NP progress.

statement: Residual distinguishability lower bound. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, and for each t in {0,...,N} and prefix p in {0,1}^t define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. Let K_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p). Any deterministic one-pass streaming membership machine that reads the bits in this fixed order, has a state set Q, and after reading t bits determines membership correctly for every length-N input, must satisfy |Q| >= K_t for every t. Consequently it needs at least ceil(log2(max_t K_t)) state bits (with zero bits allowed when the maximum is 1).
proof: Fix t and suppose two length-t prefixes p and p' reach the same machine state. Determinism implies that for every common suffix u of length N-t, the machine's subsequent state sequence and final output are identical when started from that state and fed u. Correctness says the final output on pu is 1 exactly when pu is in F, and likewise for p'u. Hence for every u, pu is in F iff p'u is in F, so R_t(p)=R_t(p'). Thus prefixes with different residual sets cannot share a state. There are K_t distinct residual sets, so at least K_t distinct states are reached after t bits, proving |Q|>=K_t. Taking the maximum over t and applying |Q|<=2^b to a machine with b state bits gives 2^b>=max_t K_t and therefore b>=ceil(log2(max_t K_t)).
scope: Finite deterministic streaming membership machines on fixed-order Boolean words of length N, with exact correctness on all 2^N inputs. This is a state-count lower bound only; it gives no transition gate lower bound and does not address witness-output machines unless their outputs determine membership.

proved_step: statement: For integers d>=2 and q>=1, let f:{0,1}^d->{0,1}^q be a Boolean map. With fan-in-two AND/OR gates, free NOTs and constants, and unrestricted fan-out, f has a circuit of size at most 2^(d+1)-4 + sum_{j=1}^q max(min(w_j,2^d-w_j)-1,0), where w_j is the number of inputs on which output j is 1. Proof: For every signed prefix of each length k=2,...,d, construct its conjunction from its length-(k-1) prefix and its next literal, using one AND gate. This uses sum_{k=2}^d 2^k=2^(d+1)-4 gates and constructs every full-assignment minterm. For output j, choose the smaller of its accepting and rejecting assignment sets, of size r=min(w_j,2^d-w_j). If r=0, output a constant or its free negation. Otherwise OR the r corresponding minterms using r-1 OR gates; negate the result for the rejecting set. This computes each output with max(r-1,0) gates. Summing the shared minterm cost and output costs gives the bound. Scope: finite Boolean maps in the stated basis; this is a constructive upper bound only.

statement: Residual quotient construction with explicit transition-circuit bound. Let N>=1 and F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For each t, define p~_t p' iff the suffix sets {u in {0,1}^{N-t}:pu in F} and {u:p'u in F} are equal, and let r_t be the number of equivalence classes. Set S=max_t ceil(log2 r_t), with ceil(log2 1)=0. Then F has a deterministic layered membership transducer using S state bits whose layer-t states encode exactly these residual classes. Each transition is computed by a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT, constants and unrestricted fan-out, of size at most 2^(S+2)-4 + S(2^(S+1)-1). Proof: For a class [p] at layer t and bit b, define delta_t([p],b)=[pb]. This is well-defined: if p~_t p', then for every suffix v of length N-t-1, pbv is accepted iff p'bv is accepted, so pb~_{t+1}p'b. Encode the r_t classes injectively in {0,1}^S; this is possible since r_t<=2^S. Define transitions arbitrarily on unused codes, yielding a total map from S+1 bits to S bits. For any such map on d=S+1 inputs, construct every signed prefix conjunction of lengths 2 through d with one AND gate per prefix, for a total of sum_{k=2}^d 2^k=2^(d+1)-4 gates; length-one signed literals are free. These include all 2^d full-assignment minterms. For each of S output bits, OR the minterms where it is 1 using at most 2^d-1 binary OR gates; constants handle empty or full sets. The total is 2^(d+1)-4+S(2^d-1), as claimed. Induction on prefix length shows the state after reading p is its residual class. At t=N, the residual class accepts exactly when its empty suffix belongs to F, so the machine recognizes F. Scope: finite nonempty Boolean languages with layered transitions and the stated circuit basis. This is a constructive upper bound only; it gives no lower bound on G_max and does not meet the separate SC witness-output experiment obligation.

statement: Sparse-domain minterm extension lemma. Let d,q>=1 and let g:D->{0,1}^q be a partial Boolean map with D subseteq {0,1}^d. For output j put A_j={x in D:g(x)_j=1}; let P(A_j) be the set of distinct signed prefixes x[1..k] for x in A_j and 2<=k<=d. There exists a total Boolean map extending g, with unspecified inputs mapped to 0^q, whose fan-in-two AND/OR circuits with free NOT/constants and unrestricted fan-out have total size at most sum_j(|P(A_j)|+max(|A_j|-1,0)).
proof: For each output j and each distinct signed prefix in P(A_j), compute its conjunction recursively, using one AND gate per prefix. Length-one literals are free. This costs |P(A_j)| gates and provides the length-d minterms for all x in A_j; when d=1, each minterm is a free literal. OR those minterms with max(|A_j|-1,0) binary OR gates, taking the empty OR to be constant 0. Distinct full minterms are true on distinct inputs, so on every z in D the resulting output is 1 exactly when z is in A_j, as required. If z is outside D, it is not in A_j, so every selected minterm is false there and the output is 0. Summing these costs over outputs proves the bound; sharing across outputs can only reduce the size.
scope: Finite partial maps on d Boolean input bits to q Boolean output bits; fan-in-two AND/OR, free NOT/constants, unrestricted fan-out. This is an upper bound only, not a minimum-cost result or a bound for a witness-output model without matching requirements.

statement: Residual equivalence exactly characterizes the minimum layer-state count for deterministic membership streaming. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N. For each 0<=t<=N and prefix p in {0,1}^t, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, and K_t=|{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|. Among deterministic layered transducers that read one bit per step and decide membership in F, the minimum number of states at layer t is exactly K_t, even when each transition map may depend on t. Proof: For the lower bound, if two prefixes p,q at layer t reach the same state, then for every suffix u the deterministic continuation from that state on u is identical, so the machine gives the same final decision on pu and qu. Correctness implies pu in F iff qu in F for every u, hence R_t(p)=R_t(q). Therefore distinct residual sets require distinct layer-t states. For the upper bound, use each distinct residual set R_t(p) as a state. Define the transition on bit b by R_t(p) -> R_{t+1}(pb). This is well-defined: if R_t(p)=R_t(q), then for every suffix v, v is in R_{t+1}(pb) iff bv is in R_t(p), iff bv is in R_t(q), iff v is in R_{t+1}(qb). At layer N, accept exactly when the sole empty suffix belongs to the residual set. Induction on the read prefix shows the machine is in state R_t(p), so this decoder decides F. Thus the minimum layer-t state count is K_t for every t, with a single family of transitions attaining all these minima simultaneously.
scope: Finite Boolean membership languages F subset {0,1}^N; deterministic layered machines with arbitrary time-dependent transitions and a final membership decoder. This concerns state count only; it does not establish transition circuit cost, witness-output correctness, or an asymptotic P-vs-NP consequence.

proved_step: statement: One-hot transition lemma. Let Q_t and Q_{t+1} be finite nonempty state sets of sizes q and r, and let δ:Q_t×{0,1}→Q_{t+1} be any total transition map. Encoding each state as its one-hot indicator vector, the next-layer one-hot vector is computed by a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free constants and unrestricted fan-out using at most 4q gates. Proof: For each u∈Q_t form the two edge indicators e_{u,0}=x_u∧¬b and e_{u,1}=x_u∧b, using 2q AND gates (NOT is free). For each v∈Q_{t+1}, output y_v as the OR of the edge indicators e_{u,b'} for which δ(u,b')=v. If there are d_v such indicators, this takes max(d_v−1,0) binary OR gates, with the empty case implemented by constant 0. Since δ is total, Σ_v d_v=2q, and therefore Σ_v max(d_v−1,0)≤2q. Total size is at most 4q. On every valid one-hot input x_u and arriving bit b, exactly the indicator for δ(u,b) is 1, so the outputs are exactly the next state's one-hot encoding. Scope: one transition layer of a finite deterministic automaton; this is an upper bound only, and does not cover witness-output decoding or prove an exact minimum for SC_{3,1}.
