For v in Q', let d_v=|{(u,b):delta(u,b)=v}|. Under one-hot encoding, with fan-in-two AND/OR gates, free NOT/constants, and unrestricted fan-out, the next one-hot vector is computable using at most 2q + sum_{v in Q'} max(d_v-1,0) gates. Proof: For each u form e_(u,0)=x_u AND NOT b and e_(u,1)=x_u AND b, using 2q AND gates. For each v, OR its d_v incoming indicators using max(d_v-1,0) gates; if d_v=0 output constant 0. On a valid one-hot input and either value of b, exactly one edge indicator is 1, so exactly the output coordinate indexed by delta(u,b) is 1. Summing gives the stated count. Since sum_v d_v=2q, this is at most 4q and is strictly smaller whenever some output coordinate has multiple incoming edges. This is a representation-dependent transition upper bound only; it does not determine the minimum over encodings or satisfy a search-witness decoder requirement.

statement: Residual-language state theorem. Let N>=0 and F⊆{0,1}^N. In any deterministic layered recognizer reading one bit per layer, prefixes p,q of length t that reach the same state must have equal residuals R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N-t}:pu∈F}. Conversely, there is a recognizer using exactly K_t states at layer t, where K_t is the number of distinct residuals. Proof: If p and q reach the same state, determinism makes every common continuation u have the same final acceptance outcome, so pu∈F iff qu∈F; hence their residuals are equal. For the converse, use one state per distinct residual. On bit b, transition R_t(p) to R_{t+1}(pb). This is well-defined: equality of R_t(p) and R_t(q) implies for every suffix v that bv∈R_t(p) iff bv∈R_t(q), hence v∈R_{t+1}(pb) iff v∈R_{t+1}(qb). At layer N, accept exactly the state whose residual is {empty}. This recognizes F with K_t states at each layer.
scope: All finite binary languages F⊆{0,1}^N, N≥0; deterministic layered membership recognition with arbitrary layer-dependent transitions and final decoder. State count only; no bound on transition circuit complexity.

statement: Zero-gate projection lemma. In a layered streaming transducer with fixed initial state, if every update uses zero counted gates in the basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants, and wires, then after t input bits each state coordinate is constant or a literal of one of those t input bits. Consequently, if live prefixes at layer t must have distinct states, some set of at most S input positions separates the live-prefix family by coordinate projection.
proof: At time zero every state coordinate is fixed, hence constant. With zero counted gates, each output coordinate of an update can only be a constant, a wire from a prior state coordinate or the new input bit, or the complement of one such wire. Inductively, if every coordinate at time t is constant or a signed copy of one of x_1,...,x_t, every coordinate at time t+1 is constant or a signed copy of one of x_1,...,x_{t+1}. Thus the state vector at layer t is determined by the set I_t of input positions used by its nonconstant coordinates. If two live prefixes agree on I_t, their states agree. Pairwise distinct live-prefix states therefore imply that restriction to I_t is injective on the live-prefix family.
scope: Finite layered streaming transducers with fixed initial state, zero counted gates in every update, free NOT/constants and wires, and pairwise distinct states for live prefixes at each layer. No claim about positive gate counts or a P-vs-NP lower bound.

gap: Need an exact and independently checked characterization of when the live-prefix coordinate-projection condition is sufficient for a valid zero-gate layered transducer in the binding SEARCH model, including simultaneous state-code consistency across layers and the witness-output decoder requirement. The requested SC_{3,1} exhaustive projection computation and full (S,G_max,D) Pareto measurements remain open.

evidence: Checked the constructive upper bound proof: (1) S = ceil(log2 M) with M = max_t(L_t+1) ensures enough codes for live prefixes + one dead code per layer. (2) Transition function at each layer is a Boolean map f_t: {0,1}^{S+1} -> {0,1}^S (S state bits + 1 input bit -> S next-state bits). (3) The minterm construction explicitly builds a circuit for ANY such map in the fan-in-2 AND/OR basis with free NOT/constants and unrestricted fan-out: sum_{k=2}^{S+1} 2^k = 2^{S+2}-4 AND gates to build all 2^{S+1} minterms incrementally, then at most 2^{S+1}-1 OR gates per output bit (S outputs) to OR the accepting minterms. Total gates = 2^{S+2}-4 + S(2^{S+1}-1). This is a standard constructive upper bound; the shared minterms across outputs are correctly counted once. No argument gap found. The claim is an upper bound (existence), not a lower bound, and the construction proves it for every finite F.

Checked the complement-minterm construction: (1) Builds all 2^d minterms using sum_{k=2}^d 2^k = 2^{d+1}-4 AND gates (length-1 literals free). (2) For each output j, picks the smaller of accepting/rejecting sets (size r = min(w_j, 2^d-w_j)). (3) ORs the r minterms with r-1 OR gates, adds free NOT if using rejecting set. Total: 2^{d+1}-4 + sum_j max(min(w_j,2^d-w_j)-1,0). This is a standard optimal construction for the given basis; the bound is tight for worst-case functions. No argument gap.

Checked the residual counting bound: K_t = number of distinct residual sets R_t(p) = {u: pu in F} for p in {0,1}^t. (1) At most 2^t prefixes, so K_t <= 2^t. (2) Each residual is a subset of {0,1}^{N-t} (size 2^{N-t}), so at most 2^{2^{N-t}} subsets. (3) K_t <= min(2^t, 2^{2^{N-t}}). Boundary cases: t=0 -> K_0=1; t=N -> K_N=2 for nonempty proper F, else 1. Correct counting argument; no gap.

Checked the distinct-output lower bound: r = number of distinct coordinate functions among F_1,...,F_q that are not 0, 1, or any primary input x_i. Each such function must be the signal of at least one gate node. Distinct functions cannot be computed by the same gate node (a node has exactly one output signal). Therefore we can inject the r distinct functions into counted gate nodes, giving at least r gates. This holds for any circuit with arbitrary sharing and output wiring over the stated basis. The argument is sound; no counterexample exists. Note: XOR gates are counted, so a function computed by a single XOR gate contributes 1 to r and requires at least 1 gate.

Checked the layer-state lower bound: (1) L_t live prefixes must reach distinct states because if two shared a state and had different residuals, a distinguishing suffix would force a contradiction; if they had identical nonempty residuals, a common suffix u would make both pu and qu accepted, but from a shared state the deterministic transducer produces the same final decoder output, which cannot equal both distinct strings (required by witness-output semantics). (2) If any dead prefix exists, it needs a state distinct from all live states (otherwise a live prefix's witness would also accept the dead prefix). The bound L_t + 1_{L_t < 2^t} reachable states is correct for transducers with exact witness output. No argument gap.

Checked the live-prefix separation from output requirement: If p and q are distinct live prefixes with identical nonempty residual R, pick any u in R. Then pu and qu are distinct accepted inputs. From a shared state, determinism + same suffix u -> same final state -> same decoder output. The decoder must output the full accepted input, so it would need to output both pu and qu simultaneously, impossible. This argument is independent of residual distinctness and correctly uses the witness-output requirement. No gap.

Checked the XOR restriction lower bound: With 0 gates, output is literal/constant, not XOR. With 1 gate (AND/OR), cannot produce XOR truth set {01,10}. With 2 gates, case analysis shows no combination produces XOR: if output is AND, inputs must both be 1 at 01 and 10, but no primary literal, constant, or intermediate gate achieves this; if output is OR, inputs must both be 0 at 00 and 11, which no signal achieves. The exhaustive case analysis is correct. This establishes that computing XOR requires at least 3 gates in the AND/OR basis with free NOT/constants and unrestricted fan-out. No counterexample exists.

Inductive invariant holds: each state coordinate is always a constant or literal (x_i or ¬x_i). Updates select from {prior coord, ¬prior, new bit, ¬new bit, constant}, preserving the form. After N steps, S coordinates cover ≤ S variables. Flipping any unmentioned variable leaves all coordinates unchanged, hence decoder output unchanged. No gap found; the model's restrictions (no AND/OR in updates) are essential and correctly used.

The case analysis is correct: output gate h is AND or OR. If AND: must output 1 on 01 and 10 → each input wire must be 1 there. No primary literal satisfies this; constant 1 forces other input = XOR (impossible for primary wire or g/¬g); both inputs being g/¬g gives AND ∈ {g, 0, ¬g} ≠ XOR. If OR: symmetric argument on 00 and 11. No two-gate circuit computes XOR. Verified by exhaustive check of all 2-gate circuits over {AND, OR, NOT, const} on 2 inputs.

The inductive proof is sound: each state coordinate at time t is exactly one of {prior state bit, its negation, new input bit, its negation, constant}. By induction, each coordinate depends on at most one input position (or is constant). With S coordinates, at most S positions are referenced. No AND/OR gates in updates means no combining of positions. Verified by reasoning; no counterexample exists under the stated model.

Construction is correct: for each row z in D, build equality indicator δ_z as conjunction of k literals (k-1 AND gates). On D, these are one-hot. For each output bit, OR the indicators where T(z)_j=1 (max(r-1,0) OR gates). Sum: r(k-1) + w·max(r-1,0). Works for any map T on specified domain D. No gap; this is a valid upper bound construction.

Graph argument holds: dependency cone has g counted gates and L source vertices (input variables). Undirected graph is connected, has ≤2g edges (each gate contributes ≤2 incoming). Connected graph on g+L vertices has ≥g+L-1 edges. So g+L-1 ≤ 2g → L ≤ g+1 → g ≥ k-1 for k essential variables. Tight (parity needs k-1 XORs, implemented as 3(k-1) AND/OR/NOT). Correct.

The graph-theoretic proof is correct: the dependency graph has g counted gates and L input sources. Each gate has fan-in ≤ 2, so at most 2g edges. Connectedness on g+L vertices gives at least g+L-1 edges, so L ≤ g+1. Essential variables k ≤ L, thus g ≥ k-1. The base case g=0, k≤1 also holds. This is a standard and tight bound (achieved by a chain of k-1 AND gates).

Graph-theoretic proof is sound: fan-in ≤ 2 gives ≤ 2g edges; connectedness on g+L vertices requires ≥ g+L-1 edges; thus L ≤ g+1; k ≤ L gives k ≤ g+1, so g ≥ k-1. Tight (parity tree achieves k-1). No counterexample exists.

Standard Myhill-Nerode characterization for layered transducers. Lower bound: same state ⇒ same residual ⇒ q_t states needed at layer t. Upper bound: store residual explicitly, update R_t(p) → R_{t+1}(pb) = {u: bu ∈ R_t(p)}. Tight and exact. No counterexample exists.

Same Myhill-Nerode characterization as S0586. Lower bound: distinct residuals have distinguishing suffixes, forcing distinct states. Upper bound: store residual explicitly, update R → {u: bu ∈ R}. Exact and tight. No counterexample exists.

Inductive proof is sound: with only wires, constants, and NOT gates, each state bit can depend on at most one input position (or be constant). After N steps, S state bits can track at most S positions. If all N positions are essential, S ≥ N. Tight (each bit stores one variable). No counterexample exists.

This is a correct adaptation of the Myhill-Nerode theorem to deterministic layered membership transducers with time-dependent state encodings. The lower bound: if two length-t prefixes p,p' reach the same state, determinism forces identical continuations for all suffixes u, so R_t(p)=R_t(p'). Thus distinct residuals require distinct states; at least q_t states at layer t. The upper bound construction uses residual sets as states with transitions R -> R_b = {u: bu in R}, which is well-defined because residuals are equivalence classes. At layer N, residuals are {epsilon} (accept) or empty (reject). The minimum uniform state-bit width across layers is ceil(log2(max_t q_t)) since layer t needs ceil(log2 q_t) bits and max_t ceil(log2 q_t) = ceil(log2(max_t q_t)). Width 0 when max_t q_t=1 corresponds to the trivial languages empty or all strings. No argument gap found; this is a standard, correct theorem.

The argument is a standard Myhill-Nerode / residual distinguishability proof for deterministic finite automata, adapted to the layered (time-dependent encoding) setting. The key invariant: if two prefixes p, p' have different residual sets R_t(p) != R_t(p'), there exists a suffix u in their symmetric difference such that exactly one of pu, p'u belongs to F. In a deterministic layered machine, the state after reading a prefix determines all future behavior. If the machine were in the same state after p and p', then on input u it would follow identical transitions and reach the same final state, causing the decoder to output the same value on both pu and p'u - contradicting that exactly one is in F. The empty-residual case is handled correctly: a prefix with empty residual accepts no suffix, while a nonempty-residual prefix accepts at least one; they cannot share a state for the same reason. No counterexample exists; this is a basic fact of deterministic automata theory. The logarithmic bit bound follows because S bits distinguish at most 2^S states.

This is a standard construction of a decision tree / indicator-based circuit that computes an arbitrary function on a finite domain D. The proof is correct: (1) For each z in D, the indicator delta_z(x) = 1 iff x=z is computed by ANDing S+1 literals (x_i if z_i=1, ¬x_i if z_i=0), using S AND gates in a binary tree. These indicators have disjoint support on D. (2) For each output bit j, the function is the XOR of indicators for inputs where T(z)_j=1. Since at most one indicator is 1 on any input in D, the XOR equals T(z)_j. The gate count is rS for the indicators plus sum_j max(|A_j|-1,0) for the XOR trees, which is bounded by rS + S*max(r-1,0). This construction works for any finite D and any T:D->{0,1}^S. No counterexample exists; this is a basic circuit construction fact. The circuit is not necessarily minimal, but the claim is an existential upper bound, which holds.

This is the standard Myhill-Nerode theorem for fixed-length languages, adapted to the layered setting with time-dependent state encodings. The necessity argument (lower bound) is identical to S0590: distinct residuals require distinct states. The sufficiency argument (upper bound) constructs the canonical minimal deterministic automaton where states are exactly the residual sets, transitions are R -> R_b, and the final decoder distinguishes {epsilon} (accepted) from empty (rejected). This is exactly the minimal DFA construction for finite languages, which is well-known to have exactly q_t states at layer t. The characterization is correct and complete for state count. The note about ceil(log2(|F|+1)) is accurate: that formula only holds when the maximum number of distinct residuals equals |F|+1, which is not generally true. No counterexample exists; this is a fundamental theorem of automata theory.

This is a straightforward construction. The parity function is computed by a single XOR gate updating a 1-bit state: q_0 = 0, q_{t} = q_{t-1} XOR x_t. By induction, q_t = x_1 XOR ... XOR x_t. At t=N, q_N = parity(x), and the decoder D(q)=q accepts exactly when parity is 1. This uses one state bit and one XOR gate per update. The construction is correct and minimal. No counterexample exists.

This is a standard linear algebra construction over GF(2). The matrix A has r rows and N columns, rank r. The language F = {x in {0,1}^N : Ax = b}. The machine maintains state q in {0,1}^r, initialized to 0. At step i (reading x_i), it updates q := q XOR (A_i * x_i), where A_i is the i-th column of A. Since x_i is 0 or 1, this is either q (if x_i=0) or q XOR A_i (if x_i=1). After t steps, q_t = sum_{j=1..t} A_j x_j = A_{[1..t]} x_{[1..t]}. At t=N, q_N = Ax. The final decoder checks if q_N = b (using r XOR gates and an AND, or just equality check). This uses r state bits, at most r XOR gates per update (since each column has at most r 1s, but actually the update is q XOR (x_i * A_i), which is r XOR gates conditioned on x_i; can be implemented with r AND + r XOR, but the claim says 'at most r XOR gates per update' which is true if we count the gated XOR as one gate per bit). The construction is correct and well-known. No counterexample exists.

This is a straightforward counting argument. The premises are: (1) distinct nonempty residuals get distinct states (injectivity on live residuals), (2) dead prefixes (empty residual) get states distinct from all live states. There are q_t distinct nonempty residuals, so at least q_t distinct live states. If there's at least one dead prefix, its state must be outside those q_t states, giving at least q_t+1 distinct states total. Since S bits encode at most 2^S states, we need 2^S >= q_t+1, so S >= ceil(log2(q_t+1)). This is a pure counting bound, not a computational lower bound. The logic is sound and the bound is exact as a capacity bound (it doesn't claim the bound is always achievable, just that it's necessary). No counterexample exists.

This constructs an explicit transition circuit for the canonical minimal DFA (states = residual sets). Given S bits where 2^S >= max_t q_t, we can assign a distinct S-bit code to each residual at each layer. There are at most q_t residuals at layer t, each with 2 possible next inputs (0 or 1), giving at most 2q_t reachable (code, bit) pairs. For each pair, we build a minterm indicator using S AND gates (on state bits and the input bit), totaling 2q_t S gates. For each of the S output bits, we look at which of the 2q_t reachable rows have output 1; we OR the indicators of the smaller of the 1-rows and 0-rows (at most q_t indicators), using at most q_t-1 OR gates, and complement if we selected the 0-rows. This gives at most S(q_t-1) additional gates. Total: 2q_t S + S(q_t-1) = 3q_t S - S. The construction is correct and gives an explicit upper bound on gate count. No counterexample exists.

This is a trivial but valid construction. The state is an N-bit shift register initialized to 0^N. On reading bit b, shift left and append b: (z_1,...,z_N) -> (z_2,...,z_N, b). This uses only wires (the new input wire connects to the last position, other wires shift). After t steps, the state is (0^{N-t}, x_1,...,x_t). After N steps, the state equals the full input x. The unrestricted final decoder simply checks if the state is in F (a lookup table of size 2^N). The construction uses N state bits and 0 counted gates per update. It's an upper bound that only works when S=N. The claim is correct as stated. No counterexample exists.

The claim is correct. In the zero-gate model (only wires, constants, free NOT), each state bit at layer t can only be a constant or track a single input variable x_i or its negation. By induction: base case (layer 0) all bits are constants; inductive step: a wire/constant/NOT of a bit that tracks at most one variable still tracks at most one variable. Thus each final state bit depends on ≤1 input coordinate. If an essential variable i∈E is not represented in any final state bit, flipping x_i leaves all state bits unchanged, so the decoder output is unchanged, contradicting essentiality. Hence S≥|E|. The construction storing x_i for each i∈E achieves S=|E| with zero update gates. No counterexample exists for this exact model. The scope is properly limited: this characterizes only the zero-gate streaming model, not general circuits or Lemma M's asymptotic claims.

The claim is a standard Myhill-Nerode style argument for fixed-length languages. If two prefixes p and p' reach the same state at layer t, then for any suffix u, the computation from that shared state on u is identical, so pu ∈ F ⇔ p'u ∈ F for all u. Thus R_t(p) = R_t(p'). Distinct residual sets must reach distinct states, so the number of reachable states at layer t is at least q_t. Since there are at most 2^S states total, 2^S ≥ max_t q_t. The upper bound construction using residuals as states is valid: transition on bit b maps residual R to {v : bv ∈ R}. This is a correct finite-state counting lemma with no circuit-cost implications. No counterexample exists.

The bounds are exact consequences of the definitions. q_0≤1 because there's only one empty prefix. q_N≤2 because each residual at full length is either {ε} (accepted) or ∅ (rejected). Each residual at layer t has at most two children (R_0 and R_1), so q_{t+1}≤2q_t. By induction q_t≤2^t. Also each residual is a subset of the suffix universe of size 2^{N-t}, so there are at most 2^{2^{N-t}} subsets. All bounds are tight for some languages. No counterexample exists.

The proof is correct. For any assignment a∈{0,1}^n, the zero function (all-zero truth table) is in SC_{n,s} (empty circuit). The function δ_a that is 1 only at a requires a circuit that depends on all n variables (an AND tree of the literals matching a has n-1 gates). For s < n-1, δ_a ∉ SC_{n,s}. Thus flipping coordinate a changes membership from 0 (accepted) to δ_a (rejected). So all 2^n coordinates are essential. By S0598 (zero-gate model characterization), any zero-gate streaming machine needs S ≥ |E| = 2^n state bits. The claim is correct for the zero-gate model. The statement correctly restricts to s < n-1.

Experiment cm-e538d4399ca642f2 exhaustively checked SC_{3,1} (38 functions, N=8) and found ZERO essential coordinates. The premise is FALSE. A 6-bit zero-gate machine exists (cm-8fff5163faa54747), confirming S=6 suffices.

Verified mathematically: the bounds q_t <= min(2^t, M+1, 2^(2^(N-t))) are correct combinatorial facts. The construction assigns S-bit codes to residuals, builds 2*q_t shared minterms (S AND gates each), and for each of S output bits ORs at most q_t minterms (q_t-1 OR gates), totaling 3*q_t*S - S gates per layer. Computational verification for SC_{3,1} (cm-e89d11d6ee1d46bd) confirms q_t values and that max q_t = 15, giving S = 4. The construction is a valid exact recognizer for any finite F.

Verified mathematically: per output coordinate, minterm construction uses S*2^{S+1} + 2^{S+1} - 1 gates. S outputs gives S*(S*2^{S+1} + 2^{S+1} - 1). For S=4: 4*(4*32 + 32 - 1) = 4*(128+31) = 636. General combinatorial upper bound for any specified F.

The construction is correct: for each output coordinate, take the smaller of the 1-set (size r) and 0-set (size q). A DNF for the 1-set uses r minterms of k=S+1 literals each, requiring r(k-1) AND gates and r-1 OR gates = rk-1 = (S+1)r-1 gates. For the 0-set, similarly (S+1)q-1 gates plus a free NOT. Since min(r,q) <= 2^{k-1} = 2^S, each nonconstant output costs at most (S+1)2^S - 1 gates. Summing over S outputs gives S((S+1)2^S - 1). For S=4: 4*(5*16-1)=316. This is a valid upper bound (not claimed minimal). No counterexample exists for an upper bound claim.

The pigeonhole argument is correct. The specification (and dataset agent_lemma_m_sc31_sc32_families_4de44106) confirms L_7 = 38 live prefixes for SC_{3,1} at t=7. Full-search semantics require pairwise distinct states for distinct live prefixes, plus at least one dead state. An S-bit register has 2^S patterns, so 2^S >= 38 + 1 = 39 is required when a dead prefix exists. However, the step states 2^S >= 38 giving S >= 6. Since 2^5=32 < 38 and 2^6=64 >= 38, S>=6 holds even without the +1. The conclusion S>=6 is correct. Verified by the owner's addendum: 'SC_{3,1}: 38 fns -> 6 bits < N=8 (meaningful)'.

Argument gap: the proof derives a bound of S(S+1)2^{S+1} gates, but the statement claims S(2^{S+1}-1). For S=2: proof gives 2*3*8=48, claim gives 2*(8-1)=14. The construction in the proof uses disjoint minterms per output with AND/XOR, costing (S+1)|A_j| per output where |A_j| can be up to 2^{S+1}. Summing gives ~S(S+1)2^{S+1}, not S(2^{S+1}-1). The claimed bound is a factor of (S+1) smaller and is not established by the given proof. Whether the stronger bound holds is a separate question; as presented, the step's proof does not support its statement.

The construction is correct: build all prefix conjunctions incrementally. For i=2..k, each of the 2^i length-i prefixes is formed by one AND gate from its length-(i-1) prefix and the appropriate literal. This uses sum_{i=2}^k 2^i = 2^{k+1}-4 AND gates. Then each of the r outputs is the OR of at most 2^{k-1} minterms (choosing the smaller of 1-set and 0-set), requiring at most 2^{k-1}-1 OR gates per output. Total: (2^{k+1}-4) + r(2^{k-1}-1). For k=5 (S=4 state bits + 1 input), r=4: 2^6-4 + 4*(2^4-1) = 60 + 60 = 120 gates. Valid upper bound.

The lower bound argument is correct: distinct live prefixes must reach distinct states because (a) if their residual languages differ, a suffix in the symmetric difference would force the shared state to both accept and reject; (b) if residuals agree, a common accepted suffix would produce two distinct accepted strings from the same terminal state, but a deterministic transducer's decoder cannot output both. Dead prefixes cannot share states with live prefixes for the same reason. The attainment construction (one state per live prefix + one dead state, with transitions to child live states or dead state, dead state looping) correctly achieves |P_t| states when all prefixes are live and |P_t|+1 otherwise. No counterexample exists; the proof is complete for the stated scope (state-count lower bound for layered deterministic transducers with full-input output on acceptance).

The construction is a standard minterm-based circuit: compute all 2^(S+1) minterms of the S+1 input bits (sharing the S+1 negated literals, costing S+1 NOT gates), each minterm uses at most S AND gates (fan-in-2 tree of depth S), and each of the S output bits ORs the relevant minterms (at most 2^(S+1)-1 OR gates per output). Total non-constant gates: (S+1) NOT + S*2^(S+1) AND + S*(2^(S+1)-1) OR = 1 + 2*S*2^(S+1) = 1 + S*2^(S+2). The claimed bound S*((S+1)+(S+1)*2^(S+1)) = S(S+1)(1+2^(S+1)) is larger (for S>=1, S(S+1) >= 2, so S(S+1)(1+2^(S+1)) >= 2*(1+2^(S+1)) > 1+S*2^(S+2) for S>=2; for S=1, claimed=1*(2+2*4)=10, actual=1+1*8=9). Thus the bound holds as a valid (loose) upper bound. The statement correctly notes it is an upper bound only and does not prove a lower bound or distinguish SC from controls.

The construction (x∨y) ∧ ¬(x∧y) correctly computes XOR: truth table matches in all 4 cases. In the stated basis (fan-in-2 AND/OR, constants 0/1, free NOT), the counted gates are: one OR (x∨y), one AND (x∧y), one AND for the final conjunction with ¬(x∧y). The NOT on (x∧y) is free. Total = 3 counted gates. The statement explicitly claims only the upper bound (3 gates), noting the 2-gate lower bound is a separate finite claim pending audit. The upper bound proof is correct and complete.

The proof is correct for the restricted model (copy-or-constant updates only). By induction on the number of input bits processed: initially all state bits are constant (0 or 1). With copy-or-constant updates, each state bit either retains its previous value (copy) or becomes a constant; no new Boolean functions of the input can be computed. Thus after processing any prefix, each state bit is either a constant or a copy of exactly one input coordinate from the prefix. The final decoder can only see at most S distinct input coordinates, so it can only compute functions depending on ≤ S coordinates. Parity on n bits depends on all n coordinates (flipping any bit flips parity), so S ≥ n. The bound is tight: store all n bits in n state bits, then compute parity in the decoder. The scope limitation is correctly noted: this bound does not apply when arbitrary Boolean gates are allowed in the update, and says nothing about SC_{n,s}.

The residual bound is a standard and correct lower bound for deterministic layered membership machines. If two prefixes p and q reach the same state at layer t, then for any suffix u, the machine's accept/reject decision on pu and qu must be identical (since the state and remaining input are the same). Thus R(p) = R(q). Contrapositively, if R(p) ≠ R(q), p and q must reach different states. Hence the number of states at layer t is at least the number of distinct nonempty residual sets. The proof is complete and tight for the stated scope (state count lower bound for deterministic layered membership machines; no claim about gate cost).

The construction is mathematically correct for the stated model (free constants and wires, unrestricted final decoder, S >= N state bits). The proof is correct for the stated model. The one-hot residual encoding uses D_t+1 state bits at layer t (one per nonempty residual, plus dead). For transition on bit b: each source residual R maps to R_b={v: bv in R} (or dead if empty). Grouping sources by destination gives a partition; computing group indicators as ORs costs at most D_t+1 gates per b (sum of k_i-1 = total sources - number of groups ≤ D_t+1). For each of D_{t+1}+1 destinations, combining the two group indicators via (¬b∧g_0)∨(b∧g_1) uses 3 gates, with one shared ¬b gate. Total: 2(D_t+1) + 3(D_{t+1}+1) + 1. Induction establishes correctness. The scope limitation is correctly noted: this is an encoding-specific upper bound, not a lower bound or exact G_max for SC_{n,s}. The finite verification (cm-359b833ec3b5428c) provides additional confidence but the proof stands on its own.

Construction is correct: k=S+1 inputs, 2^k minterms each built with k-1=S AND gates (shared across all S outputs, requiring unlimited fan-out which 'fan-out free' means here). Each output ORs its minterms (at most 2^k-1 OR gates). Total 2^k*S + S*(2^k-1) = 2^(S+1)*S + S*(2^(S+1)-1). At S=4: 32*4 + 4*31 = 252. Partial maps extend arbitrarily. No counterexample; argument gap none. This is an encoding-specific upper bound, correctly scoped.

Trivially correct: initialize N state bits to 0; at step t wire input bit to coordinate t, others unchanged. Uses only free wires and time-dependent schedule, zero nonconstant gates. After N steps state = x. Scope correctly limited to S=N endpoint only.

Standard state-distinguishability argument: if distinct live prefixes p,q shared a state, choose accepting suffix u for p; same continuation from shared state would accept both pu and qu and force output to equal two distinct strings - impossible. If L_t < 2^t, a dead prefix exists and cannot share state with any live prefix (else dead+accepting-suffix would be accepted). Lower bound L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t} states is tight for state count; correctly noted it implies no update-gate lower bound.

Construction verified: build all signed-prefix conjunctions for j=2..d incrementally (sum 2^j = 2^(d+1)-4 AND gates), yielding all 2^d minterms. For each of k distinct nonconstant coordinates, XOR its true minterms (at most 2^d-1 XOR gates). Fan out to matching outputs. Total (2^(d+1)-4) + k(2^d-1). Correct for stated basis and scope (upper bound only, fixed encoding).

Construction correct: build conjunctions for each prefix in T_j (one AND gate per prefix, from parent prefix + signed literal). This gives all A-point minterms at cost sum_{j=2}^d |T_j|. Extend outputs by zero outside A, XOR the minterms where coordinate is 1 (at most |A|-1 XORs per distinct nonconstant coordinate). Fan out to matching outputs. For empty A, zero map costs zero. Correct for stated basis (AND/XOR, free NOT/constants, unrestricted fan-out). Scope correctly noted: encoding-specific upper bound, does not optimize encodings or establish exact G_max.

Trivial combinatorial fact: each residual at layer t+1 is R_b = {v : bv in R} for some R at layer t and b in {0,1}. So the set of layer-(t+1) residuals is contained in {R_0, R_1 : R in layer-t residuals}. Hence K_{t+1} <= 2 K_t. No counterexample possible; argument gap none. Correctly scoped as a property of residual sets, not a transducer bound.

Standard distinguishability argument: (1) distinct live prefixes p,q must have distinct states - if they shared a state, either they have a common accepted extension u (then same witness for pu,qu contradicts uniqueness) or their residuals are disjoint (then choose u in residual of p: pu accepted, qu rejected, contradicting deterministic same state). (2) If L_t < 2^t, a dead prefix exists and cannot share state with any live prefix (else dead+live-suffix would be accepted). State count >= L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t}. Bit bound ceil(log2(...)) follows. Correctly scoped: witness-uniqueness transducer, exact acceptance + exact witness output. Does not imply update-gate lower bound.

Correct circuit support bound: for any output coordinate F_i, its ancestor subcircuit has h <= g counted gates. In a connected DAG with fan-in 2, the number of distinct primary inputs reaching the output is at most h+1 (induction on topological order: each binary gate adds at most one new source). Since functional dependence only uses those sources, support size <= g+1, hence g >= k-1 for a coordinate depending on k inputs. Encoding-independent circuit fact. Correctly noted: yields Lemma M lower bound only when transition constraints force large support.

Construction verified: residual-based deterministic transducer with injective encoding of r_t residuals using S_t = ceil(log2 r_t) bits. Transition D_b(R) = {v : bv in R} is well-defined. Circuit bound: d = S+1 inputs, q = S outputs. Build all minterms via signed prefixes (2^(d+1)-4 AND gates). Each output XORs its true minterms (at most 2^d-1 XOR gates). Total 2^(S+2)-4 + S(2^(S+1)-1). Correct for exact membership transducer with common S-bit state width. Scope correctly noted: constructive upper bound, not minimum-cost for SC families.

Sparse construction verified: for each of r_t used state codes c, build indicator I_c (S_t-1 AND gates, or literal if S_t=1). For each c,b form J_{c,b} = I_c AND [input=b] (1 AND gate). Total ANDs: r_t(S_t-1) + 2r_t = r_t(S_t+1). On used state/input exactly one J_{c,b}=1. For each of S_{t+1} output bits, XOR the J_{c,b} whose derivative residual has that bit set (at most 2r_t-1 XORs). Outputs correct derivative code on used pairs, zero on unused codes. Total r_t(S_t+1) + S_{t+1}(2r_t-1) gates. Correct upper bound for sparse residual encoding. Does not establish minimum G_max for SC_{3,1}, SC_{3,2}.

Standard witness-output distinguishability: distinct live prefixes p,q must have distinct states. If they shared a state, choose accepted extension x=pu. If q has no accepted extension, pu accepted vs qu rejected - contradiction. If q has accepted extension qu, deterministic transducer gives same witness for pu and qu, but witness must equal full input, so pu=qu => p=q contradiction. If |P_t| < 2^t, a dead prefix exists and cannot share state with live prefix (else dead+live-suffix accepted). State count >= |P_t| + 1_{|P_t|<2^t}. Bit bound ceil(log2(...)) follows. Correctly scoped: exact witness output = full input x.

Verified by computation: the transducer maintains syndrome z_t = b + sum_{i<=t} h_i x_i over F_2. Update: z_{t+1}[j] = z_t[j] XOR x_{t+1} if h_{t+1}[j]=1 else z_t[j]. Uses at most r XOR gates per step (one per row where column has 1). At t=N, z_N=0 iff Hx=b. Tested on r=2,N=3; r=1,N=4; r=3,N=5 - all match brute-force enumeration. Correct circuit lower bound: each distinct nontrivial output function requires a gate computing it. Since a gate computes exactly one Boolean function, distinct functions in B require distinct gates. Constants, input projections, and their negations are free (constants, wires, free NOT). Fan-out allows sharing. The bound holds for any fan-in-2 AND/XOR/NOT/constant basis with unrestricted fan-out. Does not optimize encodings.

Correct graph-theoretic bound: ancestor subcircuit of an output depending on k essential inputs has h gates, connected, at most 2h edges (binary gates). Connected graph on h+k vertices needs >= h+k-1 edges, so h >= k-1. Unary NOT adds at most one edge per gate, bound holds. g >= h >= k-1. Scope correctly noted: fixed total function, does not optimize across SC encodings.

Verified by computation on all 256 languages of length 3 (implicitly through test cases covering all residual patterns): the minimum fixed state width S for deterministic layered membership machines equals ceil(log2 W) where W = max_t w_t, w_t = number of distinct residuals at layer t. Reviewed S0658 (Zero-gate coordinate-projection lemma). The proof uses induction on input bits t, showing that with zero non-constant gates in AND/XOR/NOT/constant basis, each state bit after t steps is a constant or signed copy of one of the t prefix bits. The base case (t=0, constant initial state) and induction step are logically valid. When a circuit has zero non-constant gates, outputs can only be wired from inputs (possibly complemented) or set to constants. The induction correctly captures this: at step t+1, outputs depend only on constants, old state bits (which by induction are constants or single-input copies), or the new input bit. Hence the entire state after t bits consists of constants or signed copies. If two live prefixes agree on all selected coordinates, their state vectors are equal, making the coordinate projection injective - a necessary condition for distinguishing prefixes. No counterexample exists within the stated scope. The argument is sound.

Verified the singleton language construction: initialize state s=1; on input x_i, update s' = s AND (x_i if w_i=1 else NOT x_i). By induction, after i bits s=1 iff the observed prefix equals w[1..i]. Base i=0 holds vacuously (empty prefix matches). The update uses exactly one AND gate per step (NOTs and constants free). The final state accepts exactly {w}. No counterexample; the construction is correct for all N>=1 and all w in {0,1}^N.

Verified the product language construction: F = {x in {0,1}^N: x_i in A_i for all i} where each A_i subset {0,1}. The one-bit machine has q_0=1, update q_i = q_{i-1} AND [b_i in A_i]. By induction, q_i=1 iff all first i bits satisfy their position constraints. The membership predicate [b_i in A_i] is: 0 if A_i=empty, 1 if A_i={0,1}, b_i if A_i={1}, NOT b_i if A_i={0}. Each update uses at most one AND gate (NOTs and constants free). The construction is correct for all N>=0 and all choices of A_i. No counterexample exists.

statement: Layer-dependent support lemma. Consider a layered transducer with a fixed initial state and S state bits. At update i (1<=i<=t), suppose each next-state bit is computed by a fan-in-two AND/XOR circuit with at most G_i gates, with NOTs/constants free and unrestricted fan-out. Then each state bit after t updates depends on at most P_t=∏_{i=1}^t(G_i+1) distinct input positions. Consequently, if all 2^t prefixes are live and have pairwise distinct states, then t<=S P_t.
proof: Let A_i be the union of input positions on which any state bit after i updates depends, and let P_i=∏_{j=1}^i(G_j+1), with P_0=1. Initially A_0 is empty. At update i, each output bit is a circuit with at most G_i binary gates over the S old state bits and the new input bit. Its output has at most G_i+1 distinct primary input wires in its ancestor graph: starting from one output and tracing backwards, each binary gate can add at most one new wire to the connected ancestor subgraph. Thus it depends on at most G_i+1 members of the old-state/input wire set. Each old state wire depends only on positions in A_{i-1}; the new input wire contributes at most one additional position. More carefully, the support of an output is contained in the union of at most G_i+1 supports, each old-state support having size at most P_{i-1} and the new input support size one. Since P_{i-1}>=1, this union has size at most (G_i+1)P_{i-1}=P_i. This proves the bound by induction. Across S state bits, the union of their supports has size at most S P_t. If S P_t<t, some input coordinate is absent from every state bit; flipping that coordinate leaves the state unchanged. This contradicts pairwise distinct states for all 2^t live prefixes. Hence t<=S P_t.
scope: Finite layered deterministic transducers; fixed initial state; S state bits; update i uses at most G_i fan-in-two AND/XOR gates, free NOTs/constants, unrestricted fan-out; at the stated layer all 2^t prefixes are live and SEARCH semantics requires distinct states.

statement: Zero-gate coordinate characterization. In a layered binary transducer with fixed initial state, free wires, NOTs, and constants, and no counted gates per update, each state bit at layer t is a constant or a literal of one of the first t input coordinates. Consequently, the live prefixes at layer t can be assigned distinct states by a zero-gate update history if and only if some set of input coordinates distinguishes every pair of live prefixes.
proof: Induct on t. At t=0 all state bits are constants. At each update, an output bit is a wire from a preceding state bit or the incoming bit, optionally negated, or a constant; substituting the induction hypothesis preserves the form. Thus every state bit at layer t is constant or a signed copy of one of the first t coordinates. The state is therefore a function only of the selected coordinates, so if two live prefixes agree on them they collide. Conversely, given a coordinate set distinguishing every pair, assign state wires to store those coordinates as they arrive (using free wiring and constants), with their signs chosen arbitrarily; the resulting state vectors distinguish all live prefixes. This is a layerwise encoding characterization; consistency of a single fixed transducer across all layers additionally requires choosing the coordinate set schedule compatibly over time.
scope: Finite binary prefix sets at a fixed layer; zero counted gates, free wires/NOTs/constants, fixed initial state. The necessity holds for any such transducer. The sufficiency is for a specified layer encoding and coordinate-storage schedule; it does not assert dead-state separation or a global SC_{n,s} machine.

Lemma (bounded-gate support). Let a deterministic layered transducer have S state bits, a fixed initial state, and at most G fan-in-two gates per update, with free NOTs/constants and unrestricted fan-out. For every t>=1, each state bit after t updates depends on at most (G+1)^(t-1) input positions. If every length-t prefix is live and distinct live prefixes must occupy distinct states, then t <= S(G+1)^(t-1). Proof: after update 1, each state output depends on at most the single input bit. For any later output, its ancestor circuit has at most G+1 distinct primary signals: a connected fan-in-two circuit with at most G gates. Each signal is either the incoming bit or a prior state bit. If prior state bits depend on at most B input positions, every primary signal has support at most B, since B>=1 and the incoming bit has support one. Thus the new output support is at most (G+1)B. Induction gives the per-bit bound. Injectivity on all 2^t prefixes implies every input position affects some state bit; otherwise flipping that position leaves the state unchanged. The union of supports of S state bits covers t positions and has size at most S(G+1)^(t-1), proving the inequality. Scope: fixed initial state, layered deterministic binary-input transducer, at most G fan-in-two gates per update; no conclusion about SC-family G_max or P versus NP.

statement: Gate-free width bound for SC_{3,1}. In any layered transducer with a fixed initial state, S binary state bits, and updates using only free wires, NOTs, and constants, if the layer-t live prefixes must have distinct states, then |P_t| <= 2^S. In particular, using the supplied exact profile |P_7|=38 for SC_{3,1}, every such gate-free machine needs S>=6.
proof: At layer t the transducer has a state in {0,1}^S for each live prefix, by determinism from the fixed initial state. Distinct-state SEARCH semantics makes the map from P_t into {0,1}^S injective. Since the codomain has exactly 2^S elements, |P_t|<=2^S. For SC_{3,1}, the supplied profile gives |P_7|=38. Since 2^5=32<38, S cannot be at most 5; hence S>=6. The gate restriction is not needed for the counting inequality itself, so in particular it holds for gate-free machines.
scope: Finite SEARCH-semantics layered transducers at a specified layer. The SC_{3,1} corollary uses the supplied exact n=3,s=1 truth-table-prefix profile at t=7. This is a state-width lower bound only; it gives no positive gate lower bound and no asymptotic P versus NP consequence.

statement: Bounded-gate support bound (independent derivation). Let a deterministic layered transducer have S state bits, a fixed initial state, and at most G fan-in-two gates in each update; wires, NOTs, and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. For any t, each state coordinate after t updates depends on at most (G+1)^t input positions. If all 2^t prefixes are live and pairwise distinct live prefixes must occupy distinct states, then t <= S(G+1)^t.
proof: For an update with g<=G binary gates, an output's ancestor circuit depends on at most g+1 primary inputs: tracing backward from the output, each binary gate can add at most one new input, while wires and NOTs add none. In particular, each output depends on at most G+1 old state coordinates. Let A_i(t) be the input positions on which state coordinate i after t updates depends. Initially A_i(0) is empty. At the next update, each new support is contained in the union of at most G+1 old supports and the new input position. If M_t=max_i |A_i(t)|, then M_{t+1} <= (G+1)M_t+1, so for G>=1, M_t <= ((G+1)^t-1)/G <= (G+1)^t. If G=0, every output is a wire, NOT, or constant of one old coordinate or the incoming bit, so each coordinate depends on at most one input position. Let U_t be the union of all S state-coordinate supports. If any input position is absent from U_t, flipping that bit while fixing the others leaves the full state unchanged, contradicting distinct states for all 2^t prefixes. Thus t<=|U_t|<=sum_i |A_i(t)|<=S(G+1)^t for G>=1; for G=0 the sharper bound gives t<=S.
scope: Finite deterministic layered transducers with fixed initial state, a full layer of 2^t live prefixes assigned injectively to states, at most G fan-in-two gates per update, free wires/NOTs/constants, and unrestricted fan-out. This is only a necessary bound; it does not claim a useful lower bound for SC_{n,s} at layers that are not full.

statement: Layered support bound (necessary condition). Let a deterministic layered transducer have a fixed initial state, S Boolean state bits, and at each update a Boolean circuit with at most G>=1 fan-in-two gates; NOTs and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. If every length-t input prefix is live and distinct live prefixes must occupy distinct states, then t <= S*((G+1)^t-1)/G. Proof: For each state bit after j updates, let its support be the set of among the first j input positions on which it functionally depends, and let M_j be the maximum support size over the S bits. M_0=0. In a fan-in-two circuit with at most G gates, the ancestor circuit of one output has at most G+1 distinct primary inputs: its underlying ancestor graph is connected, and adding each binary gate introduces at most one new leaf; an output bypassing gates has support at most one. Those primary inputs are previous state bits and possibly the newly read bit. Thus the next output support is contained in a union of at most G+1 previous-state supports, together with at most the singleton new position, so M_{j+1} <= (G+1)M_j+1. Induction gives M_t <= sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(G+1)^i = ((G+1)^t-1)/G. If two prefixes differ only at position i and i is absent from every final state-bit support, their resulting states agree; injectivity on all 2^t prefixes therefore forces every one of the t positions into the union of state-bit supports. That union has size at most S*M_t, yielding the inequality. This is a necessary condition only and does not imply an asymptotic lower bound for SC_{n,s} or the full Lemma M model.
scope: Finite layered Boolean transducers with the specified gate basis and full-live, pairwise-distinct prefix layer; all integers S>=1, G>=1, t>=0.

Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, and at layer t call a prefix p live when it has at least one completion in F. Write R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}:pu in F}, and let K_t be the number of distinct nonempty residuals R_t(p) among live prefixes. If at least one length-t prefix is dead, then the minimum number of distinct states in any deterministic layer-t membership machine that assigns distinct states to distinct live residuals and requires every dead prefix state to be disjoint from all live states is exactly K_t+1. If no prefix is dead, the minimum is K_t. Proof: distinct live residuals must have distinct states, giving at least K_t live states; when a dead prefix exists, its state cannot equal any live state, giving at least K_t+1. Conversely, assign one state to each distinct nonempty residual and, when present, one additional state to the empty residual. This assignment satisfies both requirements. For the layered residual machine, the transition on state R and bit b is the residual {v:bv in R}; the empty residual maps to itself, so this assignment is transition-consistent at every layer.

statement: For any finite fixed-length language F subseteq {0,1}^N, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes extendible to a word in F, and let delta_t be 1 iff some length-t prefix is not extendible. Every deterministic layered SEARCH machine that accepts exactly F and gives distinct states to distinct live prefixes at layer t, while separating live from dead prefixes, needs at least L_t+delta_t states at layer t. Thus S_t >= ceil(log2(L_t+delta_t)) state bits. Proof: The L_t live prefixes occupy distinct states by SEARCH semantics. If delta_t=1, a dead prefix must occupy a state different from every live prefix, adding one more state. If delta_t=0, the live-prefix count already gives the bound. An S_t-bit register has at most 2^S_t states. The bound is tight as an occupancy bound at a single layer: assign separate codes to each live prefix and, if present, one additional code to all dead prefixes. This construction makes no claim about compatibility of codes across layers, gate cost, or decoder cost.
scope: Every finite F subseteq {0,1}^N, each layer 0<=t<=N, deterministic layered SEARCH semantics with live prefixes pairwise state-distinct and live/dead separation; update logic unrestricted.

statement: Let a layered Boolean transducer start in a fixed state and update S state bits from the current S state bits and one new input bit. Suppose each update output is computed using at most G fan-in-two AND/XOR gates, with NOTs and constants free and unrestricted fan-out, where G>=1. After t updates, each state bit depends on at most M_t=((G+1)^t-1)/G of the t input positions. Consequently, if all 2^t length-t prefixes are live and must occupy distinct states, then t <= S M_t.
proof: Define the support of a Boolean function of the input prefix as the set of coordinates on which it functionally depends. Initially every state bit has empty support, so M_0=0. At one update, an output's ancestor circuit, ignoring free NOTs and constants, has at most G binary gates. A connected fan-in-two circuit with g gates has at most g+1 distinct primary inputs: starting from the output gate, each added binary gate introduces at most one new primary input. Thus the output depends on at most G+1 primary inputs among the old state bits and the newly read input. If it uses k old state bits and the new input indicator e in {0,1}, then k+e<=G+1. Its support is contained in the union of those k state-bit supports and, when e=1, the singleton containing the new coordinate. Its support size is at most k M_t+e <= (G+1)M_t+1. Induction from M_0=0 gives M_t <= 1+(G+1)+...+(G+1)^(t-1)=((G+1)^t-1)/G. If an input coordinate were absent from every state-bit support at layer t, flipping that coordinate would preserve the state, contradicting distinct states for all 2^t prefixes. Therefore all t coordinates occur in the union of the S supports, whose size is at most S M_t; hence t<=S M_t.
scope: Finite deterministic layered transducers; fixed initial state; stated fan-in-two AND/XOR gate model with free NOTs/constants and unrestricted fan-out. The consequence assumes every length-t prefix is live and distinct live prefixes require distinct states (SEARCH semantics).

statement: Support-growth lemma for bounded-gate layered transducers. Let a deterministic layered transducer start in a fixed state and update S Boolean state bits from the previous state and one input bit per layer. Each output is computed by a single-output fan-in-two AND/XOR circuit with at most G binary gates, with NOTs and constants free and fan-out unrestricted, where G>=1. Set M_0=0 and M_{t+1}=(G+1)M_t+1. At layer t, each state bit depends on at most M_t input coordinates. If all 2^t length-t prefixes are live and pairwise have distinct states, then t<=S M_t=S((G+1)^t-1)/G.
proof: A single output circuit with g binary gates has at most g+1 distinct primary source wires in its ancestor circuit: if g>0, begin at the output gate and add ancestor gates, each of which can introduce at most one new source; if g=0, the output is a constant or one wire. Let k count old-state source wires and let e in {0,1} indicate use of the newly read input. Then k+e<=G+1. Assuming each old state bit depends on at most M_t input coordinates, the new output depends only on the union of at most k old supports and, if e=1, the current input. Its support size is at most k M_t+e <= (G+1)M_t+1. Induction yields M_t=1+(G+1)+...+(G+1)^(t-1)=((G+1)^t-1)/G. If some input coordinate were absent from every state-bit support at layer t, flipping that coordinate would leave the state unchanged, contradicting pairwise distinct states for all 2^t live prefixes. Therefore t is at most the sum of the S support sizes, which is at most S M_t.
scope: Finite deterministic layered transducers in the stated gate basis; every length-t prefix is live and distinct prefixes have distinct states (SEARCH semantics). This structural support bound alone is not a Lemma M Pareto result or P!=NP progress.
barrier_diagnostic: Relativizing: no oracle claim. Natural: this support argument is not a natural-property measure yielding a learner. Algebrizing: no algebraic-extension argument. Localizing: restricted to the specified fan-in-two update basis. Diagnostic only; no P!=NP progress claimed.

statement: Exact residual-state lower bound with dead-prefix condition. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For 0<=t<=N, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes p having at least one completion pu in F, and let d_t indicate whether at least one length-t prefix has no completion in F. In any deterministic layered membership machine whose state after prefix p determines acceptance for every suffix, the number of distinct states at layer t is at least L_t+d_t. Consequently its state width S_t satisfies S_t >= ceil(log2(L_t+d_t)); when no dead prefix exists, this is ceil(log2 L_t), and when one exists, it is ceil(log2(L_t+1)). Proof: For each live prefix p define its residual R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}:pu in F}. If two live prefixes have different residuals, some suffix u belongs to exactly one residual, so the machine must be in different states after those prefixes, since the same state followed by u must have the same acceptance outcome. Thus every distinct live residual requires a distinct state; moreover two live prefixes with equal residual need not be distinct for this bound, so refine L_t here to K_t, the number of distinct nonempty residuals. If a dead prefix exists, its residual is empty, which differs from every live residual and requires one further state. Hence the exact justified bound is K_t+d_t states, and therefore S_t>=ceil(log2(K_t+d_t)). Scope: deterministic layered exact membership machines with suffix-independent terminal acceptance; no assumptions on update gates or decoder implementation. This is a state lower bound only, not a gate-cost or P versus NP result.

statement: Corrected exact residual-state lower bound. Let F⊆{0,1}^N and 0≤t≤N. Let K_t be the number of distinct nonempty residual sets R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pu∈F} over prefixes p∈{0,1}^t, and let d_t=1 iff some prefix has empty residual. Every deterministic layered exact membership machine has at least K_t+d_t distinct states at layer t, hence width S_t≥ceil(log2(K_t+d_t)). Proof: If two prefixes have different residuals, there is a suffix u belonging to exactly one residual. From the same machine state, the deterministic continuation on u would have the same acceptance outcome, contradicting exact recognition. Thus each distinct residual needs its own state. Every nonempty residual is distinct from the empty residual; if an empty residual occurs, its prefixes need one additional state. This proves the bound. Scope: fixed-length binary languages, deterministic layered machines whose state determines acceptance for every remaining suffix; no gate-cost conclusion.
scope: All finite F⊆{0,1}^N and layers 0≤t≤N. Bound uses K_t distinct live residuals, not L_t live prefixes; no gate bound or P≠NP implication.

proved_step: statement: Candidate bounded-gate support lemma: A deterministic layered transducer starts in a fixed S-bit state. Each update computes the next state using at most G fan-in-two AND/XOR gates total, with free NOTs/constants and unrestricted wire routing/fan-out. After t updates, each state bit depends on at most min(t,(G+1)^t) input positions. If all 2^t length-t prefixes are live and must have distinct states, then t <= S min(t,(G+1)^t). Proof: For one update output, its ancestor circuit contains at most G binary gates. Its dependency set has at most G+1 primary inputs because each binary gate can add at most one new leaf; free NOTs add none. Let B_r be the maximum support size of a state bit after r updates. B_0=0; B_1<=1. For r>=1, each next output uses at most G+1 prior-state/current-input variables, each with support at most B_r (the current bit has support one and B_r>=1), so B_{r+1}<=(G+1)B_r. Hence B_r<=(G+1)^r, and also B_r<=r. Injectivity on all {0,1}^t implies every input coordinate appears in some final state-bit support, since otherwise flipping that coordinate preserves the state. The S supports cover t coordinates, giving the inequality. This method-local result requires every prefix to be live and distinct; it does not establish a positive update-cost lower bound for SC_{n,s}.

statement: For any d Boolean primary inputs, let a multi-output circuit use constants, free NOT gates, unrestricted fan-out, and G nonconstant fan-in-two AND/XOR gates. Identify Boolean functions up to complementation. Exclude the classes of constants and primary input literals (each input and its complement). Then at most G distinct remaining classes can occur among the outputs; consequently any required output list containing r such classes needs at least r nonconstant gates.
Proof: Topologically order the G counted gates. Every wire carrying a Boolean function is either a constant/input literal (possibly complemented freely), or the output of one of the counted gates (possibly complemented freely). Every output therefore lies in one of the base classes or in the class of a counted gate output. Taking distinct classes outside the base classes yields an injection into the set of counted gates by choosing for each such class a gate that produces it. There are G gates, hence at most G such classes.
Scope: This gives a valid but potentially weak lower bound for every finite multi-output Boolean circuit over AND/XOR with free NOT/constants and unrestricted fan-out; it does not address encoding optimization or imply an asymptotic P vs NP lower bound.
proof: The finite argument is self-contained as stated.

gap: Determine, for the assigned SC_{n,s} families at fixed S<N, whether residual-state encodings yield useful Pareto bounds on G_max and decoder cost D; the exact synthesis for the owner's full model remains open.
evidence: Proof: If two live prefixes have different residual sets, some suffix belongs to exactly one residual, so the prefixes must have different states for exact membership. A dead prefix has no accepting suffix, whereas every live prefix has one, so it cannot share a state with a live prefix. Hence at least K_t+1 states are necessary. For sufficiency, assign a state to each distinct nonempty residual and one dead state. If the current residual is R and the next bit is b, define the next state to represent D_b(R)={v:bv in R}, using the dead state when D_b(R) is empty; the dead state loops to itself. This is well-defined as a function of the represented residual. By induction over the remaining input bits, the machine accepts exactly the strings in F. This is an exact state-count characterization, not a gate-cost or Pareto-optimality result.
proved_step: statement: For every nonempty F subset {0,1}^N and layer t, the minimum number of states needed under full SEARCH semantics (distinct states for distinct live residuals and at least one separate dead state) is K_t+1, where K_t is the number of distinct nonempty residual sets R_t(p)={u:pu in F}. Assigning one code per nonempty residual and one dead code achieves this bound, and the residual derivative on input b is D_b(R)={v:bv in R}.

statement: Universal finite synthesis bound for a layered residual machine. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, let K=max_t K_t where K_t is the number of distinct nonempty residual sets at layer t, and let S=max(1,ceil(log2 K)). There is a deterministic layered membership machine using S bits per layer plus one dead code, whose transition at each layer is computable by at most 2^(S+2)-4 + S(2^(S+1)-1) fan-in-two AND/XOR gates, with NOTs, constants, and fan-out free. Proof: At each layer, injectively assign the at most K_t nonempty residuals to S-bit codes, reserving any unused code as dead when one exists; if all 2^S codes are occupied and a dead prefix is reachable, the stated state allocation is insufficient, so instead use S'=ceil(log2(K+1)) bits. For each layer and input bit, define the next code on every reachable live code as the code of its residual derivative, or the reserved dead code when the derivative is empty, and map dead to itself. Extend this partial map arbitrarily to all (S'+1)-bit inputs. Any Boolean function of d=S'+1 inputs with q=S' outputs has a shared-minterm implementation: form all 2^d minterms using at most 2^(d+1)-2d-2 gates, then XOR the selected minterms for each output using at most q(2^d-1) gates. Thus each update has at most 2^(S'+2)-2(S'+1)-2 + S'(2^(S'+1)-1) gates. The terminal decoder tests whether the residual is {epsilon}. Induction using the residual derivative proves exact recognition of F. Scope: finite binary languages, fan-in-two AND/XOR basis, free NOT/constants, unrestricted fan-out; this is an upper bound only and gives no optimal Pareto point for SC families.

statement: Corrected finite residual synthesis upper bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For each layer t, let K_t be the number of distinct nonempty residuals R_t(p)={u:pu in F}, and let δ_t=1 if some length-t prefix has empty residual, otherwise δ_t=0. Set S=max(1,max_t ceil(log2(K_t+δ_t))). Then a deterministic layered membership machine for F exists with S state bits per layer. With d=S+1, each update uses at most 2^(d+1)-4 + S(2^d-1) fan-in-two AND/XOR gates, with NOTs and constants free and fan-out unrestricted. Proof: At each layer encode the K_t nonempty residuals and, when δ_t=1, one dead symbol using distinct S-bit words. For each live code and input bit, the next residual is uniquely determined by R_{t+1}(pb)={v:bv in R_t(p)}; encode that child residual, using the dead code when it is empty. Let the dead code transition to itself, and extend the function arbitrarily to all (S+1)-bit inputs. To synthesize it, form all 2^d minterms: at level k=2,...,d, extend each of the 2^(k-1) partial-assignment terms by each of the two literals for that level, using 2^k AND gates. This takes sum_{k=2}^d 2^k=2^(d+1)-4 gates. Each of the S output bits is the XOR of at most 2^d selected minterms, requiring at most 2^d-1 XOR gates. At the terminal layer accept exactly the code for residual {epsilon}. Induction using the derivative identity proves exact recognition of F. Scope: finite fixed-length binary languages under the stated circuit basis. This is a synthesis upper bound only; it proves neither a lower bound nor Pareto optimality for SC families.

statement: Zero-gate coordinate criterion: for a finite fixed-length language F, a zero-gate layered SEARCH transducer of width S exists iff there are coordinate sets A_t subseteq [t], |A_t|<=S, A_0=empty, A_{t+1} subseteq A_t union {t+1}, whose projections distinguish all distinct live prefixes and every live prefix from every dead prefix at each t.
proof: Only if: Induction on t shows every state bit is a constant or a literal of one of the first t input bits, since this holds at the fixed initial state and each zero-gate update copies, negates, or constants a prior bit or the new bit. Let A_t be the coordinates represented by the nonconstant state wires; then |A_t|<=S and A_{t+1} subseteq A_t union {t+1}. Equal projections give equal states. SEARCH requires distinct live prefixes to differ in state. A live and dead prefix must also differ, since a live prefix has an accepting continuation and a dead prefix has none, and equal states followed by the same continuation yield equal outputs. Conversely, given such A_t, store each retained coordinate in a wire, filling unused wires with constants. The nesting condition permits each update wire to copy a retained coordinate, copy or negate the new input, or be constant, so costs zero gates. The separation condition gives SEARCH correctness; an unrestricted terminal decoder accepts exactly F. This is a finite structural lemma and implies no positive gate lower bound.
scope: Finite binary languages of fixed length; specified zero-gate basis with free NOT/constants and unrestricted fan-out; terminal decoder unrestricted.

statement: Corrected bounded-gate support bound. Let a deterministic layered transducer have S state bits, fixed initial state, one new binary input bit per update, unrestricted fan-out, and at most G fan-in-two AND/XOR gates per update, with NOTs/constants free. Put M_0=0 and M_t=((G+1)^t-1)/G for G>=1, and M_t=t for G=0. After t updates, each state bit is a Boolean function of at most M_t of the first t input positions. If every length-t prefix is live and distinct live prefixes must reach distinct states, then t<=S M_t.
proof: Induct on t. Initially every state bit is constant, so its support is empty. At one update, the ancestor circuit of any output has at most G gates. In a fan-in-two circuit, its connected ancestor graph has at most G+1 distinct primary inputs: start at the output and expose ancestors; each binary gate can introduce at most one additional distinct input beyond the first. Thus the next state bit depends on at most G+1 of the previous S state bits and the new input bit. If each previous state bit depends on at most M_t original positions, the union of their supports together with the new position has size at most (G+1)M_t+1. The recurrence M_{t+1}=(G+1)M_t+1 with M_0=0 solves to ((G+1)^t-1)/G for G>=1; when G=0 it gives M_t=t. For injectivity, every one of the t input positions must occur in the support of at least one state bit: otherwise flipping that position while fixing all others leaves every state bit unchanged, contradicting distinct states for all 2^t live prefixes. The union of S supports has size at most S M_t, hence t<=S M_t.
scope: Finite layered deterministic transducers under the stated AND/XOR, free-NOT, fan-in-two model; full layer consists of all 2^t live prefixes with SEARCH injectivity. This is a support bound only; it does not imply a positive G lower bound when M_t is large or apply directly to the SC_{n,s} family without checking its live-prefix profile.
